A game where you spend hours gathering resources under constant fear of a quick death from your fellow players. Everytime you see another user in Rust, your heart rate will double. That is really the thrill of the game. Sure, there is building a base and gathering resources, even animals you can fight and kill, but it's the interactions with other players that are the core experience of Rust.
Most of those experiences really depend on who you meet. There will be some players that kindly say hello and might even offer to help you. For every such user there are at least 5 players that will murder you on sight, which can make for very nervous interactions with others.
There is the ability to build in Rust, which is necessary to store your resources and protect your sleeping body when you log out. Building is horrendously expensive when you move past a single wooden shelter. It takes thousands of wood or metal pieces to create a base solid and complex enough to prevent other players from simply using 1-5 c4 to enter and take EVERYTHING you own. In contrast, that c4 is very easy for a player that was fortunate enough to research both c4 and explosives allowing them to produce unlimited amounts. C4 is expensive, but only a fraction of the resources obtained from raiding.
This is the main problem in Rust. Unless you are an offensive player that was fortunate enough to obtain a source of C4, you are essencially just collecting resources for the 1% that do, who grow exponentially more wealthy as time goes on if they remain unchallenged. This eventually leads to a completely untouchable, one to five player group with a base so large and laiden with walls, traps, and expensive to destroy decoys, that they are nearly invincible to all on the server.
As a result of all this, if you don't have a friend or two to play this game with, find one or skip it. Having a partner you can trust and work with will make everything easier. Essentially, it doubles or triples your ability to collect resources, build, and defend yourself. If you work together, running into another player is less of a big deal - there are 2-3 against 1, and those odds are usually good enough to be left alone. Even if you do get smoked, you buddies will be there to get revenge, protect your dropped inventory, or just get you back up on your feet. And if all you stuff gets raided, you still had a good time with friends, and will recover twice as fast rather than just thinking about how you wasted the last 20 hours of your life grinding to lose it all.
Conclusion:
-If you play Rust alone, you're gonna have a bad time.

Day 305:
Built a civilization, thriving and filled with characters of joy and happiness. We all lived together foraging and surviving the onslaught of radiation, zombies, and the occasional bears or wolves. Todd...I remember him well, the local cook, could grill the best chicken breast this side of Rad Town...good man...didn't deserve what was done to him. Then, oh god his wife, Clarice...she was so beautiful and so full of life...They took them both behind the rocks and shot them with pipe shotguns. I could still hear the screams in my sleep. I know they are coming for me, I hear them, chanting "Let us in, we wont kill you if you just unlock your doors." They scratch at the door with pickaxes and rocks trying to taunt me.
The inevitable happened, I was gunned down in front of my house with my dignity far far behind my back.
I then spawned with a rock, got killed by another man because he said my rock was sexier than his and he wanted it.
10/10

I stumbled towards a campfire, lighting it and dropping my raw chicken breasts on top. My hunger meter was fine, but I'd feel better if I knew I had some rations to fall back on as I travelled.
I decided to walk off and get my bearings while my chicken cooked, taking a quick stroll around the area. I stopped to admire the view of the plains in front of me, the way the grass swayed. The orange tinted sky would have made it look even more beautiful, had I not had the settings on low.
Damn FPS.
I turned back towards my temporary resting spot, surprised to hear a man growling over voice chat, "This my chicken!"
He'd already seen me. And he'd attempted to steal my food.
I yelled at him to back away and pulled my hatchet free, strafing around him as I approached.
"This my chicken boy, I'm takin' it!" The naked man rushed at me, raising the rock he was gripping tightly in his hands. "MY CHICKEN!"
We exchanged blows, the rock doing little damage in comparison to my sharp blade. As he crumpled in a bloody heap, I whispered "I win" as I scavenged his backpack.
He'd had a stone hatchet, why hadn't he equipped it? No matter. I took my chicken and his hatchet and went on my way. Not but ten seconds later did I see a man being chased by a wolf, obviously helpless. I yelled that I'd help him, sprinting after the wolf and swinging the hatchet down into its back.
Once he realized I wasn't trying to attack him, he turned and began to bash the startled wolf with his rock. Within seconds it fell.
"You can have the stuff the wolf drops," I told him as I turned and began sprinting away. I didn't trust him and thought for a moment he might chase after to attack, but I felt a small bit of glee when I heard his voice faintly over VOIP. "Wow, thanks bro!"
Unfortunately, this is where I ran face first into a bear.
Fortunately, it didn't detect me. At first. I felt irony wash over me as I switched positions with the man I'd saved-- but I knew his rock wasn't going to cut it. I'd just have to make Usain Bolt proud and sprint away.
The sun was starting to set, and I could hear the heavy steps of the bear behind me. It was dead set on catching me. If I didn't lose it soon, it would likely catch me as I stumbled around in the darkness.
"I was checking his steam profile and.." What was that?! Oh hell- I'd run right near someones house. I could hear two men chatting inside, and while I feared they might attack me if I spoke, I figured it was worth a shot.
"Heyguysdon'tmeantointerruptjustpassingbynotathreattheresabearchasingmejustwantedtoletyouknowincaseitstopsbyyourhouse!" Casual enough. They'd obviously heard me-- my voice echoed through one of their headsets and they went silent.
I heard a door open behind me, and a moment later two loud shots. I feared they'd taken to shooting me, and yelled. "Motherf(steamcensored)s!"
"We got the bear... we weren't shooting at you," this revelation made me facepalm. Of course. I was running in a straight line.. had they wanted me dead they would have done so. And I'd just insulted them after they wasted precious ammo and helped a complete stranger.
"I- oh. I was calling the bear a motherf(steamcensored)r. Thanks guys!" I don't know if we were close enough for my words to reach them.
Multiple shots mere seconds later suggested they hadn't. But none of them hit, and I didn't stop.
I LOVE THIS COMMUNITY.

Rust is the closest thing to real life that you'd get if you dropped a bunch of guys off on a deserted island.
The peak of satisfaction comes from constructing your shelter; whether it towers above the rest, or small, but, hosbitable, and durable, and living in it, gathering supplies, haphazard encounters with strangers, and the occassional run-in with some cool people. While, in my personal opinion, the game does require some more in-depth scrutinizing of its social aspects, it is an authentic, community-driven title that provides an experience unlike any other.
Rust’s alpha is 'rough around the edges,' however, it's surprisingly playable. The underlying systems are, and appear to be essentially complete and functional from a 'looking into the glass' perspective, and recent updates have dramatically improved the performance of the server browser.  In my opinion, Rust has a potential that reaches above and beyond, with honest, and diligent developers, and provides an intense and impressive experience even now.
While the visuals have improved, they're no great shake, and you can expect an oddity with shadows, and other occasional glitches.
All in all, an intense, take-no-prisoners survival game, Rust is a great use of Steam Early Access. It's certainly far from finished, however it's definitely ready to play - so says this enthusiast.
Please note:
This review is based on the current alpha build of the game.
I will re-review this game once it is complete.

A great psychological online social survival game.
The real greatness does not come from the game itself, but how people interact with eachother in an environment where resources are scarce.
There's two main paths to take in this game...
You either group up with others to increase your chance of survival, while you gather and build up.
or
You kill others, and raid there homes to gain a quick & easy source of income.
Whatever the case, it's fun to kill, and it's thrilling to be hunted. You can never trust anyone in this game, and true human nature is exploited as people will often trick others into letting their guard down only to get blasted in the face with a shotgun. The battles are constant, and rewarding as rivaling groups battle for world domination.
-----
Personal things I love doing in this game:
Waiting outside someone's house with a shotgun for hours waiting for them to open the door. xD
Roaming the map looking for possible ways to enter unsuspecting homes.
Grouping up with random people, and being forced into very social groups.
Gathering resources in dangerous environments.
Sneaking up on unsuspecting players.
Building very small homes in hidden mountain crevices.
------

I Hate to change this review to a negative review but due to recent developments my review of the old game is irrelevant. Here are some of my problems with the game and why i will give it a negative review.
1. This game has been in early access since 2013. This game got quite close to being finished with the legacy version starting to feel more polished with many features implemented and server lag being nearly eradicated. This all changed when they introduced the new version of rust which is not expected to be completed for at least a year or two. This means that players once again have to play through a version of rust that is unpolished with performance issues. This is probably the main part of my negative review as i have already invested years into this game and will not be wasting more time in a game that is not close to completion and may never be since the developers interest is waning and they seem to only implement useless chamges to the game now.
2. This game has been dumbed down somewhat it used to be a gritty survival game that was intense and hard to survive in. On my return to this game about a month ago i found a game more akin to a a first person shooter that looked less realistic and ridiculous (this may appeal to some people but it is not the game that i bought).
3. Hacking is still running rampant in this game and the developers cannot seem to fix this problem that originated in legacy. This means that days, weeks, months of hard work can be undone by a hacker wo will likely not be banned for a long time if ever.
This review is simply opinon on what i have seen over the development of this game and it may become updated when they fix some of these problems. Goodbye Rust i enjoyed the 300 hours we had together but i refuse to waste more time in a game that will likely never be finished in the near future.

Rust is a lot of fun... At first. However after a few weeks of owning it and putting many hours into it, it's grown stale. I do believe the game is wonderful if you have the friends to play it with, if not, it gets boring and frustrating alone. Another issue seems to be the way the community is right now. There's a large issue of hackers in almost any server you go into. At first I joined a less populated server to explore and build with a friend, but as he started to not play as much, that stopped being interesting. A lot of the fun comes in player combat as well. That being said this can also be a downside since often, spawning into a new server with near-nothing means getting killed by everyone. So if you're lucky enough to find a spot where you're secluded and have resources, then you can build yourself a nice little base, gather weapons and defend yourself. But the opportunity for this to happen has been rare to me. I'd say this game is still interesting. But with it being early-access many bugs and changes still are to be fixed. I'd say wait for full release. I believe the game still has the potential to be better (I don't know how yet though). This is by no means a bad game, it can be very pretty (especially with its lighting) and building things with people and PvP can be fun and interesting. It just needs to be fixed and tweaked.

The best multiplayer survival game out there right now.  Everything persists and decays on the server, including the player, at all times.  Everything has reverted back to basics and the players in the game reflect this through desperate scavenging and making grim decisions,
Most play sessions feel like adventures and the adrenaline rush you get from PvP is quite killer in this game due to all the chaos (can't see names of players until they get close, no in-game map, etc.). Teamwork and coordination is heavily rewarded due to no in-game organization features (which is good) and the lone wolf types have lots of room to thrive in the chaos. The crafting is kept to necessities.  Very well balanced, heavily addictive and my favourite real PvP simulation game since Ultima Online! The devs are great at communicating upcoming features and squashing bugs quickly as well.

Even though Rust is still in early alpha stages with only a couple in-game items it still provides plenty of entertainment that can only get better as more items and features are implemented and the map is expanded.
Unlike other FPS games where you have scary or stressful moments and know you can relax right after, Rust provides a constant level of terror for every sound you hear. There is no relaxing in this game. Even logging out gives no respite as your character simply goes to sleep at the last location you were standing. This means no avoiding a fight by simply closing the game. Your body will simply slump to the floor and be easy pickings for wildlife and other players.
Yes, other players... trust is a tricky thing in Rust. You never know the intentions of anyone else in the game. Resources are scarce and people will kill for them. That plane flying over dropping supplies? It's both a blessing and a curse. You know there are going to be rare items and food parcels in those drops. Unfortunately, so does everyone else who saw it fly over.
They might share the spoils with you and then suddenly they find a shotgun in the last crate. Suddenly they don't seem to feel like you deserve half the food.
Human nature is a tricksie hobbitses, welcome to Rust.

I bought Rust earlier this week and after putting a decent amount of time into it I feel as though I am ready to review it. I started off in a medium size server (about 30 other players) with no idea on how to play. After talking to some of the players with the chat I figured out how to collect resources and survive. After a few deaths I came across my first friendly player. He game me one of his old shacks with the basics: furnace, fire, storage, along with some tools. Unfortunately my internet cut out and I forgot which server I had been on and when I joined a new one I had a very different experience. The new server was less helpful and I found that I had to fend for myself. I created a small set up similar to the one I had been given before and began collecting resources. I was eventually ambushed and spawn camped by 5 guys with bolt action rifles. With my first house on this new server destroyed I made another one further away from the road and stockpiled more items and logged off. When I got on the next day I spawned in a new place and when I found my way back to my old house the door had been ripped off and everything except for an old torch had been looted. Feeling slightly exasperated I began to wonder if I would ever be able to get enough items to protect myself. I eventually came across a random other new player and he and I set off to make another house. We constructed one in the middle of a field due to a glitch where we were unable to place our foundation anywhere else and amassed a much larger supply than I could have hoped. We made ourselves shotguns and crafted armor. When we came across new players we gave them pickaxes and hatchets to help them and if they stuck around we protected them from other players. We found it was easy to make alliances with other players by playing nicely and soon we had up to 10 allies. We had been playing for several hours so I said goodbye to my new friends and got off, when I got on later that day I found that our new home had been raided and my friends had been killed by the same players who had spawn camped me in the beginning. My friend messaged me saying that the bandits had come by pretending to be friendly and had gunned everyone down when he opened the door to come out and meet them. Today I will be starting again from scratch.
My one and only complaint about this game is other players' abilities to take your stuff while you are offline. There is literally no way to keep your stuff safe. When you log off your body simply drops to the floor helplessly and will be killed by anyone that finds you. If you are in a house people who can make lockpicks or c4 will destroy your door to get any valuables inside. It is relatively simple to get to "mid game" with the help of others but soon you will realize in order to move up you will need to kill or be killed. This game has a steep learning curve not with basic game mechanics but with how to deal with other players. It is kill or be killed, take the shot or I assure you the other player will. It was a tough lesson to learn and cost me quite a few hours worth of gathering resources but I am looking forward to my next adventure in Rust with a new foreign policy.

Though I do like the premise behind the game, Something about the entire experience rubs me the wrong way. Survival games can be fun, though the only way to play this one is multiplayer- which could be fun except that the entire community that plays this game is far to competitive. Generally the first person you meet will more than likely kill you and loot you, no questions asked, no speech. In my entire play of this game, I've been to about four or five different servers, one of the official servers, heavily populated, and others with very few people. The heavy traffic servers are the worst- you're lucky if you can even spawn without someone killing you. The entire game is an arms race and nothing more. With less people it can be more enjoyable, but overall I have to give this game a thumbs down. The constantly negative player interaction is something I cannot stand in a game, especially one with such a focus on multiplayer survival. I don't care for this community of people, and plan to move on.
Even though it is in early development it is an amazing game with great potential.

Rust is both fun and infuriating.  While it is still in Alpha testing, there is a LOT of work to be done. the game environment is great for this type of game and the concept is similar to Minecraft but much more detailed.  The graphics are a step up, the crafting system is adequate and the interactions can be fun.
Some things to be aware of:
- Player killing is permitted on most servers(and happens every 2 seconds, it's painful.)
- There are "Sleeper" and "No Sleeper" worlds, where when you log out you remain in the game but sleeping on the ground.
- Houses can be broken into and your things stolen.
- You only receive access to basic crafting initially. You must locate blueprints for the more intricate items.
Recommends tips:
- Start on a NO PVP server to get the hang of it.  PvP is horrible on regular servers, you get attacked by some immature child every 2 seconds even if you JUST spawned right in front of them.
- Build a house with a door and a sleeping bag immediately.(Hide your house deep in a forest or mountain.)
- Create two or three houses and space them out and keep your gear spread out between them.  If you get raided you won't lose everything in one hit.
- On a PvP server, DO NOT TRUST ANYONE.

I hope that this game will evolve to a really cool survival game. So ..as conclusion, yep, the game is worth the money, play with your friends and double the fun. ^_^

Theres much to had in the world of Rust, theres trees and ores that you get to beat to death with your nice shiny rock. Theres deer, boars, rabbits, chickens, wolves and bears that you get to smash their face with a rock. You even get moments when a plane flys overhead to drop out some stashes of desirable goodies, but if you still have just your pet rock I wouldnt go for these goodies. There is also many towns, filled with radiation mind you, that you get to take your rock on adventures exploring. And when you find someone else in the wild world of Rust, just scream at them, provide some humor in the moment, because most likely your about to die and your rock will be had. After all, Rust is simple about how long you keep your rock, and about how many rocks you collect throughout all your travels.

After logging 9 hours I feel I've experienced enough to write some what of a review. Rust in alpha is a very rewarding game. Starting (and starting over) with a rock, 2 bandages, and torches your job is to survive.
I've spent the past 9 hours starting over continously, because I went hungry (once) and died from starvation. I was killed by several players, and even one hacker. I have been mauled to death by bears and wolves who saw my half naked piece of man meat and wanted a piece of it. I've had great adventures and heart breaking loses and I've loved every moment of it.
Once I had restarted at night. I found an ore node and harvested it and a couple trees. Started getting dark so I trekked up into the mountains to set up a fire hoping to avoid the attention of other players and safely ride out the night. I realized quickly I was not going to survive the night as I was getting hungrier and hungrier so I trecked down my mountain in the middle of the night to see what I could hunt. Braving the darkness with my torch in spurts, just long enough to scan the area but not long enough to attract the attention of another player I started running through the woods in hopes of encountering a pig, deer, chicken, or rabbit. I had been running through the darkness for 2 minutes when I heard the unmistakable growl of a wolf behind me and it was on. I turned to the wolf lifted my rock and realized if the wolf didn't kill me I was going to starve so I gave it all I had. In the end I was left bleeding and barely alive but I killed that wolf. Hacked his body apart with my stone, hacked some wood from a local tree, and cooked him up as my food reached zero and I began to starve to death. Barely saving myself, but riding out the rest of the night huddled up to the fire with my ears straining to hear the approach of any other player. When daylight came I was relieved, and continued my adventure.
This is just one of the stories I've had and the adventures just keep coming. While the game is only 20% complete, the $19.99 testing fee is well worth it. If you have a chance, and want to see a game that looks beautiful and brings that unknown excitement with real loss that is missing from other games then I suggest you take the plunge and try Rust. So far it reminds me a little bit of UO (without the magic) and Hunger Games.

This game can be seperated in to 5 steps.
These steps are from the begining
Step 1. Freshspawn farming
´When you first spawn in to the game you got nothing else than your rock, some bandages and torch. You will need to set a base of operations in well hidden location and hope that noone will find it before you can fortify it to be safe enough to store goods. You will hit♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of wood piles and rocks with your rock to get enough stuff to make your first base. Process that is slowed by other players that will shoot you in hopes of getting your precious rock and some wood that you might have despite the fact that you just spawned.
Step 2. Building the base and blueprint farming
Once you have eonugh resources to build up your base and get a metal door for your hut so that not every noob in the region can raid your resources. This is the point when you will craft your bow and go farm some bears and wolfs covered in perioid and run through radiated towns in hopes of finding good loot boxes with blueprints or weapons. Your main goal at this point is to get research kits, blueprins and weapons. And again the process is slowed a lot by your friendly neighbors with guns who want to kill you just for the sake of killing.
Step 3. Gearing up and fortifications
After you find good weapons and make sure you  can craft more of them(Really important! You will lose your weapons but you will never lose the knowledge how to make them!). You will need to make♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of ammo, kevlars and guns and fortify your base better with some spikes or making a new metal base whatever floats your boat.
Step 4. Raiding and killing,.. and meeting the hackers
You have come a long way and it is now your time to hunt some newb meat and get easy materials from them. Or craft some explosive charges and go raid someones base. It is time for some pvp action. Sadly this is also the point where you will most likely start meeting a lot of hackers. More ballsy ones will be using stuff like speedhacks, high jumps and flying. More subtle once will use nospreads and aimbots. The game is absolutely riddled with hackers.
Step 5. Losing it all
Eventualy will come the time when your base is raided and you lose it all. Doesnt matter if it was by legit door bombing or by hackers. You are at point zero again and must start anew. Only good thing is, that you still have all your blueprints. And if you had the foresight to hide some stuff and/or make a secondary base you might still have some gear up your sleeves.
In the end, this game is just massive grind and farm fest with occasional shootouts and♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of hackers running around. If you like grinding, building and farming while your stuff are perioidicaly raided and destroyed. This is a game for you.

Dev Blog 121 Review:
Rust has had this problem since the beginning. I occasionally check back on updates when people like Faceless, Zuckles, or Rhino Crunch post videos on YouTube. Don't get me wrong, the game is probably fun if you can spend 2-3 hours playing it every day without break. For that reason, I basically haven't played rust in like a Year outside of like 5 hours scattered across a few patch tests.
Rust consistently forces players to join clans, and they offer no alternative play styles for people who would want to have a try at survival without dedicating hour every single day.
Simply put, Rust has (and probably will always have) bad game design because the developers will never address the very serious issue of unstoppable snowballing which nearly every AAA multiplayer game addresses effectively.
People who join clans and play all day handicap skill with their time to the extent that casual players who might be clever builders/gathers and skillful shots will 8/10 get wiped. Adding to this, has a severe shortage on mechanics which leads to these unstoppable groups steam rolling the quarter of half of the map where they have their bases.
Basically this is ONLY for players willing to throw a solid 10 - 20 hours a week every week into this game alone. This game is essentially a part time job that you don't get paid to do.

This is a long review. It lists good and bad aspects of the game; while I strive to make it both comprehensive and impartial, I can only work from my personal experience and  opinion.  I hope you find it useful, specially if you're considering buying the game.
Rust is a post-apocalyptic survival FPS,
being the operative word.
And in order to survive, you will have to gather resources required to craft almost everything you can use in the game (from stone hatchets to automatic rifles), hunt for food and clothing, build your house and fend off attackers.
While many recent games offer the same basic premise, in Rust it is implemented in a very interesting way; designing and building up your base of operations is quite enjoyable, specially because you have to be smart about your design, as burglars are always looking for weak spots to invade your home and steal your stuff.
The crafting aspect offers some degree of depth, since you need to process raw resources in order to acquire building materials with which you can build parts of your house or other items. It's not just mind-numbing resource farming and it does bring a sense of accomplishment, as you can learn how to craft more advanced items as you progress in the game.
The sandbox map is big and there are several points of interest where you can find special items, like blueprints for weapons/armor, ammo and other stuff. Those places tend to attract players, so in any reasonably populated server, they will be PVP hotspots.
Those places are usually easy to find (just follow the gunshots). Anywhere in the map, however, you really have to pay attention to your surroundings, as there is no navigating system in the game (no compass, no gps-like device, not even a map, nada!), which I personally find refreshing, but it takes some time to get familiar with the geography. Boulders and hills have a dismaying low genetic variation, therefore many places look quite exactly like others. On the other hand, the sun rises and sets at the right directions, east and west, so it is possible to navigate with some degree of accuracy, as long as you can tell your left hand from the right one. Even so, until you actually know the map, it's very easy to get lost, specially during the pitch-black hours of the night.
Since this is an environment full of pockets of radiation, rabid animals and aggressive players, it's not a good idea to wander around aimlessly, and it's better to  sit tight until the sun is up again before moving too far. You spawn with torches, and while they do provide a 3-feet radius of light around you, their true purpose is a bit more sinister: They broadcast to all beasts and aggressive players alike in a radius of three miles that a clueless, unarmed new player has just spawned, and you don't want that.
There's a widespread culture of killing other players on sight and, regardless of how careful you are, eventually you will run into the wrong player(s), at the wrong place and time. Sometimes it makes for an exhilarating fight, sometimes it will be a heart-pounding escape in order to save the materials you've been harvesting for the last hour... and sometimes it will be a bunch of bored older players equipped with automatic weapons, reinforced armor and every existing item in the game shooting the crap out of just spawned, naked new players.
It can be somewhat frustrating in the beginning, as you're likely to die a lot and lose items, but once you get the hang of the game and make a few friends, it's a blast. While you can play on your own, it's much better to find some like-minded fellows and band together, because, as your enemies already know, there's strenght in numbers, to the point that even an actively defended base can still be raided by a persistent and well-coordinated group.
Despite still being in Alpha stage, Rust has a tremendous potential to achieve greatness. It's been consistently among the five top sellers for a reason and, in the right server and company, you can really enjoy this game. I surely do.
Unfortunately, at such an early development phase, the game is also plagued by serious issues that can make your experience
.
First and foremost, there are too many ways to grief other players, like building stuff on other player's foundations. That means a troll can use C4 to destroy the front door of your house and replace it with another one that YOU, the house owner, can't open or close.
Likewise, they can destroy a flight of stairs and replace it with a ceiling, which is currently undestructable, completely and permanently cutting off acess to other floors, ruining all the hours of work you put into your base - and they do that just for "sh¡ts and giggles".
They don't even need to actually get inside your house; if you're not careful, they can build walls to block your door or around the house, locking you inside/outside.
I actually like the whole raiding idea, so I don't have a problem with the fact that you can't completely prevent people from invading your base (in part due to bugs and exploits), but you can (theoretically) make it so difficult that it's just not worth the trouble.
But I do find it unsettling that, in practice, with
, people are able to undo other's players work so completely that it might render their game unfeasible from that point onwards, and they would be better off starting over in another server rather than rebuilding.
Hacking is also a serious issue at the moment. For example:
Suicide is a game feature. You can kill yourself in order to respawn in a more favorable spot on the map or back at your base, but you will lose any items you have in your inventory. Some people somehow are able to exploit that feature and "suicide" other players, which means you can be suddenly killed anywhere, anytime, and have your possessions stolen or lost.
It's not funny when that happen while you're in the middle of a supply run, miles away from your respawn point.
In two separated occasions, while playing on different servers, not only I had some guy join the game, suicide me and disconnect right away, but I also found out the shelters I had just put up (so it wasn't decay) had vanished as well, along with everything inside.
It doesn't help that admin abuse also seems to be commonplace.
Your mileage may vary, but in the last week I've seen:
- Invisible people rummaging through my storage boxes (supposedly safe between locked metal doors inside multi-story buildings) to see if there's anything worth taking in a raid (which happened the next day while I was offline);
- Admin über-items being used by players;
- Massive airdrops flooding the servers with items that should be extremely rare;
- mass-production and distribution of said items for those few selected friends of the powers that be...
...and several other things so stupid they just don't merit a description, usually resulting in a terribly unbalanced environment where the server is completely dominated by one group or clan full of bored players, while the other players struggle to put up a shack and find anything worth taking (only to have it destroyed/taken in a matter of hours).
Even if you never meet a hacker or an asshat administrator, the server browser will give you all the grief you need, and then some. The history doesn't work, the server you've been playing in for two days vanishes from the list forever, it will refresh and find no servers at all.
Rust can be a lot of fun and I still recommend the game, as long as you can live with the many shortcomings present in such an early production stage and
if you're willing to look past the bugs and the aggravating behavior displayed both by the software and the players. Otherwise, wait a few months until the developers are able to smooth out some rough edges.

Rust has really matured over the 2-3 years I've had it. Recent updates have put a hefty focus on scavenging rather than crafting, which has removed a lot of the grind present in the game before. You can now be kitted out and running around with guns in about an hour or two, although not fully kitted out to raid bases. Explosives are easier to get than ever, but not unfairly so. There's good weapon variety (melee and ranged) and the combat is heart-wrenching and enjoyable. Encounters with other players are always tense, as is customary in the survival-multiplayer-PVP genre. On certain servers, groups and clans host massive raids on eachother, often with over 50 people involved.
One of my only issues with the game is its blatantly bad optimization. Even cards like the GTX 970 or RX 480 have issues hitting 60fps approaching higher settings, and on lower settings the game just looks plain bad. Another prominent issue is animals (specifically bears and wolves) glitching through terrain and unfairly killing you. Can't count how many times I've lost all of my stuff because a bear decided that it wanted to walk straight through a rock wall.
Regardless, if your PC is up to the task, Rust is an excellent survival game.

This is a long review. It lists good and bad aspects of the game; while I strive to make it both comprehensive and impartial, I can only work from my personal experience and  opinion.  I hope you find it useful, specially if you're considering buying the game.
Rust is a post-apocalyptic survival FPS,
being the operative word.
And in order to survive, you will have to gather resources required to craft almost everything you can use in the game (from stone hatchets to automatic rifles), hunt for food and clothing, build your house and fend off attackers.
While many recent games offer the same basic premise, in Rust it is implemented in a very interesting way; designing and building up your base of operations is quite enjoyable, specially because you have to be smart about your design, as burglars are always looking for weak spots to invade your home and steal your stuff.
The crafting aspect offers some degree of depth, since you need to process raw resources in order to acquire building materials with which you can build parts of your house or other items. It's not just mind-numbing resource farming and it does bring a sense of accomplishment, as you can learn how to craft more advanced items as you progress in the game.
The sandbox map is big and there are several points of interest where you can find special items, like blueprints for weapons/armor, ammo and other stuff. Those places tend to attract players, so in any reasonably populated server, they will be PVP hotspots.
Those places are usually easy to find (just follow the gunshots). Anywhere in the map, however, you really have to pay attention to your surroundings, as there is no navigating system in the game (no compass, no gps-like device, not even a map, nada!), which I personally find refreshing, but it takes some time to get familiar with the geography. Boulders and hills have a dismaying low genetic variation, therefore many places look quite exactly like others. On the other hand, the sun rises and sets at the right directions, east and west, so it is possible to navigate with some degree of accuracy, as long as you can tell your left hand from the right one. Even so, until you actually know the map, it's very easy to get lost, specially during the pitch-black hours of the night.
Since this is an environment full of pockets of radiation, rabid animals and aggressive players, it's not a good idea to wander around aimlessly, and it's better to  sit tight until the sun is up again before moving too far. You spawn with torches, and while they do provide a 3-feet radius of light around you, their true purpose is a bit more sinister: They broadcast to all beasts and aggressive players alike in a radius of three miles that a clueless, unarmed new player has just spawned, and you don't want that.
There's a widespread culture of killing other players on sight and, regardless of how careful you are, eventually you will run into the wrong player(s), at the wrong place and time. Sometimes it makes for an exhilarating fight, sometimes it will be a heart-pounding escape in order to save the materials you've been harvesting for the last hour... and sometimes it will be a bunch of bored older players equipped with automatic weapons, reinforced armor and every existing item in the game shooting the crap out of just spawned, naked new players.
It can be somewhat frustrating in the beginning, as you're likely to die a lot and lose items, but once you get the hang of the game and make a few friends, it's a blast. While you can play on your own, it's much better to find some like-minded fellows and band together, because, as your enemies already know, there's strenght in numbers, to the point that even an actively defended base can still be raided by a persistent and well-coordinated group.
Despite still being in Alpha stage, Rust has a tremendous potential to achieve greatness. It's been consistently among the five top sellers for a reason and, in the right server and company, you can really enjoy this game. I surely do.
Unfortunately, at such an early development phase, the game is also plagued by serious issues that can make your experience
.
First and foremost, there are too many ways to grief other players, like building stuff on other player's foundations. That means a troll can use C4 to destroy the front door of your house and replace it with another one that YOU, the house owner, can't open or close.
Likewise, they can destroy a flight of stairs and replace it with a ceiling, which is currently undestructable, completely and permanently cutting off acess to other floors, ruining all the hours of work you put into your base - and they do that just for "sh¡ts and giggles".
They don't even need to actually get inside your house; if you're not careful, they can build walls to block your door or around the house, locking you inside/outside.
I actually like the whole raiding idea, so I don't have a problem with the fact that you can't completely prevent people from invading your base (in part due to bugs and exploits), but you can (theoretically) make it so difficult that it's just not worth the trouble.
But I do find it unsettling that, in practice, with
, people are able to undo other's players work so completely that it might render their game unfeasible from that point onwards, and they would be better off starting over in another server rather than rebuilding.
Hacking is also a serious issue at the moment. For example:
Suicide is a game feature. You can kill yourself in order to respawn in a more favorable spot on the map or back at your base, but you will lose any items you have in your inventory. Some people somehow are able to exploit that feature and "suicide" other players, which means you can be suddenly killed anywhere, anytime, and have your possessions stolen or lost.
It's not funny when that happen while you're in the middle of a supply run, miles away from your respawn point.
In two separated occasions, while playing on different servers, not only I had some guy join the game, suicide me and disconnect right away, but I also found out the shelters I had just put up (so it wasn't decay) had vanished as well, along with everything inside.
It doesn't help that admin abuse also seems to be commonplace.
Your mileage may vary, but in the last week I've seen:
- Invisible people rummaging through my storage boxes (supposedly safe between locked metal doors inside multi-story buildings) to see if there's anything worth taking in a raid (which happened the next day while I was offline);
- Admin über-items being used by players;
- Massive airdrops flooding the servers with items that should be extremely rare;
- mass-production and distribution of said items for those few selected friends of the powers that be...
...and several other things so stupid they just don't merit a description, usually resulting in a terribly unbalanced environment where the server is completely dominated by one group or clan full of bored players, while the other players struggle to put up a shack and find anything worth taking (only to have it destroyed/taken in a matter of hours).
Even if you never meet a hacker or an asshat administrator, the server browser will give you all the grief you need, and then some. The history doesn't work, the server you've been playing in for two days vanishes from the list forever, it will refresh and find no servers at all.
Rust can be a lot of fun and I still recommend the game, as long as you can live with the many shortcomings present in such an early production stage and
if you're willing to look past the bugs and the aggravating behavior displayed both by the software and the players. Otherwise, wait a few months until the developers are able to smooth out some rough edges.

Игра затянула меня еще на открытой альфе, хоть и лагала безбожно (частично из за слабого ноута). В общем суть проста, тебя выкидывают в открытый мир с одним лишь камнем двумя бинтами и факелом. Камнем надо пилить деревья на дрова и долбить камни на руду (только одиноко стоящие круглые камни, респавнящиеся рандомно по карте, я же не одупляя этого 3 минуты долбил скалу). Из деревьев делаем простенькую халупу с ящиком для награбленного и идем добывать еду, иначе скоро окочуримся. Камень меняем на каменный топор. В альфе пока есть медведи волки олени и кабаны. Чтобы не парится и гонять кабана бейте волка и после перевяжитесь бинтом. Просто мясо есть нельзя или обблюешься, надо жарить его на костре Из больших камней добываем собственно камни, медную руду и железную руду, чтобы плавить руду необходима специальная каменная печь, дабы избежать непоняток с ней в нее тоже надо запихивать дрова. Железная руда лежит в основе всех дальнейших ништяков, далее строим верстак чтобы клепать огнестрел и патроны к нему. Кстати не забудьте сшить одежду, она дает бонусы к защите от разных типов урона. Вскоре вам покажется что вы уже слепили все что только можно, а вот х"й. В особо опасных радиоактивных зонах с зомбями лежит самый вкусный лут от антирадиационных костюмов, модулей и карабинов до собственно чертежей к ним. Чертежи хороши тем что их стоит выучить раз и потом хоть миллион раз вас убьют вы все равно при достаточном количестве ресурсов соберете то что выучили. В ощем могу сказать что для альфы игра очень даже ничего, купить стоит, но конечно приготовьтесь к бесконечным патчам и обновам (дотерам не привыкать). Из плюсов это все плюсы DayZ и майнкрафта вместе взятых, из минусов невозможность сносить свои дома, из за чего карта всегда нагромождена квадратными хижинами, что несколько раздражает, надеюсь исправят. Ну и типичные минусы альфы присутствуют. Желаю удачи ребятам из facepunch а вам приятной игры.

Rust is not for the faint of heart or for those quick to rage. Rust, in its current stages, is quite the amazing game. Gathering chicken meat from pigs, deer, and wolves has never been so much fun! You start out with a rock and work your way up to bows and guns - eventually grenades and C4. The controls are pretty quick to figure out, smooth, and I liked the style of graphics. I do hope for more customization in the future.
I highly recommend playing on a non-pvp server when you first start playing rust to get used to the controls, and how to survive when you begin playing (i.e. what you need to craft different items, and how to quickly set up your own liveable space)
There are many different tricks for survival - such as healing your walls / doors with wood (if you're in a wooden shack at the start) when someone is trying to break it down at night.
Rust is an experience that I will never forget, and will return to time and time again.
Beware trusting players in this game, as it is easy for them to turn on you, kill you - and leave you with nothing. Always have a back-up plan. This game is best played in groups, but I live for solo survival.

Overall I would consider this a great game especially since it is only in early access. I remember when I played the first release of the game which really was just a bunch of ugly rocks, terribly textured grass, lots of zombies, bugs, and worsed of all millions of shelters dotting the landscape. The developers have made a great deal of progress in the development of the game but there still are some problems. Other then the occasional bugs here and there the game overall is not for those hoping to be friends with anyone for any period of time. On most servers the second you join you are at risk of being killed. This of course, is a surival game but not only against the elements but against mankind itself. If you are looking for another Minecraft don't bother buying this game since you will spend much more time shooting then you will building. Of course there is a great deal of building as well but only of bases where you can survive the cruel days and the worse nights.
Game strengths:
- Great Developer Dedication to fixing bugs and banning hackers in a somewhat timely fashion (most hackers have to purchase new accounts on a monthly basis)
- Great Enviornment for PVP (I love hardcore games like this)
- Endless nights in your basement where all you want to do is play Rust
- Great to play with friends (you won't survive without them)
Problems with the game:
- Lots of hackers.. Althought they do ban lots of hackers just as quickly new hacks come out and new hackers buy the game or repurchase it on a new steam account. Regardless of the efforts made to reduce the amount of hackers you will still encounter hackers on an almost daily basis but many of these hacks will probably be patched eventually. Regardless of the hackers I would say the game is still worth buying at this time.
Overall Rating: 8/10

Rust is one of the most addicting games I've played in years.
Rust brings a lot to the table. It's almost too much. Rust has far, far exceeded the expectations of the developers, and I'm struggling to figure out why. They should have expected this game to become huge. Here are the reasons:
1. It brings that whole "crafting" and "building" addiction from minecraft into a legitimate engine.
2. It brings the abject horror of surviving in a harsh, cold, deadly environment filled with people you can't trust from "Day - Z" (They even borrowed the zombies.)
3. It brings big time first person shooter aspects into becoming the king of your server. (I believe they borrowed the spray pattern from CS:GO?)
It has EVERYTHING that any casual or hardcore junkie could ever want. Unfortunately, this also includes the bad things that come with everything just listed above.
1. Who doesn't know about griefing by now? If I had a dollar for every time some troll blocked me out of my base...
2. It brings the idea that a group of friends. (5-10) can pretty much own any given server if they're well coordinated, so playing alone gives a huge disadvantage.
3. There's hackers.
All in all you have to keep in mind Rust is still in ALPHA. This game is absurdly good. I'm just sad they didn't believe people would agree with me.

Before I begin, Rust is not a "Zombie" Survival game. It is a "Survival" game where you face mother nature as well as other players. The game was not intended to be a "Zombie" survival game. As well Rust is in it's "Alpha" stages, meaning that this game is far from being complete. As Facepunch studios said "game is not 95% complete, it's only about 10% complete" So you must understand you're buying an incomplete game which will be completely different from the finished version. Forget what your friends may or may not have said. With this said, Rust for what it is, is worth the $20 for an incomplete game. Yes it maybe frustrating to die the 100th time in a row, but once you've built your house, you truly feel a sense of accomplishment. Finding the one person who doesn't chase after you naked with a rock and pooling your resources together adds more depth to the game. I've found the most enjoyable thing about this game is hunting the wildlife. I love moving from bush to bush, sliently, before I draw the bow back to land the killing blow. How real it feels as I beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of an animal with my crude "skinning" rock for meat and cloth so I can survive the night.
How great this game is, it does have some flaws, for example, some players have been playing for so long (veterans) that they only hunt "noobs" now. I've died plenty of times from veterans, but I take a break from the game, understand what I did wrong (don't run around with a bright♥♥♥♥♥torch in the middle of the night,  you're asking to be killed) and I try to improve for next time. But keep in mind, the game is only 10% complete, things will change.
Overall, I recommend this game to those who don't mind working hard to the top, meeting new people (Best played with friends!), or are just looking for an escape from the real world.

240 HOURS OF GAMEPLAY:
My "don't recommend it" review is below this one. I have changed my stance surrounding the game a bit. It can be fun if you manage to get a couple of walls and a metal door up. Don't hoard stuff, it's just going to end up in some other guy's crates anyway! Live in the now, don't save stuff for later.
As I play alone I tend to have a harder time than most. No one to cover me, defend our base or help gathering resources. I have learned your best bet at survival in this case is to be friendly to anyone you meet.
See guys in armour with guns? Give them some ammo for a gun you don't even have.
See a guy being chased by animals? Shoot them, lend him some food and go on.
Just by doing this and never ever shooting them I became friends with an entire server. No one raided me, no one shot me (on purpose), they gave me stuff for being a good sport, if I get killed they give me my stuff back, etc...
The game is brutal, survival is hard with all the hostile people. But perserverance and patience WILL get you along the dangerous roads of the world of Rust.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
30 HOURS OF GAMEPLAY:
I've been playing Rust for 30 hours now and all I can say is that it's anything but entertaining. Not because of the game. But because of the community.
Do you plan to play this game without friends? Don't. You will get robbed, raided, shot, clubbed and mauled by everything. Do not think of making friends inside the game, the people you share a fire with will kill you as soon as they can. do not think someone who says he's friendly, will be friendly. He'll be that until you turn your back to him. When you finaly manage to build a house of your own, know that the next day it WILL be raided of everything of value. They wait until you leave so they can take your belongings unopposed. But that doesn't matter because they all have modern weapons they can always recraft against your flimsy bow or medieval rifle.
Do you plan to play this game with friends? Good luck, it will take an hour before everyone is at the same place and alive! After that your main problem will be food and shelter. But because you are in a big group of people this will not be difficult. After that all that's left to be done is craft guns and rob people really. The next problem will be keeping your base defended. Big group of people = big base = large treasure chest for other people. Be prepared to do the same thing each night all over again unless you have someone who can stay online 24/7.
I must say not everyone's corrupted, but those people are new to the game and havent yet seen the devastating lack of morality this game radiates. You think the community of LoL is bad? Or that of Call of Duty? Try Rust.
Let's talk about the game itself now, shall we? The game looks nice, astounding even for the Unity Engine it's built on. It doesn't shun adult nudity. Oh and the concept is wonderfull. But that's probably it, the animals have only one sound effect per type, they run stuttery from location to location. Wolves and bears do NOT stop chasing you, even if they can't see nor hear nor smell you. Your only choice is to face them or let them kill you. And then there are the zombies, who populate the irradiated places. Or rather, used to populate.
At first the zombies were dangerous, yet manageable for even a freshly spawned person, albeit a bit of finesse and skill was needed. Facepunch has chosen to replace them with something else because "they didn't want Rust to be a DayZ clone". Now we have regular wolves and bears. And red painted wolves and bears! So the exact same annoying creature you can't even kill meleewise unless you are loaded on medkits or it lags to one spot. Just got copy pasted and painted red. The zombies made sense, this however...
Before I end this review I'd like to say I did not make this out of pettyness like most of the other negative reviews. I played the game for a good enough amount of time and experienced it all. For as much I could at least. I did not enjoy myself for the most part. The only times I did was when I managed to take over a house no one lived in. I have yet to kill another human in this game, mostly because I didn't want too. I regret my decision of never killing others as well as buying this game.
TL;DR: don't buy it unless you plan to play with friends and expect hours of work for a bit of fun.

Some interesting experiences that happened to me in this survival game:
A friendly played the Lion King song as the sun rose. (Sunrise in Rust is a very special thing indeed)
I took a chance with the randomized air drop and somehow managed to get away with almost all the loot, even though I was naked and unarmed. (Although I got shot at)
I met a nice guy who gave me 40 chicken. I ended up losing it when I died but it still restored my faith in humanity.
Had a dance party with guys playing Tunak Tunak Tun around a campfire before a gunman crashed it.
Joined a guy who ended up trolling people at night by playing creepy sounds outside their house. We got some pretty funny reactions.
Led a pack of wolves back to a hostiles camp and looted all their stuff as most of them died and had their hands full. And the wolves heads clipped through their homes and bit them dead. Sweeeeet revenge.
Its one rollarcoaster of a game at the moment but I'm glad I got it. And if you are looking for a fun and friendly dude to play it with look no further. :P

Rust is one of the most addicting games I've played in years.
Rust brings a lot to the table. It's almost too much. Rust has far, far exceeded the expectations of the developers, and I'm struggling to figure out why. They should have expected this game to become huge. Here are the reasons:
1. It brings that whole "crafting" and "building" addiction from minecraft into a legitimate engine.
2. It brings the abject horror of surviving in a harsh, cold, deadly environment filled with people you can't trust from "Day - Z" (They even borrowed the zombies.)
3. It brings big time first person shooter aspects into becoming the king of your server. (I believe they borrowed the spray pattern from CS:GO?)
It has EVERYTHING that any casual or hardcore junkie could ever want. Unfortunately, this also includes the bad things that come with everything just listed above.
1. Who doesn't know about griefing by now? If I had a dollar for every time some troll blocked me out of my base...
2. It brings the idea that a group of friends. (5-10) can pretty much own any given server if they're well coordinated, so playing alone gives a huge disadvantage.
3. There's hackers.
All in all you have to keep in mind Rust is still in ALPHA. This game is absurdly good. I'm just sad they didn't believe people would agree with me.

A fun yet frustrating survival game. My first few playthroughs were very average. Collect wood, rocks, ores, kill to survive and many more survival like traits. After a couple of playthroughs I decided I was ready to go to a server with alot of people in it. It was decent, people talked like how any other online people talk (usally insults). The spawn point was filled with wooden shacks with locked doors people built to keep others out. There was no point of staying there so I left and went on a journey with nothing but a rock, 2 medkits, and a torch, As I was wandering around looking for a place to build camp I see a giant unfinished tower made up of wood built by a player or group of players as a home. Knowing never to cross path with anyone who built that, I avoided it until I saw a shack with a door wide open. Some player must have forgotten to close it. I went to the shack as quietly as I could and I looted as much as I can. Apparently this shack was kinda like a loot shack. they put nothing but material like cloth, wood, stones, a couple hatchets  and alot of meat. My God there was so much meat, It seemed as if who ever built this was a bandit making it big. I took about a quarter of how much meat they had, a stone hatchet, and some wood and stones. I ran away as fast as I could and had an Idea of becoming a meat trader. Even though online players could easily kill me I took the risk. I traveled back to the spawn point, built a shack, and annouced I was trading meat for supplies. Players responded and we met at several places to insure that we wouldn't be ambushed. Surprisingly most did not try to kill me and were very polite. I guess players didn't want to risk killing me due to me being their supplier. Some however, were not that smart and tried to kill me. They did not succeed. It was going good, I earned a decent amount of stuff, no guns but materials like wood and stone. All fine and dandy until I ran out. As much as I hated to go out into the wilderness, I couldn't help but to try and find the very same shack and get more meat. About halfway into the journey I was ambushed by 3 wolves. What the luck I had. I tried to outrun them and I was almost out of their sight but only to hear gunshots in front of me, a group of hunters. My luck was getting worse. Wolves behind me and hunters to my front. I had to run either to the left or the right. I decided to pick left but it led to my death. I ran into one of the hunters who was collecting woods. He saw me. My heart was pumping, was he gonna kill me or the wolves? He pulled out his gun and starting shooting. I hid behind a rock and I had no choice but to let the wolves get near. I wondered if they would attack him instead and ignore me. I gambled with my life. The wolves got near and looked as if they were running at him but changed direction as soon as they were 10 feet away from me. You can guess what happened then and you would be right. Ironic, I died by wolves rather than a player.

I can't recommend this game YET. It is destined to be a good game in the future, but right now it is still too early alpha.
The good:
Rust exceeds at being a social game, something it's competitors (Day Z, War Z) lack. There are lots of community building mechanics that encourage players to cooperate and build social heirarchies, like passwords for doors on your shelter. It also has non-PVP servers.
The bad:
Resources are far too scarce. Wood is easy enough to find as there are trees everywhere, but animals and rocks, things you use for 90% of your recipes, are way too rare of an occurance. I get it, it's a post-apocalyptic crafting game. Resources should be rare, but I can only wander for so long until I get bored.
The game runs terrible. I have an Nvidia GT 430, which isn't a great video card I know, but it exceeds the minimum system requirnments by quite a bit and it is nearly unplayable.
DO get Rust, but wait until it's in beta.

Free Roam Survival. These types of games do not go well with the Loner type. You will be found and raided, killed or robbed by naked men. This game is a ton of fun, with a very impressive Alpha that is currently active and available to the public to play. It promises allot more and with doubt it will happen. Seeing that its from the same Great Creator of Garry's Mod. It has very distinct qualities that puts it apart from any other game you compare it to. It has Crafting, It is Online, It has Building and it has Nude bambi's running around armed with a rock heading towards your shack of loot or your head. Its a game where you need a group to survive, be too friendly and you die. Be to mean and people make you a target... well lets say "More" of a target. Try to have a fair balance between Saint and Bandit, but most importantly: Have a good group. Communication is vital. Use Team Speak to talk to your team, and only use in Game chat when you need to talk to someone you don't know. Otherwise everyone is in on your little secret and might just want to come give their Lead opinion.  Sound is one of this game's best and most prominent features. You can hear the environment around you. You can hear people moving and sneaking, and also gun fire, explosions and so on. Use the basics to get by, get a group and use your head. This game will keep you alert and very jumpy. But its all worth it. Other than that for more tips on how to survive Rust go watch some FRANKIEonPC! Videos on Youtube. I got my basics there and well, I haven't been nude since. Happy Hunting in the world of Rust, and don't stay nude for too long... Its cold out there, your little fellow does not like the cold.

This game is barely finished and has entertained 15 hours from me in just 3 days. Dear God it's so worth it. It's one of those games that gives a really player-driven experience and forces you to interact with others, or risk losing everything.
There are problems with the game right now, and to sum those up I would say that right now it's a little too difficult to get established as a newbie on a ~50 player server. You can get comfortable with a reasonable amount of resources and be able to defend yourself while online, but as soon as you go offline your character is left as a sleeper in the game world. At that point, people can simply destroy your poorly defended hut with one or two C4 bundles and take everything with ease. The result is that you have to spend 1 or 2 consecutive, successful hours of survival to be able to continue beyond cloth armor, pipe shotguns and a 1x1 single-floor wooden shack. It's hard, it's a little unforgiving, and I think the game would be better if new spawns on a server had more ability to defend themselves.

TLDR: Buy Rust, best $20 you'll ever spend.
After nearly a thousand hours game time, I have to say Rust is possibly one of the best FPS Survival games around, if not THE best.
The gunplay is tense whether its bows & spears or a gunfight, resembling gunplay in CS:GO - that is, functional but not too realistic so as to drown the user. Gunplay in a game like this doesnt need to be as realistic as possible, it just needs to be functional, responsive and skilled enough that anyone can learn.
Music can be very atmospheric, especially with environments like the Caverns or the Oil Tank, affectionately known as "The Dome" or "The Death Star". The water drops and wind in the Caverns or the groan of the rusted metal @ the Dome is amazing.
Sound is snappy, directional and generally accurate - given its an alpha though, there can be sound issues with direction from time to time. This shouldnt dissuade the user though, as it is only a minor gripe and generally is fixed quickly.
Building and the component system make the game interesting and accessible by Noobs and Hardcores alike, while not being so restrictive that the game becomes far too PvE than PvP and generally detracts from the gunplay.
All in all, this game is fantastic. Servers are generally good, patches are frequent and it really seems like the Devs have an honest direction about what they want.

UPDATE FOR RUST REVIEW: Ok, So I began playing it a bit more with some friends. And I've decided that 1) The game isn't as bad as I had originally stated but 2) I would still not recommend it to anyone.
The biggest turn-off for me with this game is the dependability, which comes in the form of "decay". For those of you that don't know, in Rust, when you build a structure, that structure will slowly take damage while you are offline. If you stay offline for a week or so, most of your wooden structures will have decayed away, leaving you open and exposed on the inside. This is a very poor design in my opinion, because it forces players to play on a regular basis to really enjoy the game.

If you want to build a huge castle in the mountain, you can.
The game never truely logs you out, if you log out, your character faceplants on the floor. Anyone walking by can kill you, which is why making a shelter is crucial to preserve your survival and loot. The game is nearly in alpha stage, and yet has great gameplay replayability and challenges. Once this game is complete, it will surely be spectacular. Also, <3 Garry!
Almost forgot, devs are very quick to pump out updates and tweak the game as need be. Garry is also very transparent with his thoughts and dev process. And has a very non-hold hand mentality, which is great and different from most other games.
I highly recommend people to try this game.

What's wrong?
The resource "node" system is boring and very tedious.

Crafting appears to be currently a last developed concept so it is extremly basic for now.
Memory leaks causing servers to lag and make pvp un doable.
The good:
When not lagging pvp is fast and fun.
This also applies when/if you actually find someone.
The house building system is basic but shows possibilities.
Overall:
I wouldn't have bought it until further in development as they have already sold lots of copies, but from update logs it does not seem that is rolling over to the game itself.
As it stands right now, if your going to play solo then don't buy it.
If you have a group then you may possibly be able to get stuff to be able to actually play.
Enjoy.

I won. Claiming my opponent's rock as my trophy, I felt immortal. A very different man (actually wearing clothes) soon approached me from the right. He said he just watched me kill a man in cold blood. I tried explaining! With a gun in my face I panicked. I didn't know how to explain how he challenged me first! My mugger grew impatient.
"What time is it?"
"Uh...about 7PM?"
"Oh really?! I think it's time for you to die!"
A mere second had passed before my eyes were filled with hot lead and my brain turned to nothing but dust. After respawning I read a single chat message...
"Welcome to Rust motherf*cker"
7/10 Great fun at this stage, can't wait for the game's future. :D

In this game you play as a geologist who lost his clothes. Coincedentally there are many geologists around you who also seem to have lost their clothes. You must use your knowledge of rocks to take control of the surrounding area in an effort to find your clothes whilst at the same time protecting and maintaining your rock collection. You may team up with other geologists to find the best rocks, or fight off others in an effort to keep the number one rock collection. In the hours I have played this game I have become one of the greatest geologists this world has ever seen, and I do say that my rock collection is quite impressive. You will come across many a geologist who will be jealous at the sight of your mighty rock collection, and in turn you must destroy them so they do not interfere with your studying of the minerals in the game. Eventually it will turn into all out war and you will be forced to do the unthinkable in order to protect that which you have strived for so long. 10/10 an Emotional Roller-coaster the whole way.

I really enjoy this game, this is a very cut throat game... a bit like old runescape PKing, because you kill or be killed. Higher skill level and group numbers play a big part in your success. This game is for the hardcore gamers. Its also very great in the sense that people can do whatever you want. If you want to make an alliance and backstab them, you can. If you want to build a huge castle in the mountain, you can.
The game never truely logs you out, if you log out, your character faceplants on the floor. Anyone walking by can kill you, which is why making a shelter is crucial to preserve your survival and loot. The game is nearly in alpha stage, and yet has great gameplay replayability and challenges. Once this game is complete, it will surely be spectacular. Also, <3 Garry!
Almost forgot, devs are very quick to pump out updates and tweak the game as need be. Garry is also very transparent with his thoughts and dev process. And has a very non-hold hand mentality, which is great and different from most other games.
I highly recommend people to try this game.

Current rating: 6/10
Possible future rating 10/10
What's wrong?
The resource "node" system is boring and very tedious.
The map is made for a few hundred players and takes a ridiculus amount of time to traverse. Thus leaving it mainly barren.
With the map being so large, the problem is most servers have under a hundred players.
Damage seems to be incorrect as a person in leather can survive 4 shotgun blasts, that shows all shots hit. While someone in kevlar(highest armor) can get 1 shotted by a p250 ( pistol)
Crafting appears to be currently a last developed concept so it is extremly basic for now.
Memory leaks causing servers to lag and make pvp un doable.
The good:
When not lagging pvp is fast and fun.
This also applies when/if you actually find someone.
The house building system is basic but shows possibilities.
Overall:
I wouldn't have bought it until further in development as they have already sold lots of copies, but from update logs it does not seem that is rolling over to the game itself.
As it stands right now, if your going to play solo then don't buy it.
If you have a group then you may possibly be able to get stuff to be able to actually play.
Enjoy.

While this game is fun to mess around with for a short while, it gets tiring fast. If you play on a non-pvp server you will realize how the zombies and radiation just become a mute challenge and that if you are building it is just a grind to find resources and collect. This wouldn't be as big of a problem if what you built could last through a game update, but every time the game updates you lose your progress and have to start over. Now none of this would be an issue if the community was a bit nicer.
During my time I quickly realized that the only thing somewhat fun in the game is playing a pvp server. I quickly found a lower population server and made 'friends', but as soon as I had enough resources these friends killed me and looted my corpse. So then I moved to another server since that one was dying and I had nothing left, and it feels that the same thing is consistent among the community in the ~6 servers I played on. Pvp also is heavily unbalanced since automatic weapons and armor tip the scale so heavily. When you get killed you lose any gear that was on you and those with the power keep the power and increase their power. The weapons need to be more like the handmade shotgun and less like automatic m4's with lasers, flashlights, and holographic sights.
While I know this game is in alpha and this is what you can expect, a completely unbalanced game that need a lot of work, I will not recommend this game until the developers fix their mistakes. One final note is that the resource regeneration within the server should depend on the population of that server. So if you have a server with 30 people on it that resources will replenish fast enough for all 30 people to have a SHOT at finding a stone or something. One of the dedicated non-pvp servers I played on had an insane amount of people, an incredible amount of lag, and yet every time a node popped up there was someone around to instantly claim it. I spent around 3 hours on that server only to find 2 rock nodes and 4 wood nodes.
I will change my recommendation later when this game has it's improvements, but currently I can't recommend a game where  there is little non pvp challenge, yet the gap when playing pvp is so large.
EDIT:
It has been 11 months since my last review and currently the game has a new version available. The version my review is on is called 'legacy' and the current version is nothing to be excited about. The legacy version of the game was glitchy and problematic, but fun. This new version isn't fun at all. They fixed some issues with resources, but created other issues with those resources. While the new version looks great, the actual gameplay is pretty boring. I still prefer the legacy version. Even though this new version has been out for some time now the legacy servers still have plenty of people.
The problem with this game in its current state is it appears that the community prefers to play legacy, but the developers aren't doing anything for the legacy version anymore. Looking at the patch notes it looks like progress for the Rust game as a whole is pretty slow.
Even with the incredible hype this game got and the huge amount of copies sold they Rust staff maybe got too much money too fast. Since instead of improving upon the Rust game that everyone played and bought they decided to use that money to create a completely different game. While this might not be bad it isn't great considering when you purchase an early access game the developers should listen to player feedback and improve upon the game with said feedback. Instead of just working hard to improve the game they had, they decided to just abandon the current game and start from scratch. All this said I understand that unity has limits and they wanted to do a lot more outside of those limits.
TL;DR Rust development team starts with a really cool game with a lot of bugs -> a lot of players buy into said game -> rust development team decides to smother the flame by no longer updating old version of game and starts a new game from scratch -> while people who already bought the game play legacy version more than current version.

Facepunch Studios has a long road in front on them in order to compete with the plethora of games out there that are similar.  Games like DayZ -which spawned Rust- as well as 7 Days to Die, and many others are popping up on Kickstarter and Steam.  Even less graphically intense games such as Minecraft and Lords of Uberdark pose a threat to Facepunch in these first few months.
What is Rust shaping up as? Almost solely PvP.  Player-vs-player is a substantial part of each of the aforementioned titles, but so is player-vs-environment.  This is something the guys at Facepunch need to keep a wary eye on.  One of the greatest hurdles I see in the coming days is their valid need to remove zombies.  Although I do agree that zombies do not have a place in the world of Rust, I feel that a replacement should be ready to fill the void their absense will have created.
Facepunch Studios, just by having the walking dead present from the start (albiet alpha stage), have instituted a sense of PvE in their game which has drawn in players who prefer to band together and survive against the unforgiving environment.  Instead I feel that these cooperative-style players may be abandoned for a mindless free-for-all that is the majority of the current servers.  I have high hopes that the developers will meet the demands of both types of players.  In time, we will see.
