I bought into the hype and purchased Rust in a drunken holiday sale binge. I'd never played any sort of survival/free play game (like DayZ, etc) so the concept alone was new to me. I also did no research or reading on the game so I entered completely blind and dumb. I'd say it took me a good 5 play sessions of 30+ minutes apiece to start getting the hang of things. Figuring out how to even gather resources, the 0th step essentially, took me some time not only because I got KOS'd a couple times but also because resources aren't available everywhere (wood is from trees but it's super super slow/inefficient). Once I found resource spawns, then it took me awhile to realize that crafting is available all the time from a dropdown at the top next to inventory and armor. After that, it's less a survival game and more of a social engineering/navigation game where you are more worried about being killed gathering wood by some random player than zombies or bears. But there is that drive to keep surviging longer each time. I've died a ton, and have only gotten started on a 'base' that might actually survive a day but it's been a blast and it's awesome being able to experience it all as it is developed.

It's rare that a beta, much less an alpha like Rust, is this functional and this much fun. The minimal feature set even seems expansive enough, because what Rust really comes down to is relationships and reputation. At any moment, a meeting with another player can be anything from a friendly greeting, to trading, to cold-blooded murder, to unnoticed stalking. Rust removes the physical limitations between players, and leaves it to them to decide how to interact with each other. It's a regular occurrence that you log in to realize your sleeping body has been murdered, your house raided, and everything but your researched recipes gone.
And as Rust proves, that's all the motivation you need to keep going. Whether out for revenge, justice, new allies, or more efficient and raid-proof building designs, each death reminds all of us why we continue to play a game in such an early stage of development. Where most games would implement skills, saves, or some other kind of safety net for the player's character, Rust forces the player to better themselves instead. Nobody's going to hold your hand; it's actually more likely to be shot than held.
Including the famed Garry of Garry's Mod, the Rust dev team is one of the best I've seen at communicating with its players, be it through general status updates, responding to feedback, or updating the beauty that is the public Trello development board.
Considering the recent disasters of games labeled full releases that reveal themselves to be riddled with bugs, littered with in-game purchases, advertisements, and DLC, and developed by teams that have almost no control over their project, little to no QA testing, and/or no ability to communicate, Rust proves that early access can be one of the most effective ways to develop a title.
I've paid $20 for a game that calls itself Alpha, but honestly, it's already earned every cent of that money. This is how a proper business treats its customers-with honesty and respect. If you can only buy one game in all of 2014, you're reading a review for it right now.

A server with low ping and few players can be fun, especially if people are playing together in groups.  Unfortunately, the game quickly descends into chaos as more players join.  The balance of power is quickly tipped with air-drops and the introduction of C4.  A large number of players are quickly sent back to the Stone Age while a small group will wander with modern weapons, picking off those players trying to rebuild.  If you haven't got endless hours to try and rebuild or there isn't a server reset every few days it is easy to get frutrated.
Any good game has a way of striking a balance, this one does not.
A suggestion to the devs, create levels of advancement.  Once certainly items are found in the game by a certain number of players, set the respawn at a higher level.  Provide something better than a rock, torches, and bandages to players who have to contend with Semi-Automatic weapons and C4.  Otherwise you will have a mass exodus of players. Bears bark likes wolves and taste like chicken. 10/10 would cook bear-chicken meat again.
That aside, the game is really fun in it's current form, and with the redesign on the way and getting closer to completion, it's looking to be a very interesting game! Base design is simple yet extremely useful and allowing for some pretty complex designs, gunplay is a little tricky at times but overall fairly good (most servers I find have insta P250's so not a whole lot of weapon variation in shootouts, but more shootouts in general, leading to a "shoot on sight and take belongings" mentality). Crafting is done in a great way, no needing to arrange recipes, you only need to have the correct amount of materials, and the actual blueprint learned for rarer items to give players some endgame content.
A lot of item variation, which will likely spiral upwards when the new version comes out of redesign, but there are some items and clothes that share models. The art style is simple yet detailed, allowing for a good looking game without sacrificing a lot of performance. The same audio is used for a number of animals, but overall offers some good sounds and is quite useful when listening for gunshots and their origins. The music is a bit repetitive and there is little ambient noise, but it is an early access game after all. For an early access game, very promising. Check out the dev blog and get a good look at the upcoming content as it's looking terrific. Gameplay is smooth, great base customization, and lots of raiding.

Rust is a peculiar game. The best way I can describe it is like if Minecraft had a brief but passionate fling with Fallout 3.
Your first day, as the video helpfully demonstrates, involves running naked around a large, irradiated field, hitting pigs with rocks, to mine their bodies for cloth, blood, fat, and chicken fillets.
You can then plonk down a crude shack and a door, and live in bliss until someone else runs up with some C4 and blows your door off to steal all your precious chicken.
You can then make bigger houses. Huge towering tributes to your own vanity that survey the far reaches of your domain.
The feeling of invunerability is strong at this point, but you're always only so far away from someone blowing the doors off your mansion, and stealing your stuff.
The first time I ever met another player, it was like hostage negotiation, with every move being scrutinised for hostile intent. Happily he just wanted to test his microphone, and gave me cloth trousers for my help.
Later, I gave him a laser sight, and he paid me back by having all his friends kill me and steal my precious chicken resources.
We have a blood feud now.
All in all, I recommend the game, because you will all get stories like this. You might be the aggressor, or you might be the victim, but this game is pretty much a 1:1 simulator of what would happen if you ended society tomorrow.
I would like to see more stuff be implemented in the game, like some sort of discoverable reason for the island to exist, or what happened to make it like that, or your purpose there.
All in all, intriguing and addictive.

Rust is a peculiar game. The best way I can describe it is like if Minecraft had a brief but passionate fling with Fallout 3.
Your first day, as the video helpfully demonstrates, involves running naked around a large, irradiated field, hitting pigs with rocks, to mine their bodies for cloth, blood, fat, and chicken fillets.
You can then plonk down a crude shack and a door, and live in bliss until someone else runs up with some C4 and blows your door off to steal all your precious chicken.
You can then make bigger houses. Huge towering tributes to your own vanity that survey the far reaches of your domain.
The feeling of invunerability is strong at this point, but you're always only so far away from someone blowing the doors off your mansion, and stealing your stuff.
The first time I ever met another player, it was like hostage negotiation, with every move being scrutinised for hostile intent. Happily he just wanted to test his microphone, and gave me cloth trousers for my help.
Later, I gave him a laser sight, and he paid me back by having all his friends kill me and steal my precious chicken resources.
We have a blood feud now.
All in all, I recommend the game, because you will all get stories like this. You might be the aggressor, or you might be the victim, but this game is pretty much a 1:1 simulator of what would happen if you ended society tomorrow.
I would like to see more stuff be implemented in the game, like some sort of discoverable reason for the island to exist, or what happened to make it like that, or your purpose there.
All in all, intriguing and addictive.

"A game of survival"
Well, if your version of survival is surviving a horror movie filled with naked men armed with rocks and assault rifles, then yeah.
But if you look at it from an open world full of interesting perks and an oppurtunity to play with a little bit of wits and a whole lot of challenge, the game is pretty good.
I've discovered most people aren't actually hostile, you've just come across that one guy out of a hundred who saw your torch and said "Mmm....newbie flesh."

So, as some of you may know, I recently purchased the video game, “Rust”, a survival game roughly based on the likes of Minecraft and DayZ. Day 1 I was dropped into the game as a naked caveman (don’t worry, it is censored) with nothing but a rock, torch and flashlight. What could possibly go wrong, right? Well, this is exactly what I thought, until I realized that there were two people with guns and in full armor heading towards me. Without a second thought, they shot me in the face, and I had to start over, not that I had accomplished much.
This is exactly what Rust is. Kill on Sight mayhem, having all your hard-earned supplies stolen from you, dealing with liars and bandits, but despite all the FRUSTRATION and ANGER at the game and other players to begin with, you finally start to get the hang of it. Before long, you’ve crafted your first hatchet, and you’re happily gathering wood, Chicken Breast (which comes from every animal in the game strangely enough), cloth and stone. Eventually, you’ll have a bow and arrow, and are able to defend yourself from zombies and wolves, except at this point, you are still highly fearful of other players, who may have guns.
The game is based in a post-apocalyptic island in the middle of nowhere. The island is MASSIVE, and at any one time there can up to 300 people connected to the game. Walking through the wilderness, for hours on end, not seeing a soul, or even so much as an animal, but yet seeing the ruins of people’s houses that came before you, people that made mistakes and got raided and killed is a very strange, and even eerie feeling. You learn that even though you can become powerful in the game, control all the guns, enslave others, it is a very slippery slope back to being a naked caveman again. Once you have fallen, why would people trust you again, and help you back up?
I honestly don’t know what keeps me drawn to this game, but it draws me like a magnet. The game is incredibly fun long term, but very frustrating short term. Whenever you lose everything, be it from death by a wolf, naked caveman with a gun, or simply starving to death, yes, it’s annoying, yes, it angers you, but you gain experience, which makes bouncing back even easier than before. I had a mansion, but it is now little more than a pile of ashes on the ground thanks to raiders. This sort of thing will make you very angry, however, you have learned not to build near the road.
Lastly, even though you meet people who kill you on sight, the thing that makes me feel really good is when you meet someone, and they don’t kill you, instead they give you a gift, or help you with something. These are the types of players that make the game worthwhile; these are the players that restore your faith in the game, and these are the players that make this game work so flawlessly.

Rust is dynamic, interesting and infuriating in its current state.
I wanted to give it a try as I was a huge fan of the DayZ mod and enjoy survival based games a great deal.
I understand this is an unfinished alpha and because of that I'll come back and play it in the next phase, but as of now here are my initial thoughts on the game.
Without enough things to do to promote strangers to work together, encounters with players will almost always devolve into a death match. I enjoy the crafting mechanics and the concept, but the game in this state is missing vital elements to keep friendly players who want to establish tribes and communities playing. Killing on sight is a huge thing that I see, and most new players who start the game with the intentions of finding friends etc, are quickly converted to the KoS philosophy due to having to deal with it so often.
I don't mind perma-death, killing-on-sight or sleepers as they make for very interesting and dynamic mechanics. What is the most troublesome aspect to this game is that new players cannot compete versus established veteran players. I'm not complaining about being shot by a veteran player. That makes sense that they'll be outgeared, what bothers me is that new players can't establish themselves anywhere. The veterans are so well established and bored that within hours of a new player trying to strategically locate a safe place to build, and gather enough items to "secure it", the vets can just easily break in and steal everything. A new player can't build a large enough base or find a safe enough place to log out because of this.
The last issue is with the technology progression. I adore the primitive weapons, tools, etc. I believe that by adjusting the curve of technology development a lot of the community issues can be solved. Not everyone should be running around in kevlar with assault rifles. I know this is in alpha and we're attempting to test the various weapons and items for bugs etc, but I will absolutely come back when the technology bell curve is adjusted. I think that will solve most of the issues and level the playing field for everyone.
I dream of a RUST with sprawling player built cities and communities on one side and on the other side of the map bandits, looters and mob bosses. Massive raids and neutral wild people. This game has great potential and can be a blast, but in the current state I can't recommend it.
I will definitely check back though and update my thoughts on it in a few months.

Once the next cycle came in game, the three of them had logged off and it was just my friend and I left...Bad news.
We took two C4 charges with us, as that's all we could make at the time, and found their base  again. Instead of trying to blow through the series of doors, crafting more and more C4 and hoping that we were able to get in, I found a structual weak spot that lead us right into their main room. LEGACY REVIEW
Having spent many hours in DayZ kind of filled me with mixed expectations when going into Rust for the first time, but I quickly found it to be an exciting and satisfying game. So far I find the game more akin to Minecraft, in that you need to eat and craft in order to survive: by gathering wood, stones, and metal with a boulder in your hands you're soon able to craft simple tools that makes gathering faster, and soon you'll be able to make yourself a small shelter. You can also harvest materials from hunted animals (including rabbits, deer, wolves and bears [the latter two being hostile]) and scavenge random items from buildings (which may include weapons, weapon parts, and resource materials).
There are also irradiated spots to look out for (indicated by the clicking sound your gauge makes) and different types of zombies to fight, who also drop loot. However I heard that the developer is soon taking out zombies and substituting them with some unknown object/creature, in order to have players more focused on survival.
In comparison to DayZ, players are probably one of the biggest threats in the game: if someone has a pack of C4 on them they likely won't hesitate to blow open the next house they see and mow down anyone inside. With this and the chances of death from zombies or animals high when venturing the wastes, the stakes can be quite high when you find yourself loaded with goodies, raising the tension.
Contrary to DayZ though, your character, inventory, and research progression is unique to each individual server. So if you play with a group of friends on one server you can swap to another and fool around on your own. Just be careful when you play on servers that enable "Sleepers"; on these servers, when you log out, your character 'sleeps' on the ground where you left, and you might log back in later to find yourself dead from an animal or player.
I wouldn't call this a "DayZ killer" or even an imitation of said game. RUST is a unique blend of survival and creative elements, and makes for a very tense but enjoyable multiplayer experience. Heck, even playing on your own on a low pop server can prove challenging. It's still very rough around the edges, both in terms of gameplay and graphics, but there hasn't been anything game-breaking so far.
Highly recommend giving RUST a try

Time for a small edit. I say small because my old review still stands up to the new version of Rust, I'm just going to add some things into it.
First off, ♥♥♥♥ those guys with the negative reviews. They ♥♥♥♥♥ about stupid♥♥♥♥♥♥ or they ♥♥♥♥♥ about the game not being what they wanted, even when it was never what they wanted in the first place and they act like its all the devs fault that they bought a game that they didnt look into first. This game is awesome, and even more so with friends. In fact, you wind up meeting some pretty good friends in this game. You'll have to sift through the massive pile of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s to get to them, but it winds up being worth it.
The games graphics had a gigantic overhaul and it is beautiful. The game looks and feels immersive now. You grow more attached to the world around you, and it truly has a survival feel to it that it didnt have before. Theres more to do, more to see, and more things to discover and it's only going to get better as they add more into the game every week.
Updates. Theyre frequent and wonderful (for the most part). The devs keep everyone up to date on things implemented and things being worked on. Even if you don't play much that week, you can easily stay caught up on how the game is progressing.
The game is really quite awesome. The fact that its already wonderful and it's still only in alpha is impressive in itself. I've not met many games that are as good as this one at the same stage of development. It's much like the lovechild of minecraft and dayz, with a more pvp focus than anything. the whole point is to spawn into a dog-eat-dog world and try to survive. This game will not hold your hand, and neither will the other players. They'll sooner shoot you in the face; ahh, the good old "welcome to Rust- BANG!"
That said, server choice is important. There are a wide spectrum of servers that cater to different needs of different types of players. there are servers out there who wipe frequently, others who try to keep things as long as possible before deciding when to wipe. there are cutthroat servers where you will constantly get shot in the face every 3 minutes. There are noob friendly servers that forces vets to give noobs a chance (but if you aggress, you WILL be shot). There are servers where mods rampantly abuse the system and everyone living in that system. There are servers where the mods, while advancing themselves, are generally kind and helpful towards everyone. There are servers with extremely stringent mods. It will probably take you a day to figure out which kind of server you like. But in the end you will find a place (or more!) to call home.
The players are similar. You will ALWAYS have those donkeys anuses who will kill you every time they run into you, and sometimes going out of their way to find you and kill you. You WILL be raided many times. If you ragequit every time you're raided, this is probably not the game for you. It will be extremely frustrating every time, especially if you're a kind player who tries to not KOS (Kill On Sight) other players. It's all part of the experience. Usually, you'll be able to tell very quickly who's cool and who's dangerous. generally, KOSers don't talk to you on VON (Voice Over Network). they'll try to approach you and shoot you, or shoot from a distance. Usually nicer players will try to identify you and proclaim their alignment. But this varies. Much like life, you have to figure it out from person to person.
The gameplay is actually pretty great. Not perfect, but pretty smooth, and not real glitchy. the controls are fairly intuitive and simple. There is no tutorial in game, so you'll have to ask (and please don't be afraid to!) and figure it all out. getting the resources is the hardest part right of the bat, as not everywhere has them. but once you get started, you pick up steam fast. Join a group, make friends (and enemies if you have to) and have fun! for 20 bucks, this is a great game and it will only get better!

Even though it is still in Alpha, Rust offers a robust environment that allows the player to explore a post-apocolyptic island populated with some passive prey and aggressive predators. The foundation is very solid, with new fixes implemented frequently to continue building towards completion.
The crafting system offers a simplistic approach that utilizes resources gathered from the environment to fashion necessary survival tools, and has room to allow additions to the list through a blueprint or research system.
The game has a gental reminder of almost 40 years of zombie / post apocolyptic / survival genres under its belt.  It currently features a single road that cirlcles a fairly large area of the map, with scattered ruins holding treasures and dangers alike. While there are zombies, wolves, and bears to contend with, the real threats are the other players.
Most servers are player versus player, and this offers a fantastic look at the baser insticts of most gamers. With no real system of punishment, there is nothing to stop a player from randomly killing everyone he meets. You can really tell alot about a person by how they initially react to seeing a new person running down the road towards them.
The soft mechanics of the kill or be killed world lend the upper hand to the agressive player who can kill, without regard, and steal another player's hard work, but this makes the rare alliance between players who are willing to watch each other's back stronger.
The idea of trusting a complete stranger who approaches you, seemingly unarmed, creates more tension than being chased by a bear or zombie. When survival is the game, to allow another player to live can mean less resources for yourself, and possibly your own demise.
I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys survival of the fittest games, and has a masochistic willingness to trust strangers in a world without rules.

Don't rush into spending your money on this game. You have a high risk of getting disappointed, regardless of what you are told about the game. It would be great to start this review from a positive note, though, because the game certainly deserves some positive attention.
First of all, the idea of the game is marvelous. You spawn butt-naked in a barren land and you develop your skills as you play by finding new blueprints and using research kits to study new craftable items. The game has some special mysterious ambience which is pretty addictive. It's really exciting to walk around a huge map (it's 1/30/2014 now, and currenly only a tiny part of the map is available but it's still decent-sized). This game shows what any society is really like. People naturally are greedy and dangerous. Some people start practicing slavery in this game. Others just derive pleasure from killing people who can't defend themselves. A lot of experienced players kill other players who just spawned and only began gathering stuff because experienced players simply want to rob them. They even coined a special term for those unfortunate guys who just happened to join the game--"harvesters". Get killed like that a couple of times and you will suddenly figure out that it's best to stay away from other players before you have any decent weapon to defend yourself. It's best not to use torches at night and to try to avoid groups of other players. That survival is the main excitement about this game.
Now about bad things. If there was a way to get a refund, I would certainly want to get it. The reasons for that are the following:
Cheaters. Some people call them "hackers". That's a real misnomer. Those guys are simply cheaters. They buy cheating software (ads for which are right on the official site of Rust. Ridiculous, huh?) Moreover, cheating became so widespread that  now a lot of players don't even buy that software, they download it from torrents. Mainly, if you walk in a densely populated part of the map, your chances to meet a cheater are about 90% if you stay there for at least 20 minutes. Be prepared to lose all your stuff that you were gathering for long hours to a cheater who can fly, see everything in the darkness, use a radar, and do many many other things that spoils the game for other players. It is quite funny to see several people on forums to claim that it is only an Alpha which is why such things should be expected. Ironically, after playing Rust for some decent time, I memorized nicknames of people who cheat on several official servers and I found them on forums saying in a quite abusive language that cheating should be expected since it is an Alpha version. I would say that a really rare game goes to this point of cheating. Frankly, I have never seen such level of cheating before. It is "ok" when you get killed by some cheater in CS, COD, Arma2, etc because there you don't lose work of several days. But in Rust, it will cause you a lot of frustration to see how one dude kills your entire group and destroys everything you have while flying in the air and yelling something immature at you. What's worse is that the developers do barely anything about cheating. They fixed several exploits in January but since then the number of cheaters only increased, that is to say the measures that are being taken against cheaters are inadequate and aren't enough to fight them.
You still have a chance to be lucky not to meet a cheater, then you would be among 5% of the lucky players. But I guarantee you, dear anonymous reader, that you are among 95% and you will be owned by cheaters on a regular basis.
I don't see other serious problems with a game. It surely needs some polishing because it is an Alpha version. Some things are even funny, like when you see that a bear barks like a dog. But cheating goes to such a crazy extent that this game becomes completely unplayable. That is the reason why I wouldn't recommend anyone to buy this game now. I hope the developers do something about the extent of cheating soon, so then the game would be a lot more enjoyable than it is now.

This game is one of the most brutal PvP games I've ever had the chance to play. I played DayZ when it was starting and growing as an Arma2 mod, and that was fine and dandy, but this game takes the cake. The crafting system is more of what DayZ needs, and with the plentiful expansions that will be coming in future weeks and months, this game is shaping up to be the essence of an "MMO" survival game. The server size is just right for the size of the map, guns feel rightly powerful for everything you go through to make them (or take them) and building a house in a game has never made me struggle to use supplies sparingly as much as Rust does.
The one complaint I have currently is the amount of cheaters present in game, but I can honestly say that those that I've had the displeasure of meeting and reporting (along with a gorup of reports from friends) haven't been seen again.
Last thing, play it with friends. Coax them into playing it with you, none of you will regret it so long as you help each other out. The map is nowhere near as absurdly huge or barren as Chernarus in DayZ, finding your friends won't be extremely difficult, and there is definite strength in numbers. Watching a group of seven people in full armor chasing after you with bows and arrows, pistols, and rifles is probably a frightening sight, as I've never been on the other side of it, but it's better to be wielding the guns, yeah?
Overall, great as far as Early Access goes, some laggy rubberbanding that should be ironed out in the coming weeks, but not a bad investment in the slightest. Looking forward to more house raiding and looting in the future.

It's night....footsteps outside.... "who's there?".... an axe hits your door.  Paranoia sets in as the door will slowly, but surely be busted before the sunrise.  A rock is your ownly hope.   This is the basic newb experience (for those able to establish shelter).
Being an ALPHA state, the game doesn't do well to explain many things right out the gate.   So expect no tutorial at all.   There's no explaination to food, to what the rocks look like, or to obtaining wood.    This is stuff that newbs have to constantly ask in chat for assistance with.
Some of the basic spawn points are broken in a sort of way.   The "broken" ones would be those that set a player right in a RAD zone or right next to zombie/mutant areas.   The other spawns in the middle of open fields, roads, and so forth aren't so bad.
The game itself is not the game, but the psychological thriller experienced by the players.   Sociopaths  run rampent with the ability to torment as many as they please.   People try to band together, distrust everyone, try to befriend the unfriendly, and so much more.   It's crazy the kind of mind games that this game sets up throughout it's play time.
In a most notable negative for the game right now, there must be mention of how many guns there are and how easily they are obtained.   After a short period of time, it becomes just another standard FPS game instead of a true survivor game.    Bows become almost useless to the rifle and P250.    Crafting an axe is good only for gathering because it will be a 1 in a million chance of actually killing someone with half a brain and isn't away from keyboard.
Overall the game is fun with friends, but becomes a frustration without anyone to play with.  So, bring them.   Also, if you have a heart condition at all, do NOT play this game.

I purchased the game in high anticipation only to be drawn into grave disappointment.  This game supports an underculture where the murder and deciet of player characters in a PvP setting flourishes, which makes it difficult for new players to dive into the crafting aspects of the game.  It's not unusual for a new player to arrive upon a new world only to be sniped down within mere seconds by a high-powered rifle before one can learn anything about the controls to the game.  If one can survive the first few hours, they will begin the arduous journey of scavenging for scarce resources...and I mean scarce.  One can search a long time before finding animals to hunt (which I also found to be a joke), or natural materials for crafting which can often lead to frustration.  I also found the world to be more a littered junk yard as shacks left behind by other players dot the landscape.
Now this does take place in a post-apocalyptic setting so the scarcity of resources, and to some extent the behavior of the player characters may be in line to what can be expected in such a setting.  But this game seems more focused on PvP than world building as keyboard commandos continually scour the landscape gunning down one another and stealing their resources....even victimizing new players as they spawn into the world through coercion or deciet.  All this given, that wasn't the deal breaker.
What really irked me the most was spending hours scavenging resources, logging off, then returning only to find everything I've worked for missing from my character.  I don't mean those kept in inventory stored in boxes on the world....those are always subject to be looted by bandits....no, I mean stuff literally kept on the player character itself....food, weapons, armor, medical supplies..... and this happened more than a handful of times.
In conclusion, the game is big on promise but short on delivery for gamers who look for character and world building and customization....and you won't be guaranteed you'll keep what you work for. PvPers might find it appealing if you can keep from getting ganked long enough to learn anything about the game.  No, this game is a huge disappointment and not worth the money spent on it.

Game is good if you count the fact away that most time you meet other players you will be shot in sight even if you are not geared with anything else except a rock,torch and few medkits. Expect to fight many animals , players zombies etc. Build your house well and expect to be raided.

In a word...  sleeper.  This means that when you log off, you don't "log off"...  your character simply stands where he was and closes his eyes.  Until you log back in.  Yes, this means you can and will be found and murdered for your dozen stones and your stone hatchet.  So, essentially, you get to start over daily.  "But you can build a shelter!" you might think.  This is true.  However, they can be brought down, your character killed, and your one measley box completely looted.  Then they destroy your sleeping bag so you can't even find your barren house.
There are also a wide variety of server issues that plague this game.  Official servers only hold 128 simultaneous players, aside from the stress servers and East Coast 1.  This means when you want to get back onto a server you were on, you get to try to reconnect over and over and over.  Stability!  The first two times I played Rust the servers crashed.  The very first time it was, literally, within 10 minutes.  And about 3 of that was spent rubberbanding all over the place.  When the servers are stable the game plays well enough...  but inevitably you'll face lag, and eventually a server crash.
And speaking of servers, if you want to refresh the list of 11 official servers you also get to sit through the list of the 300odd privately run mod servers to refresh.  "No big deal, the official ones should refresh first," you're saying to yourself.  Of course!  That makes sense in an ideal world.  But if you couldn't tell yet, this is anything but.
This game has SO much potential and I would love it if they actually implemented common sense in addition to the server stability (the latter of which I know will come with time).
Oh!  Not to mention the devs HATE feedback if your opinion differs from theirs at all.

It's a early alpha game, not much to say.  The "What the developer says" section tells nothing about what's going on.  Basically in game you have two materials to build stuff with, wood and steel, that's it.  The graphics are very muddy at best with trees clipping to see through things, the creation system is unintuitive at best with only basic thing to make, even with schematics it seems like I've seen it all.  Playing this without a friend is simply dreadful, while the community is a little bit better than Infestation's and DayZs you're still killed left and right until you find some real armor, or any armor.  Guns even things out as people aren't as willing to shoot a armed person, after that it's basically a grind for more resources, get to base, build, then stare down the occasional passerby.  Overall the game needs a lot of work, but as it's P2P at twenty dollars I'm going to judge it as is, early access titles shouldn't be happening often unless it's in a open beta stage at best.  If you want a minecrafty survival game, you found it.  Minecraft still has bugs so the jump shouldn't be too hard for people.  Later on if they add character customizations and much much more it will improve, but right now I say hold your money, alocate it to something more polished until a later date.

Well, starting off I really want to like this game....I really do. I realize that it's in alpha and given the people behind it Rust should eventually get a lot more playable.
But in it's current state I say get into it only if you really have the patience, even with the best rig and all of the non-essential settings turned off (Clouds, grass, shadows, etc) the game still stutters and lags even when GPU usage is only 30%, that's an obvious optimization issue, which is expected.
The other issue (If you play on a PvP server) is you WILL die, you WILL get your stuff stolen, you WILL have your base blown up, you WILL have people destroy your doors and put up one of their own with a lock, and this will happen A LOT.
This also does not include the ongoing problem with hackers, which seems more common on the official servers than the community hosted ones, and sure VAC does ban some people but it's not enough to prevent even ONE person from ruining a server for everyone.
Now, all of that having been said the premise of the game is solid. Think of it like a more brutal minecraft with PvP, you start off with a rock, a health kit, and a torch.
And from there you'll need to find materials/food to keep yourself alive, among your threats: Animals, Zombies, Radiation, Starvation, and of course other players.
When the game is properly optimized this will look REALLY good, just struggling with the game in max settings in it's current state looks really nice compared to other games in this genre, just not very good in the performance department.
If you already have something like Minecraft, Starbound, Terraria, etc then you probably won't find much that sets Rust apart from all of the other games, but definitely keep an eye out for updates!
Do I recommend it? Yeah, just come into it with your expectations low and play the game for what it is, a game in alpha.
A bit like DayZ, just a whole lot less realistic. Quite user friendly and a whole ton of fun when you make a massive base with all your mates.

This... game... is... AMAZING. However, protecting from raiders is hard considering that you can get raided at any time, no matter what. Given that the server is up, obviously.
Rust is a do-what-ever-the-freak-you-want kind of game. You can be all stealthy and stalk out your next raid victim for days and gather as much information about his base and friends as possible, how they act, and etc., or you could just charge in with a rock and go bash on their door until they eventually kill you. In Rust, there are no limits. Well, unless you count those people (aka ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s) who kill you for no reason whatsoever. And, unfortunately, you will run into a lot of those kinds of people. Oh, I don't think you understand what I'm saying here; I mean A LOT. However, there are also a lot of friendly people, but no matter what server you're on, unless it doesn't have PvP, you WILL get killed and raided. There is simply no stopping that.
Basically how Rust goes is that you gather materials, make a temporary shelter, gather more materials, make a more advanced structure, gather more materials, make an even MORE advanced structure, etc etc. If you're like me, you'll most likely just get the the 2nd "stage" of your shelter-ness and then get raided, having to restart from the beginning. But, in Rust, if something happens to you or any of your belongings, you have nobody to blame except yourself. If you put your house out in the open, your fault. If you forgot to put down a metal door (or any door at all), your fault. You didn't have enough defenses? Your fault. I love that aspect. Everything relies solely on the player.
TO SUM IT UP... get Rust. Like, now. I'm waiting... you get it yet? Okay, well I hope you did. This game is so much fun and I can't stop playing it. Great concept, but skeptical considering its an indie developer. Its hard to be invested in this game. I've had my hopes crushed on games with much more progress at this stage of development. I think for its genre its probably one of the better ideas out there. I've never been a big fan of survival games. I was hoping to find one that changes the trend of them. I'm curious if the developers are qualified enough and have the financial backing to make the engine into a stable, fully functional game. As of right now? I wouldn't recommend purchasing the game in hopes that you're going to get much more than a shell. IT IS ALPHA. I would purchase the game under the idea that you're supporting the company's path they plan to take.
For me, personally? I have my own list of concerns granted its engine and the natural problems that come with making persistent world games through it. First and foremost being the onslaught of hackers. That will be what makes or breaks this game if they can manage to figure out their desync problems and stability issues. There needs to be some more features out there because the content isn't there to really sustain a sandbox game, long term.
I am only recommending this game because I have friends who absolutely love it. If it wasn't for their testimony and their passion for it, I would encourage people to stay away. All in all, I'm 50/50 at this point. Only time will tell if this game is or isn't a complete waste of money.

My first night in Rust:
I spawned and was soon killed by a zombie. My second life was a bit more fruitful, I learned to sneak up on deer and bash them with my rock. With their hides I made a bow and with the wood and stone I found I made some arrows.
When gathering wood, I ran across another player. "friendly?" he typed in chat, and I attempted to speak into my mic (didn't know about the voice button yet). Seemingly frustrated with my lack of a response, he began axing me in the face with his hatchet. I escaped with only 8 health to his cries of "RUN! RUN! DON'T COME BACK." It was  now getting dark and I was getting hungry, so I built a campfire and attempted to cook the meat I had harvested. One mis-click later and I was accidentally chowing down on some raw chicken breast. I'm still happier having died to salmonella than to the crazed axe-man.
Third spawn, I was intent on getting my bearings and the lay of the land. Looking up a map online and identifying two landmarks in game helped a great deal, and it didn't take me long at all to figure out where everything was and what zone of the map I was in at the time. Just as I had figured out where I was, night began to fall and I heard "OHMYGOD ANOTHER PERSON HELPMEPLEASE!" The naked caveman was starving, so I shared my cooked chicken with him and we made a campfire for the night, attracting another friendly soul who was searching for zombies to kill. The zombie hunter left at first light to continue his search, but the hungry guy and I grouped up in order to find a spot to settle.
We searched for a good spot, but all the really good spots were already taken. We picked up another ally, and this guy actually had a 9mm pistol! The three of us set out to the cliffs in between the valleys in order to find a good defensible position. Looking down into a valley, my friend spied another naked individual, and decided we should try to make contact with him. This guy was crazy. He immediately began screaming that he was chief to his "people," who needed help, and we must follow him. Against my better judgement, our party of three followed the chief through the cliffs to his camp.
The chief dubbed me Legolas due to the bow I was wielding, and my companions Gimli and... "the other guy." The role of Aragorn, the chief took for himself. But our fellowship was to be short-lived, as upon arriving at the chief's camp we came across a VERY angry individual with full body armour and an M4 assault rifle, screaming at chief and his people. My arrow wasn't even notched before I was gunned down.
That wasn't the end of the night, as it included some blueprints, another crazy guy with a shotgun, a uniformed squad gunning me down on sight, and culminated in the completion of my first shack (with a ceiling and everything!). When I finished off my shack, I made a sleeping back and went to bed. Tomorrow: Resource gathering and building the shack into a respectable home. This game rocks.

Please skip to the conclusion for the TL;DR on this game.
First and foremost: I've written one of these sort of reviews before
and if you aren't familiar with the format, it's designed for Early Access games, and to be as unbiased as possible.  I absolutely love this game, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have
flaws people will notice.
-
* Very Stranded-like gameplay that slightly differs from the other PvP survival games out there.
* Some very interesting sociological development takes place if players respect each other enough not to kill on sight without reason.  e.g. cities are built, factions are founded, wars are had.  Pretty intriguing stuff if you find the right server.
* Many possibilities for the design of your home, from immense towers and colossal fortresses to a simple shack in the woods.
* Decent graphics even on the minimum settings.
* My HP Pavilion can run it with decent FPS before overheating a few hours later because it's an HP and HPs are terrible.
* A decent selection of weapons to choose from to fit your playstyle.
* Pretty frequent updates - We're talking every other day here.
-
* Not too much character customization, which leaves you scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you see someone running up and can't tell if they're your buddy back from the woods or that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the M4 murdering everyone in the valley.
* The "survival" stats like temperature and hunger don't even phase you late game when you have full kevlar and an entire chest of food.
* Being chased by zombies feels more like being chased by a pack of dogs then a pack of infectious undead.  They're neither dangerous nor useful to the player.
* JESUS CHRISTMAS ARE THERE HACKERS.  Hackers everywhere.  You
need to find a server with active admins and good anti-cheat mods to prevent being destroyed by a flying naked guy with a rock screaming racial slurs at everyone.
* Limited modding support - Right now only a simple Lua mod that outputs to the chat box without its own GUI is possible
* Repetitive at times - There's only so much do to in an alpha.
* Somewhat buggy - Not too buggy for an alpha, but buggy nevertheless.
-
* Let's face it: It's a DayZ clone.  Just like any other DayZ clone, there are bound to be players who kill every single person in sight without hesitation.  It's hard to have fun on a server with PvP enabled.
* ♥♥♥♥♥y community - I mean, come on, what did you expect?  Every game like it has a similar community.  It's all about finding the right server.
In conclusion, I don't recommend this game if you're looking for a lot of content, nor do I recommend it if you want to be able to have entire cities working together on a server where PvP is still enabled.  You can't eat your cake and have it, too.  That being said, it has its charm.  It's made its mark in the gaming community as its own multiplayer survival game.  Even though there weren't a lot of points in the "ugly" section, you must consider them when deciding whether to buy this game or not.  If you're trying to decide between this and DayZ, I suggest giving
a spin.  This review goes a lot more indepth than mine, and it's plenty more unbiased.

Rust is a do-what-ever-the-freak-you-want kind of game. You can be all stealthy and stalk out your next raid victim for days and gather as much information about his base and friends as possible, how they act, and etc., or you could just charge in with a rock and go bash on their door until they eventually kill you. In Rust, there are no limits. Well, unless you count those people (aka ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s) who kill you for no reason whatsoever. And, unfortunately, you will run into a lot of those kinds of people. Oh, I don't think you understand what I'm saying here; I mean A LOT. However, there are also a lot of friendly people, but no matter what server you're on, unless it doesn't have PvP, you WILL get killed and raided. There is simply no stopping that.
Basically how Rust goes is that you gather materials, make a temporary shelter, gather more materials, make a more advanced structure, gather more materials, make an even MORE advanced structure, etc etc. If you're like me, you'll most likely just get the the 2nd "stage" of your shelter-ness and then get raided, having to restart from the beginning. But, in Rust, if something happens to you or any of your belongings, you have nobody to blame except yourself. If you put your house out in the open, your fault. If you forgot to put down a metal door (or any door at all), your fault. You didn't have enough defenses? Your fault. I love that aspect. Everything relies solely on the player.

Okay, let’s get this out of the way from the very beginning; this game is in its alpha phase; the graphics are lacking; there are bugs (none of which are game breaking); there are several improvements which can be made. I’m not going into any more detail on these sections as they are thing I expect to be fixed as the game develops and progresses.
The game itself is addictive in its simplicity, yet impressive it its thoroughness; from gathering materials to crafting, and from NPC’s to game mechanics. You start off as a squishy bloke with a rock, and can become king of a twenty story high tower, donning Kevlar and wielding an M4.
You can choose to be a good guy, helping those in need and protecting the weak; or a bad guy, taking the shortcut past resource farming by simply killing another player and taking their items or assaulting someone’s base and taking it as your own.
Personally, I’m a good guy; I’ll help those I think are in need of it and I’ll trust those I think are worthy of it. I’ll band together a group of similarly minded players and together we’ll defend others and seek revenge on the bandits (aka ‘bad guys’, aka ‘PK’ers’, aka [Expletive Deleted]).
As a good guy, I can sympathise with how frustrating and annoying it can be to be killed and your hard earned items and resources to be stolen, however there are ways to combat this; regularly depositing your items in a secure location, or avoiding running around alone, especially with your best items equipped.
My favourite tactic is to play during antisocial hours. Playing on a fairly low populated server and occasionally working nights means I can get away with logging in at 2am, farming all the resources to my heart’s content, without having to worry too much about the other two players online at that time.
Yes, there is a chance you’ll run into them, but the map is so vast it is highly unlikely. However, I would not recommend playing like this always – it’s lonely, it can get boring and it totally overrides the point of the game.
There is one positive aspect about never knowing whether that figure in the distance is a zombie waiting to eat your brain, or a player lining up a headshot on you; adrenaline.
I have never played a game which can actually make my heart rate increase but when you’ve just spent an hour gathering hundreds of resources, the sound of a single gunshot causes my heart to try and escape my chest as I begin sprinting frantically back to base, zigzagging to avoid potential enemy fire.
Yes, the likelihood is that it’s another player, far off in the distance, defending themselves from aforementioned brain chomping zombies, or killing an animal, but can you really take that risk? All that effort, all that gear, just gone.
If you say “yes I can”, then I challenge you to actually play the game – spend an hour gathering resources and then see how long you can stroll around without a care in the world, as your tension and paranoia builds, causing you to direct your attention to the sound of any possible footsteps. Let’s see how long you can avoid sprinting back to base. You might do it once, maybe twice, but it gets harder to do so each time you’re killed.
What I will say is that if you’re prone to sudden fits of rage, or are of a nervous disposition, don’t get this game; you’ll either end up having a heart attack, having a visit from the police for a public disturbance report after screaming profanities through your monitor at some PK’er, or throw your computer out the window.
If, on the other hand, you enjoy the un-predictive nature that is Man, then you’ll love this. With clever mechanics such as decay, status de-buffs such as ‘cold’, ‘hunger’, or ‘poisoned’, and the undertones of the hybrid offspring from one wild night of passion between an RPG and SimCity, there are a lot of aspects which can appeal to different players for different reasons.
And don’t be pessimistic about the fact that it’s in its alpha phase because once you start playing and get into it, it’s likely you’ll think to yourself ‘if this is what it’s like in alpha, I can wait to see what it’s like when complete!”.

Rating 8-10
First off, this is an alpha release, keep that in mind the game is not complete, but they do patch about once every week or so. This game is like an FPS in a few important ways. There are hackers; however they are mostly on the official servers. Servers that are not in the official list are run by a person or set of people, and they tend to take liberties with what they give or do for themselves. You are also in a first person perspective. That pretty much takes care of why this game is like an FPS, and the admins +hackers are why I remove 2 points.
When this game says survival, there is something important you need to know. The survival in this game is against people! This game through and through is about PvPvP. Yes there are animals, zombies, radiation, and hunger, but these serve to carve out the world that the player interactions take place in. “Interactions you say, but I thought you said this was all about player killing player?” No, it is not all about killing and this is what makes rust amazing. I have had people help, kill, rob, and backstab me.  I have witnessed mob mentality take a group of 10 guys with rocks and turn them into murders knocking down shacks and murdering the inhabitants. The interactions in this game are truly awesome.
Do I put my gun away? Risk of him getting the first shot vs him knowing I have a gun and wanting to kill me.  Am I wearing armor? Does that say too much about what I have on me? Is he responding to me? Maybe he is not talking because he plans to kill me.
All of those fragmented thoughts run through my head every time I meet someone. Understand another warning however. V is for using a mic, if you don’t have one, most people will kill you before you can type a word in edge wise. This game is to high risk for typing to be anything other than a novelty or way to talk to everyone across the map. Another Warning, personal space is big. Get too close and you might get shot. Let them come close and you will find yourself getting shot/stabbed. Keep a good 10-15 foot personal space barrier. Demand people put their weapon down. 100’s of hours of playing teaches you these things that you might not think of when you’re in the moment for the first time with 60 wood, 30 metal ore and a hatchet or something else nice. If you keep a good distance you can also get away with not having a gun or weapon out, as a press of 1-6 could bring your shotgun out to deal with an over eager kid treading in your personal bubble.
Overall I love this game, and foresee many more an hour spent enjoying never knowing if this guy is going to work with me to get resources, or murder me for them...
Or perhaps I will murder him..?...

My first night in Rust:
I spawned and was soon killed by a zombie. My second life was a bit more fruitful, I learned to sneak up on deer and bash them with my rock. With their hides I made a bow and with the wood and stone I found I made some arrows.
When gathering wood, I ran across another player. "friendly?" he typed in chat, and I attempted to speak into my mic (didn't know about the voice button yet). Seemingly frustrated with my lack of a response, he began axing me in the face with his hatchet. I escaped with only 8 health to his cries of "RUN! RUN! DON'T COME BACK." It was  now getting dark and I was getting hungry, so I built a campfire and attempted to cook the meat I had harvested. One mis-click later and I was accidentally chowing down on some raw chicken breast. I'm still happier having died to salmonella than to the crazed axe-man.
Third spawn, I was intent on getting my bearings and the lay of the land. Looking up a map online and identifying two landmarks in game helped a great deal, and it didn't take me long at all to figure out where everything was and what zone of the map I was in at the time. Just as I had figured out where I was, night began to fall and I heard "OHMYGOD ANOTHER PERSON HELPMEPLEASE!" The naked caveman was starving, so I shared my cooked chicken with him and we made a campfire for the night, attracting another friendly soul who was searching for zombies to kill. The zombie hunter left at first light to continue his search, but the hungry guy and I grouped up in order to find a spot to settle.
We searched for a good spot, but all the really good spots were already taken. We picked up another ally, and this guy actually had a 9mm pistol! The three of us set out to the cliffs in between the valleys in order to find a good defensible position. Looking down into a valley, my friend spied another naked individual, and decided we should try to make contact with him. This guy was crazy. He immediately began screaming that he was chief to his "people," who needed help, and we must follow him. Against my better judgement, our party of three followed the chief through the cliffs to his camp.
The chief dubbed me Legolas due to the bow I was wielding, and my companions Gimli and... "the other guy." The role of Aragorn, the chief took for himself. But our fellowship was to be short-lived, as upon arriving at the chief's camp we came across a VERY angry individual with full body armour and an M4 assault rifle, screaming at chief and his people. My arrow wasn't even notched before I was gunned down.
That wasn't the end of the night, as it included some blueprints, another crazy guy with a shotgun, a uniformed squad gunning me down on sight, and culminated in the completion of my first shack (with a ceiling and everything!). When I finished off my shack, I made a sleeping back and went to bed. Tomorrow: Resource gathering and building the shack into a respectable home. This game rocks.

This game is only at it's alpha stage and is only 20 dollars! It is well worth the money because this game already is pretty amazing! In the sense of if you like the idea of minecraft, but hate the idea of being in a pixelated world then yeah you will love this game!

If you're looking for a a friendly "build a town and survive with friends/strangers" type game like Minecraft, this isn't for you Not yet anyway. 99% of the players are Hostile, regardless if you're a fresh spawn. Infact if you are, you're MORE likely to die at the hands of someone in full Kelvar with a M4 Yes thats the Goal for most people Hunting. New. Players.
Or you get people who live for nothing more then to wait for you to log out, or go get supplies then blow up half your house, or build around it blocking you from getting back in.
Half the time even Fresh spawns are hostile, you'll log in to go Collect from a pile of wood that no one is around only to be smacked and then chased by another player with a rock/hatchet why? You where taking that wood pile. No Voice-Communication through the in-game Voice Chat, No typed message asking you to back up or share. Just. DEATH.
There's a HUGE gap in weapons and hostile creatures. You'll first find yourself hitting boars with your rock, to finally make a bow, with which you can finally take down those zombies. But whats that on his corpse? A GUN blueprint. Yes there's ZERO middle-ground weapons No spears, axes, swords, daggers, cross-bows Nothing. Within a hour of starting you can go from using a Rock, to a Bow and arrow Straight to a fully functional M4, Pistol, shotgun or Mp5. It's not even worth trying to go after zombies, wolfs or bears until you get the Bow or a Gun, They'll destroy you.
Hitting trees is more or less pointless, You'll get 1 wood per hit, and only get about 10 wood before the tree has to "regen" it's wood, Resources don't spawn properly ( All across the map, theres alot of areas where there are no Animals, piles of wood, or rocks ) Every Animal drops Chick breasts, theres only health,Hunger and raidiation in game at the moment, which after you get a bow and start hunting you'll never have to worry about hunger and as long as you avoid raidiation areas you'll never have to worry about that ( as of now ) Thirst isn't put in yet, Being Cold doesn't seem to have any real effect at the moment.
There is a Anti-Cheat program that keeps "most" of the hackers at bay but until it's release people will always find a way.
The first 2-3 hours of the game are fun if you can get past the constant dying/respawning and most of the Admin abuse, but the Main downfall of this game is how hostile everyone is, even on the Non-PvP ( the servers being hosted by people who WANT to build/play together instead of constantly shooting each other ) there's people who Do all of the above. Unless you're lucky enough to find that one server with Active Admins/Mods who don't abuse their power and keep players like that in check. Even with all the bad players there are those people who make it worth it, those who see you're new or struggling and actually give you a hatchet, a sleeping bag or even food and help you get started they Give you a chance to actually survive.
All in all, in my opinion it boils down to a Numbers game. If you have a few friends that can play with you on a active basis, you'll find yourself either defending the weak and fighting off the majority of the other players on the server you're building on, or you'll find yourself hunting down those fresh spawn like game. If you don't have friends to play with, I would wait on picking this up it. When they've had time to adjust everything and hopefully bridge the huge gap in weapons and enemies and maybe make more Friendly servers to start out on.

If you're looking for a a friendly "build a town and survive with friends/strangers" type game like Minecraft, this isn't for you Not yet anyway. 99% of the players are Hostile, regardless if you're a fresh spawn. Infact if you are, you're MORE likely to die at the hands of someone in full Kelvar with a M4 Yes thats the Goal for most people Hunting. New. Players.
Or you get people who live for nothing more then to wait for you to log out, or go get supplies then blow up half your house, or build around it blocking you from getting back in.
Half the time even Fresh spawns are hostile, you'll log in to go Collect from a pile of wood that no one is around only to be smacked and then chased by another player with a rock/hatchet why? You where taking that wood pile. No Voice-Communication through the in-game Voice Chat, No typed message asking you to back up or share. Just. DEATH.
There's a HUGE gap in weapons and hostile creatures. You'll first find yourself hitting boars with your rock, to finally make a bow, with which you can finally take down those zombies. But whats that on his corpse? A GUN blueprint. Yes there's ZERO middle-ground weapons No spears, axes, swords, daggers, cross-bows Nothing. Within a hour of starting you can go from using a Rock, to a Bow and arrow Straight to a fully functional M4, Pistol, shotgun or Mp5. It's not even worth trying to go after zombies, wolfs or bears until you get the Bow or a Gun, They'll destroy you.
Hitting trees is more or less pointless, You'll get 1 wood per hit, and only get about 10 wood before the tree has to "regen" it's wood, Resources don't spawn properly ( All across the map, theres alot of areas where there are no Animals, piles of wood, or rocks ) Every Animal drops Chick breasts, theres only health,Hunger and raidiation in game at the moment, which after you get a bow and start hunting you'll never have to worry about hunger and as long as you avoid raidiation areas you'll never have to worry about that ( as of now ) Thirst isn't put in yet, Being Cold doesn't seem to have any real effect at the moment.
There is a Anti-Cheat program that keeps "most" of the hackers at bay but until it's release people will always find a way.
The first 2-3 hours of the game are fun if you can get past the constant dying/respawning and most of the Admin abuse, but the Main downfall of this game is how hostile everyone is, even on the Non-PvP ( the servers being hosted by people who WANT to build/play together instead of constantly shooting each other ) there's people who Do all of the above. Unless you're lucky enough to find that one server with Active Admins/Mods who don't abuse their power and keep players like that in check. Even with all the bad players there are those people who make it worth it, those who see you're new or struggling and actually give you a hatchet, a sleeping bag or even food and help you get started they Give you a chance to actually survive.
All in all, in my opinion it boils down to a Numbers game. If you have a few friends that can play with you on a active basis, you'll find yourself either defending the weak and fighting off the majority of the other players on the server you're building on, or you'll find yourself hunting down those fresh spawn like game. If you don't have friends to play with, I would wait on picking this up it. When they've had time to adjust everything and hopefully bridge the huge gap in weapons and enemies and maybe make more Friendly servers to start out on.

All I can say: great game. First off, this game is basically a simulation of what it would be like if you were put out in the middle of nowhere. Except you have no clothes, material, or food. All you get is a rock. And add zombies just to make things interesting. Preferably, I like to join smaller-medium sized servers (15-20 people), just because the risk of dying from another player is low. In my first three runs at the game, I was killed from falling off a cliff, getting mauled by a wolf, and eaten by a zombie. After that I learned to avoid these vicious natural disasters, but soon I died from hunger as I could not catch a deer. However, on my 5th try at the game I successful killed my first animal, built a shelter and fire, and began harvesting material at an exponential rate. Now, many hours in, the bears and wolfs run away from me. The zombies flee to the radiation zones to avoid me. And heights? Well they still killed me once more. But besides that, I feel like a man of the wild.
There was a day and age when I murdered anyone I saw on sight. But I soon realized that Rust was more than slaughtering your fellow mates. Instead of murdering them, I helped them. I gave them wood, shelter, fire, food. And behold, they gave me stuff back too. In fact, I got my first m4 from a guy that I met down the road. I lived peacefully in the mountains, harvesting wood and metal to make my skytower. I had suffiicient food and fire to last for days. I had shotguns, machine guns, pistols, axes, and explosive charges all at the ready. Why? I feared a dreadful day would come and those in the wild would invade my home.
And I was right.
It was a calm afternoon when the attacks first took place. Out in the fields, fifty or sixty yards from my front barricade, a group of 3 men were roaming. I put out my fire too late. They had noticed the smoke and flames and ventured up to the guarding barrier. "What do you want!?" I yelled down to them, overlooking them from the second story of my building. They did not respond. Instead, they began climbing the rocks to the side of the barrier, and within ten seconds they were over the wall. They ventured up to the wooden spikes that protruded outward and hurt anyone that touched them. "Please go away!" I told them, but they insisted on moving foward. Against my knowledge, one of them held an F1 Grenade, and BOOM! my spiked barrier was done with.
I did not hesitate to shoot. As soon as the second barrier was cleared, I whipped out my m4 and blasted away. Like ants, the three invaders scattered behind whatever they could find. They were out of sight. Unknowingly, they snuck behind my house to the back enterance; the only door in my house made of wood, not metal. Luckily, I was only on the second floor and heard them axing away at my door. I sprinted downstairs and took out my shotgun, and perched myself right on the otherside of the door.
E- that is the button to open the door. As soon as I pushed E I fired my shotgun rounds. BAM! BAM! BAM! BAM! It only took four shots to kill the threesome. I quickly rebuilt the door out of metal, and then went on the offensive.
Their camp was only a few clicks south of my house, and by late morning I had arrived. I had struck at the perfect time. It appeared as if the threesome were offline. With my superior pick axe, I mowed down their front door. Like the grinch, I stole everything they had to offer (most of it was stuff they had stolen from me). They had immense ammounts of metal and wood and gunpowder, which would all eventually contribute to the war effort. As quickly as I had raided their house, I was quicker to leave. Fleeing back to my house to make the nesscarry defenses. I knew they would come back.
A few hours later, around late afternoon, the party game back to attack. I had not had the neccessary time nor resources to restablish my front barrier, but I had managed to fix my spiked wall. Not having a grenade, the three person party sought another way to the enterance of my house. Unable to find an alternate route, they were forced to change there approach. Instead of going around the barrier, why not go over? Behold, they built a small ramp that they could get high enough to jump over the spikes. Because of the spike's nature, the ramp and jump were a one way trip.
Foolish boys, I thought, as they sprinted toward my front door. I would be able to quickly gun them down, especially with the extra ammunition from the earlier raid. My predicitions were correct. My m4 tore down two of them relatively quickly, and the third barely reached the door when I shot him in the head. Another successful battle. I went outside to harvest their goods and recover all resources from their dead bodies. Afterward I went back inside and fell asleep, feeling rather safe tonight. Boy was I wrong.
I had made a serious mistake. A tragic one too. How can a man be so stupid so that he forgets to lock his doors. Yes, while I was offline for a bit, the threesome came back to find a rather pleasant surprise. ALL THE DOORS TO MY HOUSE HAD BEEN LEFT OPEN! They called it the raid of the century, taking everything I had to offer. My weapons gone. My wood and metal gone. My food gone. My rare armor gone.
The next morning I nearly threw my computer out the window. But behold, I may have lost the battle, but not the war. And so I continued to play and rebuild all I knew and loved. That is where we are today. I seek revenge on the house that stole from mine. Wish me luck.

If you've ever wanted to build a massive fortress with your friends and terrorize an island full of other players then this is the perfect game for you. Rust starts off slow, I'll admit, but once you've managed to find a few weapons and set up a base of operations the game picks up quickly. With a vast island to explore riddled with the dangers of radiated areas, hordes of the undead, and your fellow players; you'll quickly find that your trusty shotgun on it's own may not be enough to survive.
Rust is an amazing game for an alpha release, and it's only getting better. Yes it has some bugs, but that's to be expected at this stage of the game. If you're interested in jumping into a survival sandbox that has an easier learning curve than others in the genre (Day Z for example) then this is a great buy. One tip I will say, make friends, or bring some with you, otherwise the world of Rust can be a very deadly environment.

Rust is a post apocalyptic game that sets the player in a map where they have to gather resources, build bases, and deal with other players (this can be good or bad.) Rust is two parts DayZ and one part minecraft.
The Good:
Gathering- To craft anything you need materials, right?  Of course you do. The player can gather these resources many ways, trees for wood, or even wood piles found on the ground to gather at a faster rate. For the harder stuff, the player can bang on rocks (these are special rocks, these have different colors and are found in the middle of an area, rather than close to the environment's rocks, the ones part of the actual map) These resources are common but not extremely common, meaning you do have to travel a bit from your base if you need to gather large amounts. You will find these "gathering points" but you have to be comfortable traveling a little.
Crafting- Almost anything can be crafted by the player, from weapons to med kits to building materials. But there is a draw back, crafting takes time and you move slower while crafting. Also not every item is available to player from the beginning, the player has to find schematics or a "research kit" to learn how to craft the materials..
Building- After gathering resources the player can begin to craft the materials to build their base; foundations, pillars, walls, doors, ect. Building is extremely snappy and easy. But there are something about building that I will cover later.
The Bad:
Other Players- This one is the biggest draw back to the game for me. Most people have no respect for you and your work and wont even think twice about shooting you in the face and raiding your base. While some people might like this about the game, I do not. Nothing is more infuriating than getting shot in the face because you trust a person to just go on his/her own way. This type of mentality leads to more and more of these KoS(Kill on Sight) situations. If one player is scared the other person might kill them its only reasonable to perform a preventive strike and just kill the player, thus keeping the cycle going.
Griefing- I have not experienced this first hand but I am sure sooner or later its going to happen. This is where the bad part of building comes into play. While your base is being raided, people bring explosive charges, enough of these will destroy your base completely if set correctly... but this isn't the bad part. Sometimes the raiders will place pillars in the center of the foundation, this prevents the base owner to rebuild.. Why? Because it is IMPOSSIBLE to remove pillars, they are literally indestructible, one misplaced pillar can totally change the layout of the players base..Again at the time of writing this review this is a problem that may or may not be addressed.
Rust is a great game, it has a huge amount of potential.. If you are willing to deal with the bugs and the lack of features because this game is still in alpha (at the time writing this review.) And if you can deal with the KoS type of gameplay go ahead and grab it.
But I do HIGHLY suggest that you follow this game closely and WAIT until the game officially goes "gold" and releases. Then make your decision on buying the game or not.
This review is purely my opinion of the game.

What can I say about this game that people already haven't?
I suppose I should start by saying that this game is hard. Really hard, at least for newcomers looking for a new survival game to play. This is by no means a "realistic Minecraft" in any way. Don't expect to be able to get far in this game fast by going solo, or even with just 1 other friend to help you. As much potential as this game has, I find it hard to play it without getting extremely frustrated by the fact no matter what you try to obtain to build a life for yourself in this game, it can all be taken away with one well placed shot from a player more equipped than you (This is all based of PVP servers).
I understand that that's the point of this game, that it gives you the option to choose whatever path you take in this game, whether that be good or bad, but that's also the one of the game's flaws that can't really be changed, since you run the risk of restricting the player to begin with. Unless you're just starting out, 9 times out of 10 you'll just be gunning down every person that you stumble across. You kill them, so that already sets them back in terms of items that they had on them, and unless they had a spawn point and a decent base with extra supplies built up, that means they start back from square one all over again. And even if they had a base built up, I'm sure it would've taken some. if not a lot of those supplies to make whatever they had in the first place anyway. Killing other players off when you get the chance only gets you benefits in the long run.
This is an Alpha though, so I guess I really shouldn't be saying too much in terms of flaws this game might have, since there is already bound to be SOME. I guess my only other question is "How can they fix a part of the game that should give you free will to decide without restricting the player?" I'm eager to see if they can come up with one.
As for actually recommending this, I would definitely do so, but just remember one thing. This game IS NOT for the casual player. If you really want to play this game and get things fast, play it with about 3-5 other friends if you can.
