Even the players that don't cheat, grief, or taunt you will still kill you - partly because the community around Rust is just that bad, but mostly because the game REQUIRES it of them.  They cannot trust other players, ever, and have no way of knowning if you are really a new, naked player or if you're carrying an invisible shotgun.
I did manage to have a great time playing this game with my friends on an otherwise empty server, but that server went down and all of our progress was lost so we decided to try a populated server only to find that it was a completely pointless thing to do.  There is no place on a server with more than 10 people where you will be left alone long enough to gather the materials needed to make even a basic house... and even if you somehow DO manage to build yourself a little castle with a stout, metal door, it won't last the night because "bandits" wait for you to log of so that they can go to your base, blow it up with C4, murder you in your sleep, take all of your stuff, then destroy your ability to respawn.  Yes, that is right - the griefers can grief you even when you're not playing!!
PVE servers are not the answer, either, because they do not protect you from "raiders" (e.g. 12 year olds who have figured out how to dupe C4) that will blow up your house and steal all of your stuff.
If you enjoy bashing yourself in the face with a hammer, you'll love Rust... otherwise, stay away.

But I also hate everything about  Arma II (Gunplay?!). And I played Minecraft, but I guess im not creative enough to play that game more than an hour.
Then I came across "Rust" and people said that it's a mix between DayZ and Minecraft. That intrigued me enough to buy it.
And I did not regret it at all. I have never played an early access game as long as I played this. 39 hours at the moment and counting. The only thing that is really bothering me right now are the hackers. They do everything in their power to ruin the game. But they can't succeed, because the game is that addictive. There is always something to do, something to farm, something to craft. And you don't need to search for everything, running and looting around for hours just to get a weapon while not even knowing what you will do with it, once you got it. You just need a little patience and work to get your first little house, or your first weapon. But why stop there? You can always improve your gear and your house. One little thing after the other aaand you played 8 hours in one session.
The gunplay is rewarding, as weapons aren't always easy to handle, but you'll get to know them and with a little practice you will get it right. This game doesn't look like Crysis 3, but it's easy to look at and has beautiful lighting, which creates very atmospheric scenerys and gameplay. As with DayZ, I find the social aspect of the game most interesting. I had some friendly encounters and a lot of hostile ones. And that is just the way it should be. There is a certain kind of suspense, that you just don't get in other games. This game took the best ideas from Minecraft and DayZ, crafted them together on a workbench and created an amazing experience for you to play. I'm very exited to see where this game is going, if the Pre-Alpha is this good, the final game will be amazing. And it won't get cheaper than this for a long time. So get it while you can and start playing already!

Rust is simply one of the most enjoyable experieneces that I've ever had. The game is in Alpha so expect a few bugs but nothing game breaking, it's totally playable in its current form.
My friends and I spent our first night in Rust learning the basics. We gathered resources and built our shelter town complete with storage boxes and a shared furnance (Stone Resources seem to be scare on populated servers) surround by wooden barricades. After two hours or so we finally had  enough resources to create the basic firearms (Revolver, Pipe Shotgun). After we had armed ourselves up with sufficent armor and weapons we decided we would venture further than usual from our base.
We headed south and discovered a field full of endless resources! I spotted a stone resource off in the distance and rather than check around, made an immediate mad dash for it. I begin smashing it with my hatchet, excitedly telling my friends that things were starting to look up. Moments later a Shotgun blast echoed over my speakers and I fell to the ground...dead.
My friends hearing the shots did the smart thing and fled! I was naked back in my cabin slightly irritated that I had just lost all of my gear that I had worked so hard for, apart from some basic cloth armor and a stone hatchet anything viable was gone.
After the frustration of my death faded, I set back out to re-establish myself and this time I wouldn't venture out so ill prepared.
Frustrations aside once you get going and are familiar with the lay of the land (Where Rad Towns are and Resource Spawns) Rust is actually quite enjoyable to play.
It's definitely worh the price of admission as I cannot stop playing it. It's a great game with a ton of potential.

I love this game. As of this writing, I have 8 hours played. I've been playing for 3 days. It has the adventure, exploration, and wonder that I remember from early Minecraft years ago, along with the ruggedness and danger of DayZ (Which I wasn't a huge fan of anyways).
Currently I've got a fairly nice base, I've saved up resources and made a gun, and I'm stockpiling resources so that I can expand my base eventually.
The adventure and thrill of this game is unmatched in anything I've played. It's quicker paced than DayZ, in the sense that you can immediately start gathering and crafting instead of wandering for hours and finding nothing, and it's creative and explorative like Minecraft.
I'm still fairly new, but I'd give it something like a 9/10 in my books. It's still early Alpha and that's very apparent - not by bugs, but features. Holding a stone axe my hand looks like a caveman's, switch to a gun and all of a sudden I've got Navy Seal-esque gloves on. My stone axe appears as a regular hatchet to other players, etc.
However, it's very stable and very nice for an alpha game. It's being shaped by the awesome community, and I don't think I could ask for a cooler developer than Garry himself.

As this game is in alpha, a lot of things are still pretty rough, and not very fleshed out. But, this game is still ridiculously fun to play. It's unforgivingly difficult in the beginning, and you'll probably get killed by other players a lot; I like that though. It keeps your on your feet and it teaches you to be more efficient in gathering and building very quickly.
I highly recommend that you play with other people.

I like to think I enjoy pretty hardcore and unforgiving games, and maybe I'm just getting old or never really liked them in the first place.  But... this game is basically just "Get chased by 12 year olds with rocks for 45 minutes, until someone else shoots all of you."  It's funny at first... but then it's just kind of like... ♥♥♥♥ off.
If you play on a high pop server, it's just chat spam, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and griefing.  If you play on a low pop server its... well nobody is there so it's cool for a couple days and then you get bored.  Medium population seems about right I guess.
The developers need to spread the resources across the map, and make it more difficult to make firearms, actually to be honest Firearms add nothing to this game.  I mean they go from sticks and stones to fully automatic assault rifles.  That's a little jump wouldn't you say?  They should have gone Flintlock Pistol and a Musket, or mounted cannons as the highest you can evolve your weaponry to.  I mean you literally go from smashing eachother with rocks,  to destroying eachothers houses with C4 and full auto firefights in the span of about 30 minutes.
The world is actually very large, but resources only spawn in about 1/4 of the map.  So it's pretty pointless to even wander too far east.  Players make a living out of stealing your things, so you have to hide your house... but everyone knows all of the hiding spots, because the useable map area is so small, and it's quite easy to memorize all of the terrain. Additionally you can't build foundations on rocks, so it's impossible to build anything in really cool spots.  You end up building next to cool spots, and then your house sticks out like a sore thumb, and someone will definitely raid it.   It doesn't matter how many doors you have, or what you make your house out of.  You will get raided, and probably killed in your sleep if there are active players on your server.  You can join servers without Sleeper, and without PvP... but it's not risky, so it's not fun. They need to spend some time balancing.  If it's too risky then it's not fun, if it's not risky enough then it isn't fun.
Breaking into someones house should be very difficult. Somewhere in the 'It takes hours' not 'seconds' department. With the absolute bare start out, you can break into a basic house in 10 minutes. With C4 it literally takes seconds.
Additionally players need a way to actually unbuild things incase they make a mistake.
It's worth dicking around in for a while, but it's no DayZ or Minecraft.

This was one of my first experiences purchasing a "in progress" alpha version of a game. After seeing some videos on various sites, I admit it looked pretty ready as an alpha version game and plenty acceptable to be released for purchase despite the $20 price tag.
I was wrong, and my experience with Rust has made me question the acceptability of having alpha versions of games ready for purchase. Rust is not ready for release in any form, and to release and charge people $20 for an alpha version so you can test it for the developers is a questionable act towards the gaming community.
Yes, it is an alpha, and as an alpha this is the current state.
-Extremely barebones
-Serious balance issues
-Nearly unplayable lag and warping in most areas (Not FPS lag, I'm talking popping in and out everywhere so even killing animals is a challenge sometimes)
-Hacking is out of control, I had no idea it would be so severe on a Steam sold product (alpha or otherwise)
Again, I understand what was stated when I purchased this "game." In the end I will say it has immense potential, but I feel that this highly premature release may ultimately hurt Rust when it could be a truly amazing game in the end.
Simply put, paying to be an Alpha and Beta tester is a practice that I now strongly oppose having gone through the experience via Rust.
Rust may end up being a truly great game. However, it isn't ready to be released in any form. Do not buy this game yet.

Rust is, although not yet finished, one of the most immersive games I have ever played. Its setting resembles Stalker, a huge wasteland which is radiated at some places with ruins and signs of inhibitants long since gone.
When you start the game you have nothing on you but a torch, a stone and two bandages to still your bleedings if you get into a fight and your only goal now is: SURVIVAL!
Other players will likely kill you for your ressources, zombies running around will attack and kill you if you are not carefull to watch your steps and if you get into the woods there is a lot of wildlife which isnt always peaceful.
You only chance is to gather ressources like stone, wood and ore to build yourself a small hut (preferably somewhere hidden in the mountains not next to a road) where you are safe and can keep your supplies.
Now you have to obtain blueprints to build more sophisticated items, like guns or metal buildings which help you keeping trouble at bay.
So if you like Stalker, Minecraft, DayZ or any other similar game, this one is the best of them packed into one game.
Mind though, that it is still in an alpha phase so bugs and exploiters will haben from time to time but if you cant wait to give it a try its already worth its money!

Wow, so originally I rated this game quite some time ago. The things that have changed since then haven't been much. Graphically the game is beautiful, there's an entire different building system that isn't so broken, but it leaves a lot to be desired. Currently I've played 6 hours on the Dev 86 update.
The game is pretty glitchy still, and apparently a lot of hackers and cheats still get through the system.
They implemented a ingame store that lets you spend money on in game skins.... Yeah.
Zombies were once in the game years back, but now it's just normal animals that aren't much of a threat. Wolves don't travel in packs, nor do deer. The boars do not attack you, and run away if attacked.
The combat system is still pretty much the same, they have quite a few new weapons such as swords, maces, machete's and even a few guns....
The survival system isn't too hard, the rate of hunger/thirst don't go down too fast, and seem to be pretty easy to keep maxed out. The procedural map generation is a step in the right direction, but the buildings and areas it generates pre-apocalypse are lacking, and honestly horribly made. The buildings are hard to maneuver in, such as the lighthouse, or one of the "Houses". The developers haven't had a lot of practice proportioning buildings, as in some cases the doors are built for elephants, or people on horseback.
There is no current fast way to travel, making it take atleast a half hour to travel from one side of the map to the other, assuming you're not going uphill.  There are horses currently in the game, that can't be tamed or ridden. (To be implemented I assume)
The game has become quite a bit boring in comparison to its earlier updates, and relies on mods to make the game fun and interesting.
Do not waste your money on this game until it coems out, and only buy it if it is a finished product worthy of being bought.

Wow, so originally I rated this game quite some time ago. The things that have changed since then haven't been much. Graphically the game is beautiful, there's an entire different building system that isn't so broken, but it leaves a lot to be desired. Currently I've played 6 hours on the Dev 86 update.
The game is pretty glitchy still, and apparently a lot of hackers and cheats still get through the system.
They implemented a ingame store that lets you spend money on in game skins.... Yeah.
Zombies were once in the game years back, but now it's just normal animals that aren't much of a threat. Wolves don't travel in packs, nor do deer. The boars do not attack you, and run away if attacked.
The combat system is still pretty much the same, they have quite a few new weapons such as swords, maces, machete's and even a few guns....
The survival system isn't too hard, the rate of hunger/thirst don't go down too fast, and seem to be pretty easy to keep maxed out. The procedural map generation is a step in the right direction, but the buildings and areas it generates pre-apocalypse are lacking, and honestly horribly made. The buildings are hard to maneuver in, such as the lighthouse, or one of the "Houses". The developers haven't had a lot of practice proportioning buildings, as in some cases the doors are built for elephants, or people on horseback.
There is no current fast way to travel, making it take atleast a half hour to travel from one side of the map to the other, assuming you're not going uphill.  There are horses currently in the game, that can't be tamed or ridden. (To be implemented I assume)
The game has become quite a bit boring in comparison to its earlier updates, and relies on mods to make the game fun and interesting.
Do not waste your money on this game until it coems out, and only buy it if it is a finished product worthy of being bought.

It’s had some bad press because of the usual inbred trolls that gank you either when you’re newly spawned or when you’re asleep (offline). Rust's only goal is to survive, and it’s always challenging. You begin with nothing but a rock, a torch, and a couple of bandages, and if you try to spend more than two nights out in the open in that condition, you will die. It's an intimidating, sink-or-swim introduction to the game, but Rust isn't a forgiving experience. Most of the game world will do its best to kill you and while epic multiplayer battles are rare, ambush murders are not. Nor are you particularly durable, unlike conventional videogame characters, and if somebody puts a few bullets in you, you will die. Yet that fragility, coupled with the near-absolute freedom offered by an open-world, no-rules arena, is exactly what makes it work. "Go forth and do whatever the hell you want" is exhilarating.

Went out on a resource run and gathered a nice haul. On my way back I met Arnold Shwartznegger, he asked me "who is your daddy, and what does he do?" I tried to respond but he yelled "ITS NOT A TUMOUR!" and shot me in the face. Lost everything, had to start from where I was 2 hours previous.
10/10, would play again.

I was logged-on to the server just as it got wiped. Everything reset. A fresh start for everyone. It was my chance to shine, without getting cut to bits by high-tech-level bandits and raiders.
As I was working, I had heard repeatedly over voice comms about a player who had gotten the first airdrop of the game, which contained a military shotgun and M4 rifle. The highest-tier weapons available.
During one of my runs to the radioactive military zones, I happened to run straight past the player who had found the weapons. He fired first, and we exchanged shots. Luckily he wasn't carrying his big guns, or I would have died instantly. Also lucky, while my health dropped dangerously low, I didn't bleed, so I was able to make it out okay.
I watched him for a while as he moved back to his encampment, making a mental note of the part of the road he had set up beside for future use.
Much later in the game and without a single player vs player shot fired since that point, I had managed to deck myself out in full leather armor (One less than top tier), but still had only the basic cobbled-together firearms. I really needed a weapon.
I used two C4 to break into the guy's house. It was only logical. The weak are preyed upon by the strong, and he had fired first all those hours ago. Breaking into houses is the whole point of C4. The wooden wall fell and stole two top-tier weapons, the M4 and Shotgun. As I ran, gunshots pinged at my feet, but I kept moving. I continually checked to ensure that I was not followed.
Half an hour later, my friend was chopping wood out in a field when he started taking fire. He ducked behind a tree but he didn't have any weapons on him aside from a pathetic bow. I yelled at him to stay alive and keep them distracted, and I was able to nearly take down one guy before my friend died. I had taken two hits with a bow, which nearly killed me, but I got onto the other side of the cover the bowman was firing from. I took out my stolen shotgun and was very lucky to kill him in the first shot.
I fired another shot at the other guy, then pulled out the M4 but got killed before I managed to take him down. Luckily this was right beside my house and I respawned inside, grabbed an MP5 from a crate, and ran outside again. The surviving attacker was looting a corpse and I took him down. My friend helped me gather up all the loot from our two bodies, and the bodies of the attackers, and everything from inside the house and move it up into a stash in the mountains.
When I logged back on three hours later to check on things, I spawned in a field and I knew that while I was offline my character had died. I ran north to check. My house had a hole in the side of it, which I was fully expecting. That's why I moved everything out, everything.
The mountain stash had gotten its door blown off and every last item had disappeared. Just as I was checking the last crate for any scraps, I heard footsteps, and I was incredibly conscious of the fact that one of our attackers had respawned and watched us take the stuff into the mountain. I had nothing to defend myself with. A man in black armor entered the shelter and blew me away with a shotgun.
They started a war over a wooden wall and two weapons they replaced in a heartbeat.
It is a war they won by good intelligence, but also by attacking a defenceless sleeper.
They have made an enemy they will live to regret.
The Axe has tasted blood.

I was logged-on to the server just as it got wiped. Everything reset. A fresh start for everyone. It was my chance to shine, without getting cut to bits by high-tech-level bandits and raiders.
As I was working, I had heard repeatedly over voice comms about a player who had gotten the first airdrop of the game, which contained a military shotgun and M4 rifle. The highest-tier weapons available.
During one of my runs to the radioactive military zones, I happened to run straight past the player who had found the weapons. He fired first, and we exchanged shots. Luckily he wasn't carrying his big guns, or I would have died instantly. Also lucky, while my health dropped dangerously low, I didn't bleed, so I was able to make it out okay.
I watched him for a while as he moved back to his encampment, making a mental note of the part of the road he had set up beside for future use.
Much later in the game and without a single player vs player shot fired since that point, I had managed to deck myself out in full leather armor (One less than top tier), but still had only the basic cobbled-together firearms. I really needed a weapon.
I used two C4 to break into the guy's house. It was only logical. The weak are preyed upon by the strong, and he had fired first all those hours ago. Breaking into houses is the whole point of C4. The wooden wall fell and stole two top-tier weapons, the M4 and Shotgun. As I ran, gunshots pinged at my feet, but I kept moving. I continually checked to ensure that I was not followed.
Half an hour later, my friend was chopping wood out in a field when he started taking fire. He ducked behind a tree but he didn't have any weapons on him aside from a pathetic bow. I yelled at him to stay alive and keep them distracted, and I was able to nearly take down one guy before my friend died. I had taken two hits with a bow, which nearly killed me, but I got onto the other side of the cover the bowman was firing from. I took out my stolen shotgun and was very lucky to kill him in the first shot.
I fired another shot at the other guy, then pulled out the M4 but got killed before I managed to take him down. Luckily this was right beside my house and I respawned inside, grabbed an MP5 from a crate, and ran outside again. The surviving attacker was looting a corpse and I took him down. My friend helped me gather up all the loot from our two bodies, and the bodies of the attackers, and everything from inside the house and move it up into a stash in the mountains.
When I logged back on three hours later to check on things, I spawned in a field and I knew that while I was offline my character had died. I ran north to check. My house had a hole in the side of it, which I was fully expecting. That's why I moved everything out, everything.
The mountain stash had gotten its door blown off and every last item had disappeared. Just as I was checking the last crate for any scraps, I heard footsteps, and I was incredibly conscious of the fact that one of our attackers had respawned and watched us take the stuff into the mountain. I had nothing to defend myself with. A man in black armor entered the shelter and blew me away with a shotgun.
They started a war over a wooden wall and two weapons they replaced in a heartbeat.
It is a war they won by good intelligence, but also by attacking a defenceless sleeper.
They have made an enemy they will live to regret.
The Axe has tasted blood.

This is relevant to the game as it is on 1/19/2014.  It's very rough, but it is fun, BUT do not say a word in chat...ever.  Look at wiki or ask a friend.  The hackers are rampant.  I have learned that if you don't talk, they can't target you for suicide hacks.  I think they can also teleport to you, and then there are aimbots that will insta kill you with one bullet (which is basically impossible at range).
So, if you buy this now, don't speak, it sucks, because you want to help new players, but only use voice chat.
Updated: 2/6/14  That suicide glitch is gone, so it's safe to talk in global chat now.  Cheaters are still rampant, but not as bad as before.  The "official" servers are a 100% joke, as they have no admins, so they are filled with cheaters.  My suggestion is to play on a modded server running Rust++ or Oxide with active admins.  Even with active admins, admin abuse is a problem, so you have to find a good server.  If you can find the right server, with the right admins, and the right players, the game is amazing even lacking so much.  I also suggest starting on a server with 50 or less players at peak times.  Trying to get a start on a server with even 75+ people can lead to you dying a ton.  Don't just think that all people killing nakeds are jerks either, because at around 100 players there is a subset of people who will pretend to be noobs, and run around naked with M4s and shotguns.  At this point, anyone who gets close to you has to die.  Your biggest defense on a populated server is to give people a WIDE passage, and don't look at them after you've spotted them.  If you keep staring at people, they get nervous and shoot.

Think Day Z and Minecraft as two seperate games. Now have both of them come together, go out for a nice seafood dinner, and head home to have a little fun. Day Z forgot to use protection and several months later... BOOM. Rust was born. Zombies, survival, running naked through the woods to gather essentials like wood and rocks (you gather these things with a rock at first), building your own base of operations, learning how to make different weapons, armor, supplies, and what not... This game is fantastic and well worth buying. Sure its in early alpha but hey... It's not every day you find an alpha game that runs this well. The combat can be a little clunky but I'm sure that will progress into something much more fun with time. Give it a try and be pleasantly surprised as you team up with random people from around the world and work together to survive.
Another note... Find a low population server. Those tend to be left alone by griefers, trolls, hackers, raiders, and the like. Even better if you can find a non pvp low pop server. If you can stick with one with less than 20 population, you should have a good time. Oh and I hope you like chicken because everything that isn't a zombie drops chicken.

The gaming experience in Rust is unparalleled to many similar games: of a genre so hyperbolized in systems, graphics, and gameplay.  It becomes so difficult to truly find which game is best for you.  So how does it compare?
Rust is undeniably one of the most impressive and well established survival games I've had the opportunity of playing.  Despite this game being in early access (has been 1 month and 8 days since release), it is already extremely well built and enjoyable.  Initially, this game boasts an extremely well populated community, with hundreds of players on a game at a time, with hundreds of games running in all.  In game; the game plays fairly well with solid fps even on moderate laptop and pc systems.  To sum up the experience, you will find yourself spawned in any random locaiton of the map (an island), with a number of biomes ranging from plains and mountains, to radioactive zones and coastline.  The day and night cycle is impressive, with a general atmospheric experience that has you truly immersed.  While there currently isnt any weather system in place, I am certain there will be one in the future.  Wildlife and enemies are sparse throughout the game, a situtation that has plauged gameplay as explained in the cons below.  Furthermore, a simple yet enjoyable crafting system and random event (air drops) makes the game extremely pleasurable.  Lastly, the crafting systems leads to an impressively fun building system, allowing players to be creative with their homes and defenses.
CONS
Despite the amazing well built gameplay and graphics, the game lacks in the MOST important aspect of all - the multiplayer.
My ONLY critique of the game is the overall lack of stability in multiplayer.  Inititally playing, I had faced multiple players as a fresh spawn, often times finding myself outgunned by veteran or well established players.  These players undeniably hold themselves to a standard of KOS (Kill On Sight), rampaging and hunting players throughout the game.  This can be EXTREMELY disconcerning for players, especially for new ones.  I have oftentimes been attacked within the relative safety of my home, as bandits attack new players' homes until they are forced to come out.  Oftentimes, this results in a shotgun blast to your head - an instantaneous end to all of your hard work.  To add to the inequality of the game, loot and resource spawns are extremely unequal.  Oftentimes spawning in specific areas of the map, resulting in highly contested areas of extreme wealth, and other areas lacking any (if at all) resources.  This makes it extremely difficult for these new players to establish themselves, if they are forced to contest these resource-soaked areas, while undeniably outgunned by established players.
IF there is any lasting note I have to say about this game, it would be that = Rust is an enjoyable, impressive, and entertaining experience for any/all gamers to the survival genre.  Multiplayer games can be enjoyable, while the game runs smoothly in an impressive aesthetic world.  Further enhanced by its crafting system.  Only qualms, are that you should worry about other players and initial inequality.  But once you find your mojo, and truy begin to establish yourself in the game: the experience becomes second to none.  I highly reccomend this game, and do hope that the issues (few as they are!), shall be fixed (this IS early access afterall!!!) eventually.
So go out, and play some RUST!  You will learn to love it!!

Rust is yet another early access survival game that everyone has jumped on the bandwagon to. Sadly it is a large portion of this community that has essentially ruined what is already quite a fragile and easy to destroy concept.
The reason I write this review now is largely down to the progression of development and how torrid the game has become. Updates are horrifically slow and glaring issues which should be getting ironed out are being overlooked. It may be an alpha but there seems to be a real lack of dev support for them to justify a price of £15.
The game itself is like any other in the growing genre except it can be manipulated with cheats, bad admins and people that are just out of grief/troll. The community is immature and horrible most of the time and it just diminishes the concept as PVP overrides the survival aspect. You can spawn; be killed in seconds and then have to start over. This can happen frequently and even when you finally get some items together and focusing on surviving; you run into hackers which plague the game. The inventory system is quite neat and easy to use but the combat is incredibly ropey along with the engine. Visually the game is bright and pleasing on the eye but the landscape textures are very bland and it's all very copy and pasted. The setting may seem large but it's very repetitive in time.
Too many people are giving in 10/10 within the first 10 minutes of playing thinking it is the best game ever created. This is a bug-ridden alpha that's probably 3 years of completion and even then; I can't see how they can prevent the community from delivering the final nail in the coffin.
DayZ may have a catalogue of woes itself but it is probably the best in the genre at this stage. Rust is not unique in any way; it's just a first-person survival game with glaring technical and concept issues that are years from rectifying. For £15 I do not recommend this and in all honesty; even as a F2P game; it wouldn't even be worth your time.

This game is great for an early access game. On my first day of playing, I had a few bad spawns. Being attacked by wolves, zombies and bears (Oh my!) And getting generaly lost trying to find my way around the map. Eventually, I managed to find a group of people in the server who were really friendly. They helped save me from a wolf attack outside my camp and gave me supplies to help survive later on. Someone even gave me blueprints for crafting special items. We hung around a particular spot on the map (One with a giant tower) near my camp. We started building around it and I started to improve on crafting, hunting and searching for supplies. Through one of the blueprints I recieved, I built a large supply crate for the people who helped me get to a good start. A few minutes later, I was stabbed in the back from someone nearby! The people who were with me went commando and started a 10-1 man hunt. The guy escaped and got away with a pick axe I recieved from one of the guys, (I got another one back, so it's okay.) and my sleeping bag, so I couldn't respawn to my camp. But it's the journey back to the camp that was pure torture. You get respawned to the other side of the map! You could try to follow the roads, but it's tooo easy for zombies and wolves to get you. You can hardly run fast enough to escape. Plus there's a hunger bar that gradually lowers, making it worse. I eventually made it back, and got my supplies from one of the guys. (Plus a little extra.) Everything was fine after that, and I have a good set of items, thanks to the group that were friendly enough to help a newcomer out. This is a great game to play with your friends. If you don't have any friends that play rust, you might be in trouble until you get into a group of allies who want to enjoy the game for what it is. A hunting and crafting pvp survival game that's working so well before it's finished developement.

This game is great for an early access game. On my first day of playing, I had a few bad spawns. Being attacked by wolves, zombies and bears (Oh my!) And getting generaly lost trying to find my way around the map. Eventually, I managed to find a group of people in the server who were really friendly. They helped save me from a wolf attack outside my camp and gave me supplies to help survive later on. Someone even gave me blueprints for crafting special items. We hung around a particular spot on the map (One with a giant tower) near my camp. We started building around it and I started to improve on crafting, hunting and searching for supplies. Through one of the blueprints I recieved, I built a large supply crate for the people who helped me get to a good start. A few minutes later, I was stabbed in the back from someone nearby! The people who were with me went commando and started a 10-1 man hunt. The guy escaped and got away with a pick axe I recieved from one of the guys, (I got another one back, so it's okay.) and my sleeping bag, so I couldn't respawn to my camp. But it's the journey back to the camp that was pure torture. You get respawned to the other side of the map! You could try to follow the roads, but it's tooo easy for zombies and wolves to get you. You can hardly run fast enough to escape. Plus there's a hunger bar that gradually lowers, making it worse. I eventually made it back, and got my supplies from one of the guys. (Plus a little extra.) Everything was fine after that, and I have a good set of items, thanks to the group that were friendly enough to help a newcomer out. This is a great game to play with your friends. If you don't have any friends that play rust, you might be in trouble until you get into a group of allies who want to enjoy the game for what it is. A hunting and crafting pvp survival game that's working so well before it's finished developement.

Rust: BF4 without the vehicles. That's the best way I can describe Rust in its current state. The game has MASSIVE potential, but that potential currently goes untapped. What does that leave you with? Mindless PvP where newspawns are killed for fun, because there's nothing else to do once you know how to play the game. The building aspect of Rust is currently nothing more than lipstick and the novelty of it wears off fast. The first time you play you'll probably spend a day or two building your perfect base only to find that game is currently so imbalanced it's not funny. It takes a matter of seconds to break into buildings that people spend days making, and that leaves you wondering why build at all? This conundrum has lead most servers turning into a PvP fest where gangs roam around griefing newspawn because it's about the only thing to do.
Should you buy this game? Right now I'd say no. Don't get me wrong. You'll be hooked after playing it for the first time, but unless you are a prepubescent teenager that has no job, is on holidays and can stay up all day drinking red bull, then you'll come away from this game more often than not feeling frustrated and annoyed. Great game, great potential, but seriously broken.

With the current state of the game and the rampant hackers on literally every server, I wouldn't suggest buying this game to play it - only to invest in its potential. And let me tell you, it has a -lot- of potential.
Sadly, a lot of that potential is being lost in the complete and utter lack of VAC doing it's job correctly and there being a serious lack of server-side anti-hack plugins.
4/10 in it's current state. Great atmosphere, pretty solid controls, phenomenal building core, but greifing and raiding - even on PvE servers where that kind of activity is "not allowed" (Can only be enforced when an Admin is on and witnesses said raiding) - is ruining the game.
The developers know about this already, however, and they're looking into ways to circumvent people simply building walls over a base's defenses to break in and steal everything. I'm still unsure how they're going to fix the hacker problem, however. Any server that's PvP-enabled is simply unplayable at the moment. Fresh-spawn killers and noclip flying hackers with aimbots are rampant -everywhere-.
I still recommend this game, though. On the soul basis that IF ENOUGH PEOPLE FUND IT, the potential this game has will actually become reality.

With the current state of the game and the rampant hackers on literally every server, I wouldn't suggest buying this game to play it - only to invest in its potential. And let me tell you, it has a -lot- of potential.
Sadly, a lot of that potential is being lost in the complete and utter lack of VAC doing it's job correctly and there being a serious lack of server-side anti-hack plugins.
4/10 in it's current state. Great atmosphere, pretty solid controls, phenomenal building core, but greifing and raiding - even on PvE servers where that kind of activity is "not allowed" (Can only be enforced when an Admin is on and witnesses said raiding) - is ruining the game.
The developers know about this already, however, and they're looking into ways to circumvent people simply building walls over a base's defenses to break in and steal everything. I'm still unsure how they're going to fix the hacker problem, however. Any server that's PvP-enabled is simply unplayable at the moment. Fresh-spawn killers and noclip flying hackers with aimbots are rampant -everywhere-.
I still recommend this game, though. On the soul basis that IF ENOUGH PEOPLE FUND IT, the potential this game has will actually become reality.

Have you ever played the games Mincecraft or DayZ and enjoyed them? Well, perhaps you've been drawn to this game then, interested to play something that has a combination of both worlds, wasteland survival elements with an extensive crafting system? Well, be ready for a extremely infuriating experience...
Beginning game: Mostly revolves around just hoping for some random stranger not killing you out of a few giggles, or evade them by being the biggest xenophobe in game. Getting a hatchet, the first and vital tool is your next objective. Getting this you need to gather stones and wood, which can be an experience as struggling as just trying to survive in this world of immature people attacking you on sight merely to have a short laugh since the gathering of resources is very competetive, people don't like sharing. Coming to a place where there are resources, if you are playing on a high populated server which is how the game is meant to be played, will often lead to you getting shot, axed or hit over the head with a rock.
If you manage to reach that far you'll not have your first proper tool... Now for food! Hatchet a pig to death (Because all the other wildlife will murder or run away from you at this stage in the game.) and then make a campfire to cook your food and eat. If you've reached this far in the game, call yourself lucky that you've not one of the murderous fully geared up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s that wander the wastes of Rust. Now, a bow... Your first weapon so you can defend yourself against zombies, bears and wolves which all maul you to bits of flesh if you try using your hatchet. Now you can gather food and defend yourself reliably, however this comes with a huge downside, that is players. They will see you as a threat if you have a bow, people will shoot you on sight if they see the slightest kind of weapon on your person.
Middle game: Now, you need to build a house! Don't bother trying to even build a regular ol' wood shelter, those people can break into in less than a minu... Yeah, ignore all that up there, to sum this up is this;
Great mechanics and a great idea for a game, horrible community that does everything in its power to kill, main and cause any kind of harm to you. I've literally built up a huge house, gotten full gear and then logged out, the next morning all of my stuff is gone, my house has been leveled to the ground and I have to start the frustrating journey all over again. Play this game with 5 or more friends, otherwise you're doomed.

The charm and simplicity was beaten out of Rust Legacy. Now this sluggish and chaotic version looks good but is a harsh experience without friends.
#Update:
It's gotten worse over time, now bloated with so many things that the initial experience consists of rubbish like being prompted to wait for skins to download, and being killed at spawn by animals and other players(if you didn't die before you even had control over your player) while trying to get to grips with a steep learning curve.
Not being able to run Fraps and the Steam Overlay in the same launch is souring. The saying "less is more" seems to escape the devs, where they could have spent these years making the game functional(as a program, and in its mechanics) rather than say "
" and now you need an SSD to have anywhere near proportionate loading times.
Why add a chopper if it will blow up your base when nobody's even in it? Or when you can't even figure out why it shoots you as you try to hide from it. Why have a bear in the game for such a long time when it kills players through walls? Why add fatal temperatures and radiation when the distance of a few metres take you from warm to freezing, or fine to fully radiated?
I've survived bleeding to death while underwater for a minute at 20hp and being shot, and other times died because I was running through a field and simply got radiated no matter how hard I tried to run away from the radiated parts. Game mechanics like this are a mess, and are being left in their current state, rather than reverted to something workable until they're fully realised.
In Legacy you could slap a building down anywhere(even late into the wipe) and produce some revolvers. But now you have to start as soon as a wipe hits, otherwise you get flame raided, and it has to be close to barrels(weapon components) or you won't be able to even produce revolvers. And you'll need to build a tool cupboard quickly, otherwise you can get griefed now much worse than what would happen in Legacy.
You now have to build a code lock to control your door, which makes the game much more difficult starting out, or for solo players. Anyone can steal your door even if you have a tool cupboard down. If you can't build a code lock(which takes metal) then you're stuck with a wooden key, but you have to keep it on you to open the door. Maybe this mechanic isn't seen in other games because it's complete trash?
As a solo player you can't have a base anymore. As soon as you die with your key on you, someone can take it and steal your base. Even in a group, someone has to stay inside the base to be a door opener, which reduces the experience of one player to sitting there being bored. In Legacy you didn't have to worry about these things, which I think makes this version of Rust an objectively bad game. How do you manage to get a code lock if the wooden keys you rely on until then are a failure of a mechanic?
You'd think hiding in grass or skulking around at night could make things easier until you're in a stronger position(code lock + guns) but trying to be sneaky will get you killed by what seems to be an epidemic of wallhackers. If you want to report a cheater then you need to go through the unstable recaptcha system. Wallhack prevention seems to be stuck on the shoulders of server admins, but surely with all the money in gaming a better system could have been implemented.
Seeing at night is in itself a broken mechanic, as one of my friends complained about not seeing anything, while my other friend in the same moment next to us on different hardware/software could see clearly. Even the jump puzzles in Rust are bad, some being downwards(makes jumping not work half the time) and some have you needing to not bash your head above you. I've done jumping competitions in Counter-Strike for fun, and still loathed the Rust jumps.
When I play the game more towards the balance of roleplay, I won't be able to produce good weapons, and even if you get a bow headshot; someone can easily survive that. If I play the game more towards the balance of deathmatch meta(get in first, build near components) I can amass guns which easily overpower other players, but those mechanics are so out of balance that nobody joins a server after the first 12 hours of a wipe, so what's the point of having guns on a dead server?
Even the survival element of Rust which took its DNA from Gmod Stranded and DayZ mod has been squeezed out by the addition of poor mechanics. There's sentry guns, and an AI tank, and a chopper. The tank was supposed to help fix the game, but left it feeling even more like a Battlefield title.
If you run out of torches and can't see, just suicide to get one for free. Need animal fat? Suicide. Low on health/hunger/thirst? Just suicide. Don't like your random map spawn? Suicide. The survival theme often loses the immersion on offer by the mechanics pushing a deathmatch/suicide meta at every turn.
After all these years of development surely the game should be streamlined, optimized, and intuitive by now. But instead it's a rough gem(I've left plenty of minor gripes out of this review) which merely punishes new or solo players, and the reward to experienced groups which control the high value areas of the map with dozens of guns with; will find them worthless when they have nobody to shoot the next day.
It's a step up from Legacy in terms of graphics and combating flyhack cheats, but otherwise it's a complete disaster. I might play it with friends, but not alone.

I built a majestic wooden palace in a secluded, dense forest. From time to time a weary traveler would come past and be in awe of this mighty structure that provides shelter from the elements and beasts (people as well I guess). I would welcome them with open arms if they were a naked man with nothing but a rock. It is of course the right thing to do.
I assure them the shotgun is for protection, not only for me but them as well.
I invite them in from the cold with the promise of a warm fire and food in their belly. In a world as brutal as Rust it is rare to meet a kind soul offering shelter and food, not many can resist this offer. Once he is inside I lead him through several doors which lead to a sunken pit room with an open ceiling. I then lock the door behind him.
It is only then he realises the true nature of the situation as the floor beneath him is full of backpacks and bodies. I throw scraps of chicken to my new captive from the open ceiling above. Another weary traveler walks by; I invite him inside for a can of beans.

My prisoner screams at the top of his lungs "DON'T TAKE THE BEANS IT'S A LIE!" but it is already too late. He too is trapped. Soon enough they have 3 more friends and I make them fight each other to the death for scraps of food for my amusement. It is prisoner number 7 who changes the game forever. The 4 remaining prisoners combine their limited resources to build a stair case out of the pit. It is then the hunt for the most dangerous game begins. There is no exit, all windows are barred. There are no weapons, only an 8 story tall maze building and a man wielding a shotgun hunting for you.
There were many screams that evening and people passing by quickly fled. By morning only I remained. Preparing a meal for the next person to come to my home.
11/10 would hunt man again.

The most interesting survival game on Steam. If you pick the right server, it's not just a KoS game (like some other game  *cough*), but you can make many friends, build bases with them and attack other groups.
The big differences between this and DayZ is that you can build your own house/base, which makes sense instead of running around the map without a shelter, and the crafting, so you can build your own weapons, ammo, explosives, or other supplies.
The game has a big map, but most of it is not used yet. It has a lot of potential, but it's still in alpha, and the developers are adding cool content every few weeks.  However, it is already worth $20.
One of the best thing is that you can pick a server according to your preferences (sleepers, PvP, friendly, modded server, etc.), which will change your game experience. Pick one with good admins, some will cheat.
The day/night cycle makes the game even more fun. Another thing you'll love is: if you die, you loose only the stuff you brought with you. If you left some stuff at your base, you can get it and go back fighting!
I definitely recommend this game.

As I'm sure has been said a thousand times, Rust is best described as a cross between Minecraft and Day Z: You wake up in a relatively deserted landscape, collect supplies, build a house, craft weapons, explore, and survive zombies/animals/other players. And like Minecraft and Day Z, there is something inherently fun about this simple goal. Yet, in it's current state (an Alpha pre-release) it tends to be quite frustrating too.
Playing with only a handful of other rival players can be difficult, and playing with a full server is pretty much impossible. A lot will obviously be changed over the course of the development, but I really hope they make the early part of the game easier to get into. I almost gave up after the first time playing, as it's fairly easy to spend a lot of time building supplies only to have everything wiped out after getting killed by a stray zombie (who will continue to hang around your house and kill you over and over if you attempt to collect your items).
I have a lot of minor complaints, most of which I wont bother with as I'm sure they will be addressed in future updates. But they really should re-engineer things like stucture decay and looting. It's demoralizing coming back to the game after only a couple days absence and finding everything you've worked toward completely gone. What makes a game like Minecraft fun is that you can keep building on what you've done. But in Rust you are forced to start from scratch too frequently, and collecting the large amount of wood an rocks required to rebuild a house isn't fun enough that I want to keep doing it.
I am recommending this game because it shows potentiial. No matter what direction the developers go in, I'd be willing to bet modders will eat this game up. And there will eventually be gameplay styles for all tastes and sizes.
My rating (so far): 3/5

Rust, This game has a TON of possibility.
Positive- Building, accomplishing, getting loot, killing zombies. This game is very fun. It's like unpolished minecraft with guns. The systems are really cool. Blueprints and research kits allow for expansion and make it so when you die you do not lose quite as much if you start over. I feel there are two ways  to play this game, and they overlap. The first is building, trading and being peaceful. Being nice, helping others. Creating friendships. The second is killing, ambushing, stealing and looting. Both are acceptable and both are fun.
Negitive-This is where the second play style hurts the game, its one thing to attack a base, kill its people and steal their stuff. But people really ♥♥♥♥ others over. One time I saw an unarmed naked guy, he asked for food. I gave him 6 cans of tuna and said good luck. He pulled out a shotgun and shot me in the face. This is where the game gets old. Its contagious, i found myself killing unarmed people out of fear of being robbed again. The ♥♥♥♥ery is server to server basis. Some are better then others.
Tips-Do not trust anyone
-Build a small hidden house
-Pack as little as possible, I only pack good armor and weapons when I'm planning to get into a fight, other wise I expect lose it
-Biggest tip is have friends, one fully equipped guy can EASILY be murdered by two ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with handmade pistols, as a     result, Just the presence of others makes you be a force to rekon with.
-Please, be nice to noobs, but also, Stay away from them so you don't get jacked.
-Just watch, I find myself, as a looter, just watching what groups and people do from afar, if I feel I can easily and quickly kill them, I do that. Just watch and be smart.
Overall, this is a fun game. At $20 its hard to say no. It's still in Alpha, if you're expecting a finished game, go elsewhere.

As I'm sure has been said a thousand times, Rust is best described as a cross between Minecraft and Day Z: You wake up in a relatively deserted landscape, collect supplies, build a house, craft weapons, explore, and survive zombies/animals/other players. And like Minecraft and Day Z, there is something inherently fun about this simple goal. Yet, in it's current state (an Alpha pre-release) it tends to be quite frustrating too.
Playing with only a handful of other rival players can be difficult, and playing with a full server is pretty much impossible. A lot will obviously be changed over the course of the development, but I really hope they make the early part of the game easier to get into. I almost gave up after the first time playing, as it's fairly easy to spend a lot of time building supplies only to have everything wiped out after getting killed by a stray zombie (who will continue to hang around your house and kill you over and over if you attempt to collect your items).
I have a lot of minor complaints, most of which I wont bother with as I'm sure they will be addressed in future updates. But they really should re-engineer things like stucture decay and looting. It's demoralizing coming back to the game after only a couple days absence and finding everything you've worked toward completely gone. What makes a game like Minecraft fun is that you can keep building on what you've done. But in Rust you are forced to start from scratch too frequently, and collecting the large amount of wood an rocks required to rebuild a house isn't fun enough that I want to keep doing it.
I am recommending this game because it shows potentiial. No matter what direction the developers go in, I'd be willing to bet modders will eat this game up. And there will eventually be gameplay styles for all tastes and sizes.
My rating (so far): 3/5

Rust, This game has a TON of possibility.
Positive- Building, accomplishing, getting loot, killing zombies. This game is very fun. It's like unpolished minecraft with guns. The systems are really cool. Blueprints and research kits allow for expansion and make it so when you die you do not lose quite as much if you start over. I feel there are two ways  to play this game, and they overlap. The first is building, trading and being peaceful. Being nice, helping others. Creating friendships. The second is killing, ambushing, stealing and looting. Both are acceptable and both are fun.
Negitive-This is where the second play style hurts the game, its one thing to attack a base, kill its people and steal their stuff. But people really ♥♥♥♥ others over. One time I saw an unarmed naked guy, he asked for food. I gave him 6 cans of tuna and said good luck. He pulled out a shotgun and shot me in the face. This is where the game gets old. Its contagious, i found myself killing unarmed people out of fear of being robbed again. The ♥♥♥♥ery is server to server basis. Some are better then others.
Tips-Do not trust anyone
-Build a small hidden house
-Pack as little as possible, I only pack good armor and weapons when I'm planning to get into a fight, other wise I expect lose it
-Biggest tip is have friends, one fully equipped guy can EASILY be murdered by two ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with handmade pistols, as a     result, Just the presence of others makes you be a force to rekon with.

Overall, this is a fun game. At $20 its hard to say no. It's still in Alpha, if you're expecting a finished game, go elsewhere.

Rust is an interesting challenge. If you play like me, that is, as a one man wolf pack, Rust can, and will, knock you down, call your mother fat, and then steal your lunch money.
I tend to go it alone. I don't use the chat that often, and the voice chat even less. I had played a server long enough to the point where I could craft most everything in the game and was feeling pretty good about myself. I had avoided death at the hands of my fellow players well enough, and decided it was time to settle down. I picked out a nice quiet place as far away as I could reasonably get and still find resources, where I started to build. I started building up my house, trying to make it as secure as possible, or at least make someone trying to get in go through a whole lot of trouble.
All was going well, I was hidden, my house was almost complete, and I hadn't been shot at in awhile. Then my front door exploded.
There were two of them. One began moving through the first floor, searching for loot or a way up. The other stood just outside, M4 trained on the staircase door. Never leave your staircase unlocked, children. Unfortunately for him, i had roof access, and my trusty rifle. He went down, but the one inside got a lucky shot on me as we fought in the foyer. He bugged out, but stayed just close enough to keep an eye on me and my house. That's how I knew this wasn't over.
They came back, four of them, dressed in kevlar and armed with shotguns and assault rifles. The standoff lasted three nights. I killed another one or two, in an attempt to banish them from my house, but only resulted in losing the stairwell. Now, trapped in the upper floors of my fortress, surrounded by men and boys who wanted me dead, and my possessions in their hands, I waited. I waited for them to bring the explosives. By no means would they breach my sanctuary with anything less. I settled in to the corner with my shotgun, and waited for the end.
I would view my experience in Rust as the typical experience of a player who goes it alone. You may find yourself a secluded location, and build your house strong. Craft your weapons to defend yourself from man and beast alike. Sleep comfortable at night, secure in your home, and in your defenses. But they will come. Through the night and the wilderness, the men who wear black will find you, and all that you have made will be as dust.
Find your friends, and bring them close, for only together will you be safe. So that when the men who wear black come to your door, you will be ready.

Rust is an interesting challenge. If you play like me, that is, as a one man wolf pack, Rust can, and will, knock you down, call your mother fat, and then steal your lunch money.
I tend to go it alone. I don't use the chat that often, and the voice chat even less. I had played a server long enough to the point where I could craft most everything in the game and was feeling pretty good about myself. I had avoided death at the hands of my fellow players well enough, and decided it was time to settle down. I picked out a nice quiet place as far away as I could reasonably get and still find resources, where I started to build. I started building up my house, trying to make it as secure as possible, or at least make someone trying to get in go through a whole lot of trouble.
All was going well, I was hidden, my house was almost complete, and I hadn't been shot at in awhile. Then my front door exploded.
There were two of them. One began moving through the first floor, searching for loot or a way up. The other stood just outside, M4 trained on the staircase door. Never leave your staircase unlocked, children. Unfortunately for him, i had roof access, and my trusty rifle. He went down, but the one inside got a lucky shot on me as we fought in the foyer. He bugged out, but stayed just close enough to keep an eye on me and my house. That's how I knew this wasn't over.
They came back, four of them, dressed in kevlar and armed with shotguns and assault rifles. The standoff lasted three nights. I killed another one or two, in an attempt to banish them from my house, but only resulted in losing the stairwell. Now, trapped in the upper floors of my fortress, surrounded by men and boys who wanted me dead, and my possessions in their hands, I waited. I waited for them to bring the explosives. By no means would they breach my sanctuary with anything less. I settled in to the corner with my shotgun, and waited for the end.
I would view my experience in Rust as the typical experience of a player who goes it alone. You may find yourself a secluded location, and build your house strong. Craft your weapons to defend yourself from man and beast alike. Sleep comfortable at night, secure in your home, and in your defenses. But they will come. Through the night and the wilderness, the men who wear black will find you, and all that you have made will be as dust.
Find your friends, and bring them close, for only together will you be safe. So that when the men who wear black come to your door, you will be ready.

To play and fully enjoy what Rust has to offer you will need nerves of steel, no small quantity of patience and a demeanour so cool you freeze the very ground you walk on.
The home you build in Rust will be ransacked, your loot will be pilfered and your burglars will not hesitate to plant a hatchet in the back of your skull whilst you sleep.
As you make your way through the world, collecting what few resources you need to survive the coming nights, men will approach you with guns and they will mow you down regardless of how well equipped you are.
What your assailants, burglars and run of the mill harassers do not know is that inside you a demon is growing. A dark abyss that knows only hatred, feels no remorse and craves only vengeance. You will watch from the pitch black of night as your prey revels, thinking they have bested you.
Your vengeance will be swift. You will take everything they hold dear and leave them with only the humiliation of defeat and the regret of having scorned you in the first place.
You fear nothing. You do not forgive. You do not forget. No, you are not anonymous, but something far more malevolent and sinister.
You are a naked man with a rock.

That was my knee jerk reaction when I first started playing and after 40 hours on the game, I maintain a similar stance. I know it isn't a terribly insightful observation, but that is what the game feels like.
Rust has some qualities of both games and while they aren't necessarily intricate at the moment ("it's an alpha") they do function well. Home building is simple and fairly well executed and it feels like a great baseline for it going forward, and there are some details to it currently that show what it could ultimately become. For example, if you insist on making windows, make sure to put some bars on them, less someone uses them as an access point with a conveniently placed staircase outside your abode (a lesson learned from experience). Crafting is straight forward and the system by which you unlock new builds definitely ratchets up the drive for either raiding "rad" towns and the chests/zombies therein, or raiding your fellow players, as either finding blueprints or researching an already constructed item is the only way to learn some things. And just finding the blueprint isn't always the answer. Finding the blueprint for explosive charges is great, but if you or your buddy can't make explosives, it's ultimately useless until you can. This system has potential to create a player trading market, but "trade" is a word that rarely seems to come up among players.
Of course, the biggest aspect of the game is really PVP/PVE as you need to engage in one (or both) of these to really get anywhere. Unfortunately the PVE isn't really there. Period. Yeah there are zombies and aggro animals, but they aren't really that difficult to defeat (most require 1 or 2 arrows) and most of the time fairly easy to avoid. There are some resource fields and lootable chests that are virtually devoid of PVE threats and unless you're a very poor judge of where to place your house, you'll never need it for defense from the environment. I think the best step for the game would be to figure out what direction they want to take the environmental threats and go with it. Get that system up and running and give the game some extra tension and raise the threat level not only for those who prefer PVE, but also for those engaging in PVP. It's one thing to make sure your house is secure from a roving pack of zombies, it's an entirely different thing to have your raiding party be ambushed while you pillage some saps house.
Which of course brings me to PVP. Honestly, it can be really fun, when you get 2 or 3 groups all running for an air drop and an epic firefight breaks out, but the KOS mentality really can ruin the experience. There is nothing more frustrating than being popped in the head twice after calling for "friendly" and putting your hatchet away (yep, melee against a gun, I'm outmatched dude). You want my stuff? Fine, demand it, I'm not going to resist at 2 v 1 with no weapon. Other reviewers have brought this up and I just want to reiterate how bloody stupid and frustrating it is. And in reality, it breeds that same mentality in other people. After being KOS while posing no threat so many times, eventually people will adopt, or quit playing. In either case, or a multitude of others, it's just not cool. People play games for fun or to relax, whats the point in ruining it?
Edit: One more note on KOS and PVP. Some people are completely lacking in class. Laying ambushes after asking for help to get somewhere (fought my way out of that one) then later coming back with your group to raid said friendly players, after which you gloat about your raid. Yeah, tactics like that are valid, but man do they speak volumes. -_-
Overall I have enjoyed a lot about the game, though I've only mentioned some of the things that worked really well for me. I think there is a lot of potential in Rust and if you're on the fence about it, I urge you to at least hang around and see what changes are made. I think with current systems fleshed out and a stronger PVE, plus some attitude improvement on the part of the community (but every game has its jerks) this will be a lot of fun for big groups, small parties, and lone-wolfs.

To play and fully enjoy what Rust has to offer you will need nerves of steel, no small quantity of patience and a demeanour so cool you freeze the very ground you walk on.
The home you build in Rust will be ransacked, your loot will be pilfered and your burglars will not hesitate to plant a hatchet in the back of your skull whilst you sleep.
As you make your way through the world, collecting what few resources you need to survive the coming nights, men will approach you with guns and they will mow you down regardless of how well equipped you are.
What your assailants, burglars and run of the mill harassers do not know is that inside you a demon is growing. A dark abyss that knows only hatred, feels no remorse and craves only vengeance. You will watch from the pitch black of night as your prey revels, thinking they have bested you.
Your vengeance will be swift. You will take everything they hold dear and leave them with only the humiliation of defeat and the regret of having scorned you in the first place.
You fear nothing. You do not forgive. You do not forget. No, you are not anonymous, but something far more malevolent and sinister.
You are a naked man with a rock.

I believe that it states quite a bit when I say that the most fun I have had on this game was when I played in a completely empty community server. I would pay five dollars for this. For twenty, it's a waste of money.

If you are armed, you will get attacked by a lot of people.
If you are trying to find your friends, it will take you like 15-20 minutes to find them since there is no in game map, no compass, no way to tell where you are unless you are by a permanent building.
You die if you are offline and not in your house, when you log out, your character falls asleep. His body appears on the ground sleeping.
Tips and tricks in rust:
First thing you should do in a server is get a lot of wood, like 200. Build a shelter and put a door (automatically locks when you close it) in your shelter, put a sleeping bag, workshop, furnace, and campfire.
Furnace will need some stones which are those rocks you can hatchet at, that is how you collect them.
Once you do that, try to make a hatchet.
Next, kill some hogs (TRY TO GET AWAY FROM WILD ANIMALS UNLESS YOU HAVE A PLATFORM TO BLOCK YOU FROM THEM) to get some food which you can cook in the campfire and some cloth which makes a sleeping bag and clothes.
Cook the food next.
Start killing some zombies, you will need clothes to reduce radiation. Once you kill the zombies, collect the blueprints and use them IMMEDIATELY. Blueprints help you create items. Collect the research kits from the zombies which can be used with the workshop to learn how to make an item by dragging it over the item.
Once you get a pickaxe and a research kit from a zombie, go to your workshop to use your research kit on it so you can learn how to make it.
Try to be friendly to unarmed people unless they attack you. Share your food and help nice people out. Don't trust any armed person unless you know them.

Firstly, when playing this game you must remember, it's in ALPHA. That means it's still undergoing a lot of development so nothing I write is based on playability or glitches. That said, if you choose your graphics setting carefully at the start (there are only 3 options to change) it is pretty good for an Alpha release.
To set the scene, you're a survivor of an apocolypse. The world has been sent back to the stone ages but survivors have a lot of knowledge of 20th-21st century inventions, like guns and buildings.
If you're one of those players who like to reach a goal in a game, this game is not for you. It is ruthless! Actually, it's just that many of the players are ruthless, the game itself just gives you the tools to choose how you want to behave.
When you first spawn, you're almost a caveman. You're naked (only males in this game which is sad for the perverts out there) and you have in your possession a rock (that's your weapon and tool) a couple of bandages and a wooden, fire-based torch. You're in a large world-like environment, similar towalking around the map of Skyrim.
Don't light the torch!
Torches, fires, furnaces etc can easily be seen by other players, especially at night - It makes you a potential target.
The location you spawn in is fairly random but having respawned next to ther players like me, I'm guessing the spawn-points are pretty much pre-decided but that's OK, I'd rather spawn near some noobs with the same limited items than appear in the middle of a gunfight.
The next thing that usually happens for new players is death. That's because most people playing the game don't trust anyone. Not even someone with an almost harmless rock as a weapon. They tend to kill and ask questions later. Don't get upset, it's the nature of the game. You will get used to it.
There is no built-in map, no compass, in fact very little to help new players other than blogs and guides written by other players. Sounds boring doesn't it? Let me assure you, it isn't.
If you only like games where you always gain the upper-hand in a fight, this game is not for you. If you're a rage-quitter, this game will ruin your keyboard from quitting so much. You will get angry, you will make friends (make friends, seriously, if you don't, you will die - a lot) you will feel pride in your achievements and you will become house-proud of a few bits of wood nailed together to make a shack or hut.
Research the game, download and print a map (there are some online) and read the guides. At the very least, read the beginners guide written by a player and hosted on the Steam guides page. Next, you're ready to play.
If you've already played or ignored what I said in the previous paragraph, you died didn't you? Get used to it - In this game, you will die a lot and respawn in pseudo-random locations. The trick is to figure out where you spawned and where you want to be so you can get there.
If you read the guide and survived your first night, here's a few tips to help you move along in the game.
1. Find a place to live
Sounds easy? Not when you have to build it yourself away from too much traffic and close enough to resources to build it quickly. Don't start off planning to build a super-fortress similar to others you're likely to see - You don't have time yet. Build a simple hut (not a shack like the guide suggests) so later you can add to it. Once you have a small home, put a sleeping bad in it. A sleeping bag makes a future respawn point if you leave the game. You do not respawn there if you were killed.
2. Keep warm.
When you kill animal for raw food (every animal give you raw chicken - even a wolf or bear) you also acquire a few by-products like cloth - Make some cloth armour (be honest, they're clothes with a fancy title). It will keep you warm at night so you don't feel the cold but also make you an attractive target during the day as it signifies that you have something worth taking.
3. Make better weapons
You will need them. At the very least make a stone hatchet to improve the speed you acquire resources and replace your rock with it.
3. Grab some blueprints
Let's be honest, we're not all engineers. To learn how to make better things, you need knowledge. in this game, knowledge is power. You gather blueprints from several places including zombies (the black ones usually - harder to kill of course) a few suitcases dotted around and by disassembling an item you acquired from another player you killed.
4. Avoid excessive radiation exposure
Did I mention the game was set in a post-apocolypse? Several areas in the game are radioactive and can cause you harm, especially if/when your 'rad count' exceeds 500. The good news is, the rad count decreases when you're not being microwaved by ambient radiation. I wondered why the game designers would include such no-go areas but it seems there's lots of loot in them. If you can get in and out quickly, you can gather weapons and lots more. There's even a blueprint for a rad suit to make you immune to the stuff.
Beyond that, it's a case of building a better home (or base), making friends online so you have a clan or allies and stay alive as long as you can. You can choose to be a bandit (typically no base as such, just roam around and kill people) or helpful. Personally I try to help. because I've had my face blown off enough times to learn how much it hurts.
There are many new elements being added to the game (like cars - they're planned for a future release) and always something new to learn. You can talk in public via text-chat (visible to everyone) or you can talk verbally (nearby players only). Usually, clan members and allies will talk privately on Skype etc but you'll soon figure it out.
Many common questions I've read and replied to include:
1. How do I cook food?
Kill an animal, get some raw meat, build a campfire, look at the campfire and when it says "Use", press and hold the "E" key. This opens a small, sub-menu and allows you to use your mouse to click "Open". Add raw food (I suggest 2 chicken per spare slot) and some wood (1 piece will cook 2 pieces of chicken in each slot - giving up to 6 pieces for 1 piece of wood). Light the fire and wait till it goes out, then the food is cooked and safe to eat.
2. Is there a map?
No. Not in the game itself, read above and find one online.
3. How do I know where I am?
More importantly, how do you know which way you're facing? The sun will tell you this. It rises in the east, sets in the west and typically a game-day last 45 minutes, the night lasts 15 minutes. To figure out "where" you are, run down the road and find a common landmark. You can usually work out where you are on the map once you find one. To help work out the direction you're travelling, if the road seems to bear to the right, you're usually travelling clockwise handy to know if the sun is overhead and you have no idea which way is east/west.
4. How do I craf something?
Open your inventory (press the TAB key). At the top of the screen is a crafting option to open the menu. From here, you can select items to make and also determine what resources you need to make any item you're aware of.
5. Can I go to one server, craft something and bring it here?
No. Each server is a self-contained world. You can play on multiple servers if you want, you cannot transfer resources between them.
Overall, I love this game even though I'm really bad at playing it. I was never fantastic at shoot-em-ups but I love playing them. If you don't like dying (a lot) - this game is not for you - If you like a challenge, you will love this! Friends, enemies and bob-the-builder all rolled into one!
