I'm about to describe my first 7 hours in Rust.
I spawned somewhere, and quickly started gathering wood and stone. I eventually built up my inventory to have a stone hatchet and a bow. I was pretty proud of myself. I started constructing a shelter with foundations, then pillars, walls and lastly a ceiling. I then placed the metal door on my home securing me from the outside world. I felt safe.
During a night I heard something outside of my door. "Is there anybody in there?" They said, claiming they were friendly. I reluctantly opened the door and he stepped inside, bare naked, telling me he wanted some safety throughout the night. We went seperate ways after an exchange of goods.
The sun began to rise and I heard more footsteps. It was a very well geared up player, who gave me a pickaxe. I was extremely impressed with how some other people were treating me. With the generous gift off a pickaxe, I developed my inventory quite well. I clothed my character and I crafted a pipe shotgun with 40 shells.
I was ready to go out into the world and help others the way they helped me. I came across some struggling players who were being chased by wolves, so I killed the wolves and gave them some cooked chicken to set them on their way.
I felt things were going well. But things were about to change.
I came across a player with a gun. My heart started racing as I ran into the nearest abandoned shelter for cover. He was firing on me and I was terrified. With a stroke of luck I dealt the lethal blow and I survived. After coming so close to death I started to run back home, as fast as I could, but when I got there I noticed something strange.
There was a man breaking down my door. I slowly approached him and blasted him in the back of the head, moving inside of the house and shutting the door. After a few minutes I felt the area was clear and opened the door.
His friends were waiting for me. That's when I died. I lost everything
10/10

So I bought RUST on steam a few days ago now. Basically, for the uninformed, it's a game where you're put on an island with zombies and told to survive. You have to harvest wood, stone, and metal to make tools and weapons that get progressively more advanced. Now, you can build a home, but homes can be broken into and destroyed by other players while you're not even on the game.

Rust.
What to say, really.  You start out with nothing except obstacles before you.  Find resources, find food, make shelter - survive.  Games like this really bring out the worst in people.  When you die, you lose everything since it stays where you died.  The majority of your deaths will be from other players.  Simply because they're little boys with magnifying glasses and you're an ant that can scream and run.  In the case of Rust, that ends up being a metaphor for them having shotguns and automatic rifles while you have a rock or hatchet.  Sometimes a bow.  It brings out the worst in people because those people delight in needless, consequence free cruelty, and in this setting can justify it as 'survival'.

That being said, you also get to see some of the great aspects of humanity.  The coming-togetherness where a group of individuals struggles against the odds to actually help one another and build towards something.  There's a really neat connection formed in a joint struggle such as Rust.  As many a**holes as I've met, I'm met more decent people, if not outright friendly and helpful ones.
As much as this game will♥♥♥♥♥♥you off, I have also found it to be fairly addictive.  There is an amount of masochism involved in that opinion, but it's a game experience you don't get many other places.  Even in its alpha stage, it is very much playable and really has very few bugs or glitches that I've noticed.  There is still the occassional a**hat speedhacker, but Valve is theoretically cracking down on that with VAC.
If you buy this expect to be defeated time and again, simply because some little boy can do so with little effort.  But also expect to meet some people that will genuinely want to work with you and help you to create something together.
Besides, it's awfully satisfying to cornhole a naked man with an arrow as he runs away, his attempt to bash your skull in with a rock having failed.
If you do buy it, and I would suggest it to a lot of people, just make efforts to have an ingame buddy or 5.  You won't get far on your own.
And if you want to keep it, make sure it has a metal door.

The game was great, really, both legacy and the "new" version. It was so great that i could close an eye about most of the issues (like animals clipping everywhere). Now, i've no idea about what's going on, the devs changed their mind and stopped hearing the community, taking Rust to a slow death.

Great Game

Rust is a survival game where your only goal is to.. well.. survive in a radiated wasteland. You first start out with a rock, which you can use to gather materials like wood and stone. You can then begin crafting tools, armor, base parts, even guns.
Around the world, you can find randomly generated structures that can contain loot. Sometimes it could be just something kinda useless like a flare, but it could also be something pretty damn good like an M4. You can also get attachments for most of your guns, like Supressors, Laser Sights, Flashlights and Reflex Sights. You can also find some good loot on enemies such as Mutant Bears/Wolves and other players.
Speaking of players, one of the only real bad things about this game is the horrible community. It is full of hackers, cheaters, and complete idiots. Most of the players will murder you for no reason at all. Not for loot, not for fun, not for defense, just because they can. You can be killed by a fully amored player with an M4 within 5 seconds of spawning in for the first time.
Overall, this game is good, but it is just completely ruined by the horrible community. If you play on an empty/PvE server, it's pretty damn fun though, but if you play on a full server that allows PvP, you'd suddenly begin to hate this game and wonder why you bought it.
Sweet game, tho needs a lot of work

This is a "POV review"  just a basic recap of why I think this game is not worth it anymore.
I got Rust 3 years ago and when I first played the game it was quite fun especially with the rage at that time being survival fps games. The game pinned you vs the environment, wildlife and ofcourse other players. It wasnt the prettiest or most well optimised game, heck I can even remember when glitching through walls and doors was the BEST way to raid. I miss the zombies they really added something to the game that I miss now, sure they were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ly strong and some were so damn annoyingly fast but I loved huddling up with 10 other guys in a fort we built and constantly having to protect it from other players and having competitions sniping zombies. Then they got rid of the zambies and updated everything the ui graphics map's all that jazz the game ran way worse I felt for a long time and then through the weekly updates the last year and a half to two years actually started to look like it could be fun. I would hop in and out of the game at various stages in development and honestly I just never felt like the game was as fun as it was when it first came onto the scene. It looked better every time I came back to it and had more content but sortof lost it's soul and with that it's playerbase also. The comradery and the team effort seamed to fade everyone just popping into the game now and then to see whats up make some new gizmo and then get bored and leave. I dont know if it is because the game is broken at it's core (the concept) or if the development of the game is simply not ambitious enough but it feels like this game has been in early access for 3 years and will be until the day it fizzles out and dies. I have good memories in this game I was very hyped for it's release sadly now it feels like a empty shell trying to cash in on slight increments of improvement

This is a "POV review"  just a basic recap of why I think this game is not worth it anymore.
I got Rust 3 years ago and when I first played the game it was quite fun especially with the rage at that time being survival fps games. The game pinned you vs the environment, wildlife and ofcourse other players. It wasnt the prettiest or most well optimised game, heck I can even remember when glitching through walls and doors was the BEST way to raid. I miss the zombies they really added something to the game that I miss now, sure they were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ly strong and some were so damn annoyingly fast but I loved huddling up with 10 other guys in a fort we built and constantly having to protect it from other players and having competitions sniping zombies. Then they got rid of the zambies and updated everything the ui graphics map's all that jazz the game ran way worse I felt for a long time and then through the weekly updates the last year and a half to two years actually started to look like it could be fun. I would hop in and out of the game at various stages in development and honestly I just never felt like the game was as fun as it was when it first came onto the scene. It looked better every time I came back to it and had more content but sortof lost it's soul and with that it's playerbase also. The comradery and the team effort seamed to fade everyone just popping into the game now and then to see whats up make some new gizmo and then get bored and leave. I dont know if it is because the game is broken at it's core (the concept) or if the development of the game is simply not ambitious enough but it feels like this game has been in early access for 3 years and will be until the day it fizzles out and dies. I have good memories in this game I was very hyped for it's release sadly now it feels like a empty shell trying to cash in on slight increments of improvement

Do you like survival games?
Do you like crafting, and building your own fortress?
Do you like to amass your resources until you can mount a raid in retaliation against someone who has wronged you?
Then you've come to the right place.
First, let me say this... Rust is still in Alpha. However, if you've played an Alpha before--you know just how incomplete a game can be at that stage of development. Rust, in it's current iteration is FAR from perfect, but it is miles ahead of any game in Alpha, that I've been allowed to play to date.  This game is a MASSIVE undertaking... with tons of content, and MILES of terrain to explore.  (My estimates say about 25 - 40 square miles at least.)
Second, The player driven politics that take place on every server, from the naked, all the way up to the Kevlar--in a unique world that WE create, is reason enough to play this game.
This is a game where death truly matters... where you will lose all items, and loot on your body, when killed... and your corpse is free for the picking by any passers by... and when you Log out... YOU'RE STILL NOT SAFE. Your body simply lies on the ground "asleep" with all items therein to be looted, if someone kills you whilst you slumber.
Third... Because Death is truly meaningful in this game.. revenge never tasted so sweet.  When you successfully hold-back a team of raiders, or even a pair of cloth-armor-bandits trying to stick you with arrows and 9mm ammo... the adrenaline rush is indescribable.  IF YOU DO NOT DEFEND YOURSELF YOU WILL LOSE IT ALL.  What an incredible survival instinct this game has captured.
Fourth... Building a base, your way.
This game would be amazing if it ONLY had the above features... but in addition, you can build a fortress, a village, nay... an EMPIRE.  If you play your cards right, and you actually help people along the way... They may later want to be your ally, when they too have become powerful.  When you form an alliance, it shows TRUE trust--for they can always turn on you, and take your PH4T-LOOTZ. So the feeling of teamwork, when a true ally is found, is also indescribable.  It's like feeling love for the first time. When you find another truly DECENT player out there in the wastes... you keep them close. You protect them with your life. You share your shelter, and your food... and who knows... maybe one day they'll be nice enough to drop you a full suit of Kevlar armor and an M4, when you log on to find that someone has Raided your base, and looted your treasure?
To conclude, the actual GAME CONCEPT of this title is absolutely superb.
Once they iron out the hackers and scriptkiddies...
There is no doubt in my mind that this will be one of the Greatest PC Games of this Generation.
Here's to you, Gary.

What else can I say....This is a great game! I spent the last several weeks reading reveiws both negative and positive and heavily debated buying this game at 20.00 due to it being an Alpha. It's all about WHERE you build your place at and how obviously it sticks out...that's going to determin how much attention your place gets....If you build a 4 or 5 story tower...your probably going to get looted. Hide your place in the mountains....In the thick woods or next to a Rad Town (you have to deal with the zombies though). I see the game being an all time classic and with it being only in it's infancey already has a huge number of addicted players (me included) and I can only imagine where it will be in a year from now. Good things already and Great things to come for this game!   Highly recomended!

This game is extremely difficult to reccomend for a lot of reasons. It's lack of content is mildly excusable due to the fact that it's still in Alpha, however, it has major repurcussions throughout most of the other gripes I have with the game. Nevertheless, I do enjoy Rust, and for the sake of giving Rust a fighting chance, I'll cover pros first.
First and foremost, Rust has a lot of potential to it, which is why I chose to reccomend the game. According to the Steam page, this game is likely to change dramatically, however, whatever direction they choose to take Rust seems like it has some serious value to it. The freedom of crafting and building your own structures maintains a pleasant element of variety, and the buildings being server dependant allow a different experience between each server. Unfortunately, Rust has a long way to go before it can be valued as a reasonable purchase, and any purchase in its current state is a gamble. I reccomend it because I feel that the game has taken off to a point where progression to a full-fledged, fully fleshed-out game is imminent.
In sharp contrast, the game does reek of cons, and many of them stem from either the community, or the outright lack of content. Progression in Rust is fast, and later in the game, assuming you survive long enough, it rapidly becomes a grind-fest to gather wood, metal, and sulfur to further expand your fort, or build weapons and explosives to attack other players (who likely have already gathered these materials for you). Because gathering necessary materials such as food and tools becomes so easy so quickly, the game naturally drives you towards killing and raiding other players, not out of necessity, but out of boredom. The PVE elements of Rust are virtually non-existant a mere hour or two into the game, as any hostile NPCs such as bears, wolves, and zombies are easlity taken care of by a shotgun blast, and conventional weapons can be found quite literally everywhere. Furthermore, this abundance of weapons and ammo often leads to players having weapons, but lacking materials such as food, causing them to have no choice but to simply kill other players on sight because they need the materials. This vicious cycle often leads to Rust being an outright deathmatch, at the game doesn't just lack an incentive not to kill other players, it gives encouragement. There's nothing to be gained by sparing other players, aside from a better reputation, and the loot often outweight the risk, and often times you can be killed simply because the player who killed you had nothing better to do aside from chopping hundreds of wood piles.
Cons considdered, I still reccomend picking up Rust, perhaps at a later date. The game has a great potential, but it doesn't warrant a $20 purchase unless you thoroughly enjoy a survival/PVP experience with a fast system of progression. The game needs work.

Started from the bottom now we here...
From the very first moment of playing this game, I knew it was going to be something special. I loaded into a random server full of people I had never met, most were friendly (I'm sure it was due to the fact that nobody had anything and we were all still using large rocks as tools), few were actually dangerous (Again, due to the fact the we had nothing and it would have been a waste of ammo to kill us), and there were the, "Wanna build a house together?", kind of folks.
You load in essentially naked with a large rock as your tool and weapon, a torch, and a couple bandages. The bare essentials more or less. From that point on, there is no tutorials, no missions, nothing; the object is to survive.. In doing so, it was determined that we would need to find animals to kill (food), cut a few trees down (Shelter), and sew together some cloth and other odd and ends (Clothes/Sleeping Bag). If  you can nail those basic needs before it gets dark, then you're on the right track. From there the idea is to amass copius amounts of resources and begin construction on a "tower", or any other sketchily* constructed building you can conjure up.
Playing it solo is very fun, but if you're a newcomer to survival games such as this one, grab a couple of friends to assist you in getting the necessary materials and items faster off of the start. It's a dangerous world out there, you never know if a raider is watching your ever move, waiting for oyu to slip up, or the seemingly harmless nude fellow outside your shack really needs your help, or if he's just abiting you outside so him and his friends can kill you and take your life over. apart from other players, the walking dead and wildlife render and endless challenge (Until you get repellant(Shotguns)).
Rust™ remains in it's Alpha Stage as of now with almost daily updates tweaking this or that to make your experience as clean as possible. This title has a few nice benefits such as being quite small for the type of game, sitting at just under 1gb, it's not taking up much space at all; running it is a non issue provided you have a system dating back within at least 4 years; and one of my loved attributes to any game; an easily navigated legacy browser (Not to mention simple console controls). **For just $20, even the light spenders can find the funds for this gem.
Hands down, I have to say the Rust™ smashes a easy 10/10

Rust is an open world PvP sandbox in which you must survive. Build your base, hunt animals, scavenge ruins for loot and live to see another dawn. Think Minecraft crossed with Day Z.
The idea and, for the most part, execution is brilliant. Considering this is in alpha, it looks stunning and the crafting system is intuitive enough, and will at least tell you what you need to make something. I spent hours crafting walls, forging my weapon and ammo to survive in this unforgiving land. The community was helpful and we thrived, made fun of each other and traded. It was a great time.
Then, one day I was running home and a bloke shot me, with five of his mates. All my loot gone, for no reason. I respawned in my house neaby, only to have the wall blown off and bed murdered yet again, my sleeping bag destroyed and my spawn point lost. This is what will make Rust fail; the overly toxic community. Fine, steal my stuff. I get PvP, it's a survival game and no one is safe. But destroying the sleeping bag is deliberately being a prick for the sake of it. It's actions like this, and people who don't want to go to a PvE server and fight against the bandit players (because your stuff can still be blown up in a PvE environment) that will fracture the playerbase in to the Lord Of The Flies 'kill anyone you can see' attitude. The idea of game is that you can progress. With relatively little effort, prospective months of progress can be lost when you're not even online and the hours will count for nothing. This is the one major flaw with Rust.
The rest, however, is fantastic. Get on a PvE, no sleeper server and log off with all your valuables on you and fall in love with a beautiful survival game that will suck away your weekend.

Rust is an open world PvP sandbox in which you must survive. Build your base, hunt animals, scavenge ruins for loot and live to see another dawn. Think Minecraft crossed with Day Z.
The idea and, for the most part, execution is brilliant. Considering this is in alpha, it looks stunning and the crafting system is intuitive enough, and will at least tell you what you need to make something. I spent hours crafting walls, forging my weapon and ammo to survive in this unforgiving land. The community was helpful and we thrived, made fun of each other and traded. It was a great time.
Then, one day I was running home and a bloke shot me, with five of his mates. All my loot gone, for no reason. I respawned in my house neaby, only to have the wall blown off and bed murdered yet again, my sleeping bag destroyed and my spawn point lost. This is what will make Rust fail; the overly toxic community. Fine, steal my stuff. I get PvP, it's a survival game and no one is safe. But destroying the sleeping bag is deliberately being a prick for the sake of it. It's actions like this, and people who don't want to go to a PvE server and fight against the bandit players (because your stuff can still be blown up in a PvE environment) that will fracture the playerbase in to the Lord Of The Flies 'kill anyone you can see' attitude. The idea of game is that you can progress. With relatively little effort, prospective months of progress can be lost when you're not even online and the hours will count for nothing. This is the one major flaw with Rust.
The rest, however, is fantastic. Get on a PvE, no sleeper server and log off with all your valuables on you and fall in love with a beautiful survival game that will suck away your weekend.

Rust is an open world survival game that runs on servers rather than multiplayer, adding an interesting twist on the gameplay. It's a game that whilst many people complain of its lack of safety and its constant PvP, disallowing you from any sort of steady and safe gameplay, I believe that Rust is a game that really displays human instinct at it's purest. WHen faced with a situation where the other person has a gun, and might either be trying to make peace or trying to kill you, your instincts tend to give you the choices to react, rather than your logical thinking, making quite interesting and tense gameplay, especially when every corner you turn could be your last, depending on what you find around it.
The game is by no means faced paced or action based, although certain situations may require some fast thinking before you get shot for all of your items. The game primarily revolves around collecting resources to build a house to survive the various enemies in the open world, and to defend yourself from any wandering players who may fancy an extra item or two in their backpack, preying on the newer players. Form relationships and alliances with other players, build a house together, topossibly get backstabbed and stolen from later on! Hire somebody as a mercenary, and loot radiation zones full of zombies together! Be a bandit and blow your way through other players' doors with explosive charges to get at their secret stash of guns and loot! Build and impregnable metal fortress in the center of a field, commanding attention and respect from all! Or build your house far out of the resource zone in the barren plateau, or high up in the mountains where nobody would ever find you! The possibilities are endless in the massive world of Rust.

Rust is an amazing game that offers a wide range of ways to enjoy it. If you have a "me against the world" mentality, then you can play it that way. If you enjoy playing with others and being part of a team, you can do that here. If you just simply want to be a villian and ruin other people's games, then it's a possibility. There are no rules, no force fed objectives, only possibilities in this game and it's up to you to decide what's important, where to start, and what path you take.
The idea of building yourself, or your team to a status of being able to run the Rust world, is interesting to say the least. You can gather tons of resources, food, weapons, ammunition, and tools, all of which help you build your supremacy in the game. It's not just about obtaining those resources, but it's also about keeping those resources safe against other players in the game. not only are there other players out there looking to take what you got, you also have to navigate an unforgiving world full of zombies, bears, wolves, and mother nature herself. If you like a challenge, this game is for you and remember, it's still only in alpha so I am expecting this game to grow into something iconic.

Rust is an open world survival game that runs on servers rather than multiplayer, adding an interesting twist on the gameplay. It's a game that whilst many people complain of its lack of safety and its constant PvP, disallowing you from any sort of steady and safe gameplay, I believe that Rust is a game that really displays human instinct at it's purest. WHen faced with a situation where the other person has a gun, and might either be trying to make peace or trying to kill you, your instincts tend to give you the choices to react, rather than your logical thinking, making quite interesting and tense gameplay, especially when every corner you turn could be your last, depending on what you find around it.
The game is by no means faced paced or action based, although certain situations may require some fast thinking before you get shot for all of your items. The game primarily revolves around collecting resources to build a house to survive the various enemies in the open world, and to defend yourself from any wandering players who may fancy an extra item or two in their backpack, preying on the newer players. Form relationships and alliances with other players, build a house together, topossibly get backstabbed and stolen from later on! Hire somebody as a mercenary, and loot radiation zones full of zombies together! Be a bandit and blow your way through other players' doors with explosive charges to get at their secret stash of guns and loot! Build and impregnable metal fortress in the center of a field, commanding attention and respect from all! Or build your house far out of the resource zone in the barren plateau, or high up in the mountains where nobody would ever find you! The possibilities are endless in the massive world of Rust.

Rust was less than impressive in the screenshots I saw but let me assure you, the screenshots don't do the game justice.  While there are many areas in which the game can improve (such as the "split" ability asking how much you want to split off instead of just splitting your pile in two), it is very impressive and fun for a game in alpha.  I wish the game started you off with a topological map and compass (or at least gave you the option to find or craft them) as it can be fairly easy to get lost while learning the land around you and can also prove to be a challenge to find friends (assuming you're not playing alone).
The social aspect of this game is enjoyable, but not nearly as fleshed out as in DayZ.  When you find other players you are stuck with voice commands to communicate (or you can chat via text if you don't have a microphone).
The crafting in the game is well done--it is easy to see exactly what you need (resources) to build whatever item, and any item you don't have the ability to craft can be found and then you can use a research kit on it so that you can build it in the future (this provides a way to restrict the use of better items until you've spent some time with the game).
In the end I have found this to be a very fun game to play and can't wait to see how the game develops in time.

Things I've learned while playing Rust:
1) As they very clearly warn you, it's an alpha game.  At the time of writing (Dec 31st release of the Alpha), the Developers seem to be more focused on the environment and mechanics of the sandbox, and less focused on content.  There's not much to do once you've built your base up and raided every other home, except pick another server and do it all again.  I did this on three different servers before I got bored.  That said, the game itself seems relatively free of major bugs.  There are plenty of minor bugs to be found, but they don't really have any effect on the outcome or possible enjoyment of the game.
2) There are far too many hackers.  It takes way too much effort to build up a supposedly "safe" base only to have it griefed and/or ruined by no-clippers and wall-hack thieves.  I expect people to do legitimate raids (I know I do), but you are powerless against hackers.  It takes several hours of play time to acquire enough resources to build a secure home, and hackers can undo all your work in a matter of seconds.  If you're lucky, they will only kill your sleeping body and steal your stuff.  If you're not, they'll wall off access to your base and you won't be able to use it again. You can't adjust parts of your base without obnoxious amounts of explosives...
3)  As with all open PvP games, "there's safety in numbers" in this world as well.  If you have more friends to play with you, it's likely that you will have a good time raiding other people's homes and wreaking havok until you get bored.  If you're solo, you had better be a good negotiator, a really good shot, really sneaky, or some reasonable combination.
In short, it is a novel idea, but it is not fleshed out enough at this time.  Maybe check it out in a few months.

Currently Rust is in a VERY early alpha. The game is currently broken, in a number of different ways, and many people are having issues even looking for a server without crashing. From the standpoint of PvE, the game is entirely easy and it takes very minimal effort to stay alive past the first few days. Enemies and hazards are few and far between, and so laughably avoidable or killed that you genuinely don't have to worry, so long as you've had the foresight to build a hatchet or bow. Servers reset frequently with even small updates, though, so you will lose everything you've spent time building/collecting and it feels like pulling teeth. The game is also very rough and explains nothing, so your first few hours will be frustrating and hard without a companion who knows what they're doing, and that's IF you find a community server that doesn't have terrible latency or weird settings.

Wait until it either hits late beta or goes gold, then re-assess whether or not it's worth the purchase at that time.

As an Early Access game Rust may push away certain audiences, as the game is incomplete with more than a few bugs, hackers and an apparent weakness to DDOS'ers. However, putting the $20 into the game allows one to mark the significant changes that are made as it shifts and evolves with the community. Patience, skill and luck is needed to survive the onslaught, and to establish oneself in this open world survivor-crafting game.
The game really shines once you begin to understand the lay of the land, the tendencies of people to loot specific areas and how to exploit peoples kindness or their ego. Crafting and building a house is risky, and rewarding. It's fantastic to see how well a bit of thought goes in protecting valuables and one's own sleeping body. The combat is beyond satisfying, allowing for constant replayability and the hilarity of clan-based raiding or griefing will keep you coming back. Finding your first pistol, or C4 charge will give you a huge buzz. Decisions of whether to shoot and kill that player to gain their gear, while possibly drawing other players, or to conserve ammo bring a similar feeling to DayZ.
However, the lack of things to do beyond PVP or crafting may push people away, as the frustration of constant deaths and being unable to establish themselves hinders the full enjoyment of the game (Seeing things from the other perspective). The atmosphere isn't one of creepiness or desolation, rather one of open exploration and 'should I kill this person', which again may be offputting.
The game is constantly evolving and new things are added often. The developers are constantly in communication with the community to add new and improved features. It's definitely worth the $20. As someone who has tracked it since closed Alpha I will continue to jump on with my mates and pick a few fights, build a few forts and get involved in a fantastic indie development title.

Things I've learned while playing Rust:
1) As they very clearly warn you, it's an alpha game.  At the time of writing (Dec 31st release of the Alpha), the Developers seem to be more focused on the environment and mechanics of the sandbox, and less focused on content.  There's not much to do once you've built your base up and raided every other home, except pick another server and do it all again.  I did this on three different servers before I got bored.  That said, the game itself seems relatively free of major bugs.  There are plenty of minor bugs to be found, but they don't really have any effect on the outcome or possible enjoyment of the game.
2) There are far too many hackers.  It takes way too much effort to build up a supposedly "safe" base only to have it griefed and/or ruined by no-clippers and wall-hack thieves.  I expect people to do legitimate raids (I know I do), but you are powerless against hackers.  It takes several hours of play time to acquire enough resources to build a secure home, and hackers can undo all your work in a matter of seconds.  If you're lucky, they will only kill your sleeping body and steal your stuff.  If you're not, they'll wall off access to your base and you won't be able to use it again. You can't adjust parts of your base without obnoxious amounts of explosives...
3)  As with all open PvP games, "there's safety in numbers" in this world as well.  If you have more friends to play with you, it's likely that you will have a good time raiding other people's homes and wreaking havok until you get bored.  If you're solo, you had better be a good negotiator, a really good shot, really sneaky, or some reasonable combination.
In short, it is a novel idea, but it is not fleshed out enough at this time.  Maybe check it out in a few months.

I really enjoy Rust, and altough the community is a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is actually finding a good server the most difficult part, but when you have it, it's really REALLY fun.

I nominate this game for "The test of time" award, seeing as it only keeps getting better and better. Oh and I must say, I actually have to have surgery because of this game...I'll explain, gather 'round the fire children, I got a story to tell.
It was many years ago when Rust first came out and I got it on steam, I was new to these survival-type games and wasn't sure what I was getting myself into, since i'm not so much a fan of pvp but I thought, well it might have pve servers too (which is does) but back then, I wanted the full experience and just jumped right into an official server.
I started off naked, in what appeared to be a forest and it was dark, and I mean, pitch black. I couldn't see♥♥♥♥♥♥
I ran around, thinking maybe my screen is just bugged or something since it was my first time trying the game, but then I noticed a glimmering red/yellow/orange light way in the distance and I said, "Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥ maybe someone is over there who can help me since my character sounds like he's freezing to death."
I ran over there, the light from the fire growing bigger and bigger revealing a 1x1 shack, the original Rust homestead.( i miss it) and I could hear people talking, in what I believe was an Austrailian accent. I had a headset so I started talking to them and i told them I was a new player to the game, and if I could stay inside their tiny home for the night so i dont freeze to death, then when the Sun rises I will leave and be forever thankful.
They agreed and were nice enough to even give me some crafted clothes and some food, too!
Now, what transpired next would affect me for a few years and now requires me to have surgery for an 'Umbilical Hernia' which I didn't have prior to this encounter, but I have it now and have to have surgery for it at some point...so here's what happened.
There was two of them, the Aussies, and just me by my lonesome...We were all squished inside their shack and they had 1 basic chest to store items in that I saw....it was at this very moment that the true meaning of the game was revealed to me, as if God spoke directly to me and explained the meaning of Life.
I must remind you, at this time of the game whoever placed the door on the home, was the only 1 able to open it, so at the moment I was essentially trapped inside with them, so I couldn't steal their stuff and just stand there, they would have murdered me surely i thought to myself...so I waited.
Each passing moment, they kept their eyes on me, 1 Aussie was standing directly on the chest (because there was not much room in the shack) and the other was directly infront of the door, and me in a corner.
I was able to see outsie through one of the cracks in their shacks walls, and i came up with a fool-proof plan....when the I noticed it wasn't completely dark anymore and knew I'd be able to see where I was going, I asked the Aussie near the door if he could open the door and let me know if it was light out (which I already knew it was, but I just wanted to make sure 1 obsticle[him blocking my escape/the door] was out of the way) So he opens it, steps outside, but the moment he opened the door I was already across the room (which is like half a foot away) and inside their chest, I took everything in record time...
The Aussie ontop of the chest immediately realized what I was doing, while the Aussie outside was enjoying the Sunrise, and I ran out the open door as fast as I could....I ran so fast, I could hear them in-game swearing and cursing me and saying they will find and murder me, but I was replying "I'm sorry! I'm Canadian, I don't usually do this type of stuff!" All the while I am laughing harder than I've ever laughed before and directly after I noticed that IRL my stomach was sort of hurting....apparently I got an Umbilical Hernia from laughing too hard...
If you ever hear someone say "Bust a gut laughing" well, now you know someone who actually has, and now, because of Rust I have to have surgery someday since Hernia's don't just go away lol...I think it was worth it though. Hope you enjoyed this story, because it's actually 100% true.

It's a vert well concepted game with a ton of room for innovation, and improvement.   Of course, it has issues ranging from hackers, to visual bugs, but this is honestly to be expected in any form of alpha, whaever game. Only new, and better things can come from it.

- Community:  Everyone is complanining about the community.  But from 150 hours into this game so far, I can easily tell you that this is due to people not giving an effort.  The odds of being kos'd upon spawning is very minimal, and to avoid this the NUMBER ONE thing you can do is to create a group.  Roll with some buddies on your friends list, or make some in game.   When I went into this game, none of my friends played this game  I've made friends with some prettty damn cool people since then, and I don't even have a mic. It's all about player interaction, choose what you'd like to do with it.  (Quick note: I personally don't experience people who don't have guns out kos'ing me)
- Fighting:  Fighting in this game is like no other.  It's one of those few games where your ability to kill isn't determined by your gear.   In this game, kill of getting killed is determined by deception, and skill.  Many people won't waste bullets on killing a presumabely new spawn.  Run up naked, rock in hand, get close and blast them.  In a firefight, it's all about the aim.  Someone wit the best gear in the game can be killed by someone who has better skill with the recoil, and the sway.
- Housing:  Making your own base is absolutely awesome!!  You can design it however you please, and the possibilities are endless.  Also, you can look through cracks in the wood to see whatever is inside said wall, window, doorway, etc.
- Raiding: Raiding is absolutely amazing, especially when they're online.  Firefights, planting c4 on doors, cover fire.  It's all fun, and very much enjoyable.
- Sleeping upon logging out: This feature is one of the best and most bistinguishable between Rust and DayZ (I haven't played Dayz Standalone yet) It prevents combat logging, and makes and incorporates an interesting aspect on base building and protection.
- How long does it last? (Late game?): Best feature of this game is the longevity of it.  It's completely replayable, and it takes a while to get blueprints for all of the advanced gear in the game.
- Extra Features:  Then there are many more features, crafting, airdrops, etc.  which adds to the game, and things to do.
==CONS==
- Hackers: Hackers are ruining this game accross the board.  Atleast community servers have admins to filter out some of them, but it's still an issue.  I believe that FacePunch needs to make an anti-cheat of their own, steam VAC is good and all.  But in those days where it doesn't insta-ban, and just records to ban on a certain day, hackers can wreak havoc.

- Official Server Uptime:  A lot of the larger Official servers which will have a (Stress Test) to them are very unstable, and it's unfortunately the only official game servers that have 200+ people.
- Can't think of any more major ones.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Overall:  A good game that has things coming for it, but potentially game ruining things at the moment. (Mainly Hackers)

From my first hour of playing Rust, I've learnt that a rock is your source of survival and that other players are complete tools. Upon first spawning in the world, it was night so I couldn't seen a thing and then I noticed a red pointer on the screen which indicated something was hitting me. Before I could do anything, I was killed within my first 10 seconds of playing the game. Because of this, the game gave off the impression that the spawn system was faulty and needed improving.
After joining another server it was day time so I could actually see what was going on and observe my surroundings. From the world, you will mostly see big rocks, trees and little huts scattered around everywhere. After walking around for a few minutes, my Minecraft senses kickedin and I knew what I needed to do, I needed a little hut like everyone else. From the ingame inventory you can access a crafting menu which lists all the game's tools and structures. From analysing the crafting menu, I knew I needed a few things, a hut, fire and food. From there I started my journey to collect enough wood to build a shelter and chase animals around a forest with a rock trying to gain some meat. After a tough 30 minutes, I finally had what I needed and started to build my first shelter. In the crafting menu, you can either build the small hut or build wall pieces for creating your own buildings, so being the lazy guy I am, I built myself a hut. Then I set my meat onto the open caampfire and sat inside my hut enjoying my experience...that's until a hacker noclipped through my wall and killed me.
Seriously, when games like this release with so much potential, why do players set out to ruin it. The community is ruining games like Rust and DayZ with it's stupid hacking. Just sit the ♥♥♥♥ back and play the game the way it's meant to be played.
Overall, Rust is still in early Alpha and will have bugs and a pathetic playerbase, but if you look past this, you will easily enjoy it.

Think "Minecraft with better graphic" and you've got a pretty good idea of what this game offers in gameplay.
Making a review about a game, which is in Alpha is not an easy thing to do, since many things can change, for either better or worse. But as it is, the game is enjoyable to play with friends. But I'll try to make a review anyways.
Many a good thing can be said about it, the graphics are pretty, even beautiful some times. The crafting system is easy to understand and easy to do, and within the first hour, you've got a house to live in, if you're on the right server that is. Weapons, food, tools, all these can be crafted, but for some of these items, you need a permenant house, where you can craft it, using furnace and workbence. Just like in Minecraft.
However, where you might think you're safe when you log out, like in DayZ or Minecraft, here your character can still be kill, looted and your home destroyed. This makes the game more interesting, since now, building a house won't be enough but you'll have to think about where to build it. This makes you carefully consider where to build, and where to gather resources since the world necessarily isn't a friendly place. The amount of wildlife is interesting, with Bears and Wolfs to be respectful of, and Deer and wild Pigs to actively hunt for food and skin. The wildlife is a danger in its own right. Bears and wolfs stalk the forest and fields, and will hunt a player regardless if hungry or not. Along with these, zombies, both slow and fast will hunt a player aswell.
However, as enjoyable this game is, there are some problems which isn't surprising since this is an Alpha of the game, and there are sure to be many more things to be added later on. However, I can put out a list to say what I personally want to be in the game, and what should be changed.
Though the graphics are very good, the ocean texture is the worst I've seen in a long time. I would never go near the ocean to watch the moon rise, or the sun set with water looking as unnaturally as it does in this game.
The crafting and gathering of material from the natural resources which actively spawn in semi-random locations, there are things that could be done to improve these features. It's way too easy. Metal ore and Sulphur ore along with stone is way too easy to gather. Pick up a stone, and you've got it going. Along with the too easy gathering, making weapons and is too easy. Within the first two days, you're running around with guns, and as soon as that's done, one doesn't feel in danger from zombies or animals.
As for the enviroment itself. As it is, it ain't complete. The area is scarcely big enought for 40, let alone 100 players it ain't big enough. Bigger enviroments with a more complete wildlife would make this game so much better. A complete wildlife, with herbivours and predators, a complete foodchain would make the game, not only more enjoyable, but the impact it would have on the players would make people question every situation they're in. Should one try and take out a Bear for a already dead pig or should one wait for the pack to move on to see if there is any leftovers. The competition between players and other predators would make a deep impact and created a heavier situation for the players when confronted by other players. As for the predators already in the game, they aren't fearful enough. One comes across a wolf or a bear, you can outrun it. Nothing fanzy, just sprint. But a bear is strong enough to kill a man with one hit, and a wolf is way faster than a man. If the game is about realistic surviving a post-apocalytic world with radiationposioning a constant threat, the wildlife should have a deeper impact. As for the prey, they are too easy to hunt and kill. One can sneak all the way up to a deer and land the first blow before it runs from you. Though I know improving the wildlife isn't high on the priority list, and knowing that it wouldn't be implementet out of the seare computer power needed to run the game. It is an interesting thought, and a thought I hoped realized in the near future in a survival game.
As for this survival game, I enjoy it. And if one loves the thought of the general survivormode, or have played DayZ or Minecraft before, they'll find this to be an enjoyable game aswell. :)

Rust is a game all about multiplayer. Resource Collect, Build, Craft, Survive or even Raid. Large Map, no compas, no map, pure survival. Dont Eat? Starve. Dont Build? Freeze At Night. All of which will lead to a end result: Be Strong, or be Crushed, by the elements or by that evil foe down the valley.
Rust has a good things going for it, Blue Prints, these you can find by killing Zombies(or zombie like creatures in the game when they take out Zombies). All of which drop a backpack full of loot that u can use for your advantage, like Blue Prints. Blue Prints allow you to study said Blue Print to learn how to craft it. Once it has been Learned, you never forget it even if u die and all ur stuff is raided. Meaning you have a easier start when u try to rebuild. Now this only works Server Side, and will not carry over to other servers.
In big servers, like Offical Servers(Owned by Rust Themselfs), the amount of people in these servers are staggering. Meaning that you have a high chance of just getting Shot by that one dude in full kevlar for no reason. Your base will most likely get raided in the night when you log off. Now this is where u must decided if you want to build a base near resources to mine and collect, or build in the boonies, protecting yourself from the random insurgents coming to knock on your door.
In small community servers(Owned by the Players of Rust), They can be easier to gather resources and maybe just get "Stuck Up" on the roads in rust, instead of the dreaded KOS (Kill on Sight). With less players on, the chance of getting your random house is less due to there are not 100+ people on at a time looking for places to raid.
PvP or PvE? This can be a hard choice to make in rust, most people choose PvP due to they can have fun raiding or even having wars. PvE, there is no Killing other players, but you can steal there base and raid it(while also not being able to protect your base due to you cannot kill that said raider.)
With all of this said, i would give Rust a 3.8/5. Its worth buying and getting addticed to it like every other person. Also it is a step back from DayZ types, where everything is amazing hard. Once Rust has left its Alpha-Beta Phase, the game will most likely get better, as they plan on upgrading the game to a better standpoint from what it is now.

So, lets start things off with the fact that while this game is early access, it is still incredibly fun.
I have played everything, Nether, Day Z, Day Z standalone, and half the other crappy not even worth mentioning survival games. I have to say, while Nether is in early access and the game COULD be fun in the future, This game is early access and it IS fun right NOW, and will be even more fun in the future once they add viechles and more content. Now I will describe the basic impression the game gave me when I started.
You start off with a rock and some medkits. You scatter stuff, get wood, stone ect, you build a shelter to live overnight, a campfire, food from animals.
After you get your basic gear either crafted or found, you go gear hunting. You do that by looting cities that are filled with radiation, or killing other players that have loot, or gathering more material to craft more loot.
Now something about the fact that you raid other people's fortes(houses) and take their gear is just fun. Especially when the people are actually in the house. You take C4 Charges and blow up the door with them, once the door is blown up by C4 you have access inside, but if they are there they will defend, so you use your weapon(hopefully with the scope/laser attachment) and you kill them all, then make sure to kill their sleeping bags so they don't respawn and loot that place! Of course you can do what I've been doing with my friend, get silenced guns and play special ops style, where you sneak around shoot people in the head with a silencer and make sure they never even knew you were coming!
After that you go back to the house that you built, and store the loot you got, hoping no one raids your place while you are away, but if you are good enough at hiding your place where it's hard to find, and make it really hard to get in to such as multiple doors, spikes ect, then the chances of you being raided are really low.
SO to sum it all up, this game is a lot of fun, and the more people you have to play with the more fun it will be, and the further in development this game will be, the more fun it will become as well! I can not wait to see how this game will be with viechles, more weapons, more crafting blue prints, ect! :)

Early Thoughts:
Rust is a truly fun game that is taking a bit of a different viewpoint on the survival genre. No zombies. I love zombies, but there are at least 5 games out currently (in early access) trying to be "THE ZOMBIE" game. Rust has other creatures you have to survive from including wolves and other players.
One interesting mechanic is that your player location is stored on the server and you character still persists after you log out. Making you feel the need to check in on your character to make sure he hasn't been murdered or generally bamboozled.
VOIP is a good feature in this game as it allows you to try to build relations using your own charisma. It doesn't always work and most people will attack you regardless, but there have been a few times where this has saved my life and the player taught me more about the game and how to survive. Thanks Luke! ;)
The most intense moment that I have experienced so far: I saw 2 people meet up in the middle of the field about 50 yards away as I crept through the high grass (naked - as you start the game). One man was naked and the other was fully clothed and in a red shirt. A few tense seconds passed and it felt as if the 2 were friends. Suddenly the red-shirted man shot the naked man and looted his corpse. I was slowly approaching, but then realized I had to get out of dodge. I crept away silently and cried myself to sleep.
Rust is coming along nicely but still has a ways to go to be "THE SURVIVAL GAME" of the century.

This game is perfect. I love the simplicity of it. It's still in alpha, so bugs are expected. I have not seen any bugs so far except for server lag. Yes, they have minor things to adjust, like how someone else holds a rock like a pistol, or how you can only get Raw Chicken Breasts no matter what animal you kill. I love this game. I hope they keep the simplicity of it, but add a lot more features. I give this game a 10/10 because even though it's in alpha, it's still one of the most enjoyable games on Steam. I was hesitant on buying it for $20 while it's still in alpha, but it was worth every penny. You can do so much already. You can craft bows, weapons, and even walls to build houses. You can choose to hunt and gather food while your friends scavenge for supplies. You can get a team or survive solo against other players, zombies, and wildlife. The first few in-game days are pretty difficult. My problem was that I had no idea how to find stone, but I found someone that was able to help. This game is worth it. Every penny. GET IT.

Although this game is still in beta...wait WHAT? It's still in ALPHA?!
Of course you'll notice performance-wise that it is in Alpha-stage (Minimal animations, lack of character variation: we all look the same except when you have clothes on aka NOT NAKED, strange lighting phenomenon in the night, no story, I died once trying to jump through a box that stood in the way of magical "falling" damage, whatever animal you hunt down you'll always get CHICKEN MEAT etc...)
BUT DON'T GET ME WRONG. This game FEELS already AWESOME. You jump into the game, you spawn randomly somewhere in a huge island and immediatly your instincts take over: SURVIVAL. You are searching for food, for resources to make better tools, and with those tools you're trying to make better weapons so you can hunt animals that are faster than you, like a bow taking down a deer from the distance and ultimately make your very own Shelter. Or even a Fortress! Resources like Stone, spawn randomly on the map, I know it doesn't make any sense at first but as I played along it makes very sense: By making the resources few, scarce and rare, it makes you feel really happy to find a mining spot. PLUS there is a plane DROP which contains super rare loot which triggers automatically a race with the other survivor, with other players.
Which makes us jump to the PVP part. This is where this game shines and make you forget that it is still in ALPHA version. This is where your emotions play crazy things with you. One time you play it's very slow paced, everyone you see is minding their own survival bussiness, yes almost calm and relaxing, and the other time you are chilling in your house and suddenly someone is asking if there is "someone in there?" and then you hear hell breaking out: A massive shootout right in front of your house between two gangs!! This intense decision making is very humanish. What do you do? Do you flee? Or do you want to try to ninja loot those gang corpses to find better loot, of risking your own hard earned loot? Do you stay in your house and stay quiet in hope the GANGS don't even realise that you're in there?...But what if you get caught? Even if I get caught maybe they will raid my house and steal everything?...
These intense decision making process is one hell of a emotion rollercoaster experience. The reson you are going through this processes is because you want to outsmart other people, you want to have security to build up your little empire, you want to find friends or enemies to get better loot. Whichever way you may choose, there is one motive that drives you to play more:
IT'S SURVIVAL OF THE FITTEST.

Pros: +The game pace varies everytime HOW you play the game

Rust a great new alpha survival game. You start out with nothing only a rock, some bandages, and a torch. You then gather wood to make a shelter and a campfire. Your warm and safe, but there is a problem you haven't solved, hunger. You run outside with your rock unholstered and brutally murder any living thing outside your nice wooden home. You're so hungry, you almost eat the chicken breast raw. You finally regain sanity and start cooking and waiting in the dark. Outside you hear the moans and woofing of the outside beast. After a few hours of night time, a scream of help is heard from your door, but you hesitate to open it. After a few more noises and scream, it all goes silent. You open your door to find another survivor dead on your doorstep, but you greedily loot him. The next day you come out with bow in hand, crafted from yesterdays battle. You slaughter innocent animals and beast, taking more meat and cloth for yourself. Eventually you come across another shelter. You look at your bow, and into the person inside. This is the part where you decide. Do you become a man of good and wish to help those who also suffer from this world? Or do you choose to slay for your own greed? This is the greatness of Rust. Something that DayZ lacks. So far I give Rust a score of 9.5/10. Even though it's Unity 3D engine is really buggy and laggy, its still a great alpha game.
The only thing I reccomend the developers do is change the engine of the game to something like Unreal or Valve's Source Engine. Otherwise, BUY THIS GAME NOW!

This game is perfect. I love the simplicity of it. It's still in alpha, so bugs are expected. I have not seen any bugs so far except for server lag. Yes, they have minor things to adjust, like how someone else holds a rock like a pistol, or how you can only get Raw Chicken Breasts no matter what animal you kill. I love this game. I hope they keep the simplicity of it, but add a lot more features. I give this game a 10/10 because even though it's in alpha, it's still one of the most enjoyable games on Steam. I was hesitant on buying it for $20 while it's still in alpha, but it was worth every penny. You can do so much already. You can craft bows, weapons, and even walls to build houses. You can choose to hunt and gather food while your friends scavenge for supplies. You can get a team or survive solo against other players, zombies, and wildlife. The first few in-game days are pretty difficult. My problem was that I had no idea how to find stone, but I found someone that was able to help. This game is worth it. Every penny. GET IT.

Although this game is still in beta...wait WHAT? It's still in ALPHA?!
Of course you'll notice performance-wise that it is in Alpha-stage (Minimal animations, lack of character variation: we all look the same except when you have clothes on aka NOT NAKED, strange lighting phenomenon in the night, no story, I died once trying to jump through a box that stood in the way of magical "falling" damage, whatever animal you hunt down you'll always get CHICKEN MEAT etc...)
BUT DON'T GET ME WRONG. This game FEELS already AWESOME. You jump into the game, you spawn randomly somewhere in a huge island and immediatly your instincts take over: SURVIVAL. You are searching for food, for resources to make better tools, and with those tools you're trying to make better weapons so you can hunt animals that are faster than you, like a bow taking down a deer from the distance and ultimately make your very own Shelter. Or even a Fortress! Resources like Stone, spawn randomly on the map, I know it doesn't make any sense at first but as I played along it makes very sense: By making the resources few, scarce and rare, it makes you feel really happy to find a mining spot. PLUS there is a plane DROP which contains super rare loot which triggers automatically a race with the other survivor, with other players.
Which makes us jump to the PVP part. This is where this game shines and make you forget that it is still in ALPHA version. This is where your emotions play crazy things with you. One time you play it's very slow paced, everyone you see is minding their own survival bussiness, yes almost calm and relaxing, and the other time you are chilling in your house and suddenly someone is asking if there is "someone in there?" and then you hear hell breaking out: A massive shootout right in front of your house between two gangs!! This intense decision making is very humanish. What do you do? Do you flee? Or do you want to try to ninja loot those gang corpses to find better loot, of risking your own hard earned loot? Do you stay in your house and stay quiet in hope the GANGS don't even realise that you're in there?...But what if you get caught? Even if I get caught maybe they will raid my house and steal everything?...
These intense decision making process is one hell of a emotion rollercoaster experience. The reson you are going through this processes is because you want to outsmart other people, you want to have security to build up your little empire, you want to find friends or enemies to get better loot. Whichever way you may choose, there is one motive that drives you to play more:
IT'S SURVIVAL OF THE FITTEST.

I've played this game a lot over the 2013 winter holidays. As of writing this, the game is still in an early Alpha build.
Rust is an addicting game. There's a constant urge to gather/craft/horde resources to further progress your place in the world. Servers are persistent. Your base and all of its belonging are subject to raids 24/7. It’s the closest thing to a PvP-oriented Sandbox MMO since EVE - A difficult comparison to draw considering Rust is an FPS game, and not an MMO. However, server can be as large as a few hundred simultaneous players, and the player structures are persistent; so in that sense, Rust accomplishes the same feeling without actually being an MMO.
Conditions are harsh. Just surviving the environment can be a difficult task, and the first few hours of gameplay will be spent just learning to stave off hunger, the cold, and natural predators.
“Survival” quickly shifts to the political nature of your neighbors. Do you trust no one and hope the rest of the world overlooks you? Or will you align yourself with a group for mutual protection? There is no ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ way to play. The choices you make, very much impact the server you live on. The ‘content’ in this game is purely from the interaction of players. In that regard, the game is fully playable and enjoyable even in Alpha. Having said that, there is much more to look forward to as the game evolves to extend depth in every mechanic that drives the gameplay. Improvements to gathering, crafting, maintaining items, building, defending, researching… I can only see this game getting even better over time.

This game is absolute gold. I like DayZ, and played it a good bit, but DayZ  is so buggy, and I feel that in DayZ you can more easily die, get lost, and its way harder to find your friends. In Rust I have found 0 bugs so far, and minor lag in servers. Now, understand that both of these games are both not in full version, and its hard to judge which is better. In Rust you can type in the chat which is linked to everyone in the whole server, unlike DayZ in which you can chat to only people in your vicinity. But in Rust, like DayZ you can only voice chat to your vicinity.
But enough about DayZ.
In Rust, Its kind of easier to find your friends. There is one road in the whole entire game ( see the map on my profile ), and the road goes in kinda a figure 8 shape, without crossing in the middle. The game also kinda has a Minecraft feel to it. When you start in the game you start with 2 Medkits, a torch (for night), and a rock. This rock you can use to beat people,zombies, bears,deer,pigs, and mine rocks and trees. You can craft in this game, but dont think its anything like Minecraft for a second. This game isn't blocky like minecraft, which is the mistake i made when my friend told me that this game was like minecraft and DayZ mixed. Also, theres radiation in this game, and its resembles a lot like Falllout. Radiation kills you, and they can be found in these little towns thats you find if you continue on the road. Your radiation levels are in the bottom right hand of the screen, and you hear a ticking noise (like in fallout) when your in radiation. Now why do they have radiation in this game you ask? Well they put radiation in these towns because in these towns there is good loot that respawns everys 5-10 minutes. It would be ashame if someone camped in the town, and took the loot. Its exciting to loot the towns because you find some great things like Guns, Ammo, blueprints (talk about this in a second), pickaxes, armor. The PvP is fun too, finding people while you have a loaded gun is better. Also in this game you can craft anything that is in the game, but you wont be able to just craft a gun straight from the start. When you loot towns you can find blueprints, which unlock the capability to craft more advanced stuff. Also there are airdrops, where a giant plane flys over and drops boxes of loots. Its kinda like the Hunger Games with the Cornocopia and how everyone at the same time rushes to get to the loot lol. Also you can build pretty cool houses (its not like minecraft building), and when you put a door on your house only you can open that door, so if you manage to keep your door closed when your not there people cant get in... Actually i lied, they can. If you have a wooden door people can hit down your door with a Rock, Pickaxe, Stoneaxe, or the hatchet. It actually takes a while, but if you have good stuff in your house, its worth their while. You can craft metal doors, that people CANT break down, unless they have explosives, which are pretty hard to find. One last thing, When you log off the game, your charecter does not just disapear, and you are no longer in the game. No no. When you log off the game Your character just falls down, and goes to sleep, and you are still able to be killed. So make sure your somewhere safe
Overall, like I said, this game is gold. And i totally recommend anyone to purchase it.

I've played this game a lot over the 2013 winter holidays. As of writing this, the game is still in an early Alpha build.
Rust is an addicting game. There's a constant urge to gather/craft/horde resources to further progress your place in the world. Servers are persistent. Your base and all of its belonging are subject to raids 24/7. It’s the closest thing to a PvP-oriented Sandbox MMO since EVE - A difficult comparison to draw considering Rust is an FPS game, and not an MMO. However, server can be as large as a few hundred simultaneous players, and the player structures are persistent; so in that sense, Rust accomplishes the same feeling without actually being an MMO.
Conditions are harsh. Just surviving the environment can be a difficult task, and the first few hours of gameplay will be spent just learning to stave off hunger, the cold, and natural predators.
“Survival” quickly shifts to the political nature of your neighbors. Do you trust no one and hope the rest of the world overlooks you? Or will you align yourself with a group for mutual protection? There is no ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ way to play. The choices you make, very much impact the server you live on. The ‘content’ in this game is purely from the interaction of players. In that regard, the game is fully playable and enjoyable even in Alpha. Having said that, there is much more to look forward to as the game evolves to extend depth in every mechanic that drives the gameplay. Improvements to gathering, crafting, maintaining items, building, defending, researching… I can only see this game getting even better over time.

So I got this game last night, it's amazing even in this early stage!

This game is absolute gold. I like DayZ, and played it a good bit, but DayZ  is so buggy, and I feel that in DayZ you can more easily die, get lost, and its way harder to find your friends. In Rust I have found 0 bugs so far, and minor lag in servers. Now, understand that both of these games are both not in full version, and its hard to judge which is better. In Rust you can type in the chat which is linked to everyone in the whole server, unlike DayZ in which you can chat to only people in your vicinity. But in Rust, like DayZ you can only voice chat to your vicinity.
But enough about DayZ.
In Rust, Its kind of easier to find your friends. There is one road in the whole entire game ( see the map on my profile ), and the road goes in kinda a figure 8 shape, without crossing in the middle. The game also kinda has a Minecraft feel to it. When you start in the game you start with 2 Medkits, a torch (for night), and a rock. This rock you can use to beat people,zombies, bears,deer,pigs, and mine rocks and trees. You can craft in this game, but dont think its anything like Minecraft for a second. This game isn't blocky like minecraft, which is the mistake i made when my friend told me that this game was like minecraft and DayZ mixed. Also, theres radiation in this game, and its resembles a lot like Falllout. Radiation kills you, and they can be found in these little towns thats you find if you continue on the road. Your radiation levels are in the bottom right hand of the screen, and you hear a ticking noise (like in fallout) when your in radiation. Now why do they have radiation in this game you ask? Well they put radiation in these towns because in these towns there is good loot that respawns everys 5-10 minutes. It would be ashame if someone camped in the town, and took the loot. Its exciting to loot the towns because you find some great things like Guns, Ammo, blueprints (talk about this in a second), pickaxes, armor. The PvP is fun too, finding people while you have a loaded gun is better. Also in this game you can craft anything that is in the game, but you wont be able to just craft a gun straight from the start. When you loot towns you can find blueprints, which unlock the capability to craft more advanced stuff. Also there are airdrops, where a giant plane flys over and drops boxes of loots. Its kinda like the Hunger Games with the Cornocopia and how everyone at the same time rushes to get to the loot lol. Also you can build pretty cool houses (its not like minecraft building), and when you put a door on your house only you can open that door, so if you manage to keep your door closed when your not there people cant get in... Actually i lied, they can. If you have a wooden door people can hit down your door with a Rock, Pickaxe, Stoneaxe, or the hatchet. It actually takes a while, but if you have good stuff in your house, its worth their while. You can craft metal doors, that people CANT break down, unless they have explosives, which are pretty hard to find. One last thing, When you log off the game, your charecter does not just disapear, and you are no longer in the game. No no. When you log off the game Your character just falls down, and goes to sleep, and you are still able to be killed. So make sure your somewhere safe
Overall, like I said, this game is gold. And i totally recommend anyone to purchase it.

I have a mac book pro. So lets start there. The game is still in its alpha stages like most of the reviews have stated. So you cant expect the full package right from the beginning.

This is a very fun survival game where you start out with nothing more than a rock, some first aid kits, a torch, and your released on to a world where you have to gather your own materials like stone, sulfur, wood, cloth, and food. The materials that you gather can be used to craft buildings, weapons, armor, cook food, and you can even acquire blueprints from abandoned buildings or zombies to learn new crafting recipes. The game is very fun in the sense that it is fun to gather all these materials, craft stuff, and build your own home the way you want it. The player interactions vary from server to server, there are some servers where people who are all geared up with modern weapons, kevlar, and explosives kill off everyone in sight regardless if their a shirtless newbie or an experienced player who actually poses a threat while in other servers players dont attack each other on sight. When your character dies you lose everything that you had on your character but you keep anything that you had stored inside of your player built home assuming that your home didnt get raided and that you can find your way back without a compass or world map.
The things that I feel could really be improved in this game are some really simple things which it lacks like 1) A compass to get a sense of what direction your running  2) A world map, even one with fog of war until you explore the area would be nice 3) The ability to respawn at your home instead of a random location after death 4) Vehicles 5) Tamed pets or wild animals that you can use to fight alongside your character. The servers are frequently getting attacked by hackers with ddos attacks, aim bots, dupe hacks, no night time hacks, and other exploits as well which is a big turn off for honest players.
Overall its a fun game but it still has a long way to go before its worth the $20 price tag. The game is still in Alpha stage so it has room to grow but I wouldnt recommend it right now if your looking for a game that is complete and ready to go, if you dont mind that the game isnt complete though its a fun game to pass the time when your bored.
