Rust definitely has potential to be a good survival game,and in some aspects it already is. However, most of these good parts are countered by gamebreaking flaws in game design or massive issues caused by the community.
I cannot recommend it at this stage because of the glaring problems that lie in the core structure and the Developers mentality. Even "it's an alpha" can't excuse some of the awful design decisions made by the developers,especially when it comes to core aspects of the game like Server administration and Balancing.
This review is mostly focused on the negatives because there's plenty of rose-tinted reviews upvoted on the store page anyways if you're just looking for something to convince you to buy it, so here's the most gamebreaking problems in it's current stage:
- The big One: Server administration! The developers decided to give all the power to the people who are willing to pay for hosting Servers. Server administrators have a cheat console. In a game based on survival. Yep. They have Godmode(!!!) on command, can teleport any- and everyone where they please, spawn in items for themselves or others, change server Rules on the fly without anyone ingame noticing,wipe the entire server and reset everyone's progress to zero, ban/kick anyone they wish without having to give reasons...the list goes on and will probably expand if the developers decide to keep this "feature". Some people think this is a good thing.  The notion of admins flying around in godmode without taking damage from anything,spawning in explosives to destroy bases and kicking people just because they killed one of the admins or something ridiculous seems entirely fine to some people because they think of the game like Garrys Mod. And those are the same people whose recommendations based on an hour of gameplay you see upvoted on the Store Page.
And if you think "surely admins won't abuse that power and it can be used for good only because admins are good people", you couldn't be more wrong. Giving admins a cheat console is ASKING for abuse. And don't get me wrong, there neeeds to be administration,someone to kick hackers and griefers (which there are plenty of,see below) but you cannot give anyone who decides to pay for server hosting a cheat console and expect them to only use it for those things.
Dedicated servers hosted by the game are scarce and fully populated and don't have proper administration, so griefers can flourish for days without ever getting banned.
And the solution is so simple: DON'T give admins a cheat console. Give them the tools to get rid of hackers and griefers, and give those tools to the community too. Votekick! An option to report players. An option to atleast SEE which admins are currently on,and what the names of server admins are, and an option to report those admins if they are abusing their power,which happens all the time on many servers. All of this is currently missing, and it can easily break your experience of the game.
-Server-bound progression: Everything you do in the game is bound to one server only,the server you are currently on.Now this sounds like it would be good at first,and yes,it is necessary to keep the balance and avoid serverhopping. But couple this with the cheat console admins and think about it. You might play for hours building up a base and then discover that all of it gets blown up by an admin with godmode on who decides to spawn in explosives and destroy all your stuff because he feels like it. Anything you do ingame is in the hands of the admins of the server you play on,and that is a huge issue which many people don't seem to realize until they experienced it themselves.
This would not be an issue if admins wouldn't have as much power as they currently have (and if hackers wouldn't exist) or if there were dedicated,modded servers with websites,active admins and features like votekicking or an actual working Banning/kicking software other than Steams VAC-banning which often takes several months to be processed and even then only bans the current account, not the IP. I don't doubt that those servers will start to form once the community has access to or developed new tools, but right now every server you join is a gamble, you might play for hours and get all of it destroyed by a power-abusing admin or hacker.
-The big issues caused by the community: Killing on Sight (KoS), Griefing, Hacking,abusing admin Powers, regular DDoS-attacks, Killing freshspawns, camping spawnpoints, VoiP without mute feature (enjoy your 12year olds squeaking or teens trying to be bandits), the list goes on.: This obviously depends on your personality and if you care or don't care,but even if you don't care you WILL see it,and quite often,and won't be able to ignore it. Rust has no age restrictions, is quite cheap, has similarities to Minecraft and DayZ,and is hyped just as much because...well,it's a survival game and we all want a good one. So enjoy your hordes of wannabe bandits, squeaking pewdiepie fans and teenage godmode admins wrecking your base because you didn't comply with their wannabe bandit demands. Hacking is common, abusing admin powers is essentially the same and happening all the time. Killing on Sight seems to be standard because that's the trend that DayZs banditry hype sadly set. Camping spawwnpoints and shooting fresh spawns happens all the time because some kids just need to stroke their epeen on a daily basis by shooting unarmed freshspawns or people with far inferiour gear.
- Balancing: People who have played on a server for quite some time will have all the best gear you can get. Kevlar-clad players with Holo-scope silenced M4s with laser sight and flashlight who are able to instantly heal themself up with large medkits at the press of a button are the sort of thing you'll inevitably face,naked or in cloth armor that barely protects you,with your rock or hatchet or maybe even 9mm Pistol if you managed to set up a shack before you got oneshot randomly for no apparent reason. The combat system is barebones, most weapons oneshot or kill a fresh spawn in about 2 seconds flat while kevlar armor seems to absorb Pistol bullets like a spongue, not to mention how much easier it is to hit someone with holo sights and laser designation. The blueprinting system seems fun at first and adds a layer of progression into the game but once you encountered a fully geared out person you'll see the issues with it: to even stand a chance of winning versus someone who has played on a server for a long time and has a base with tons of supplies somewhere you will need dozens of hours of gathering,crafting and farming zombies and "radtowns" for blueprints and a good bit of luck paired with the constant danger of getting oneshot or your base raided by snowballing fully geared "veterans". On high populated servers your base will inevitably get raided quickly before you can even build enough defenses to stand a chance, and the people who already played a long time on the server will simply be able to break through anything with c4 anyways.
Theres plenty more issues with the game but those are the most potent gamebreaking ones you should know about. A lot of people don't know about these issues because they haven't encountered them yet or ignore them because of the hypetrain, and "it's an alpha" seems to be an excuse for bad design choices and massive core structure flaws nowadays, so I'll leave it at that.
Rust undoubtedly has positive aspects and I've had my fun building stuff with others, but until they decide to strip admins of their ridiculous godmode powers or dedicated servers with policing are established I simply cannot recommend it to you. I want a good survival game as much as everyone else but unfortunately Rust isn't it,at least not in the current state. If those glaring issues get fixed/ proper dedicated servers are established I will change the review/recommendation

Rust is a post-apocalyptic multiplayer survival game in which you can´t trust anyone. The game is good at making you paranoid and I love it. You start with nothing but a rock, a torch and two bandages, which you have to use to survive the zombies, wolves, bears and other survivors. You have to make a house to live in, but this house can be taken over by others if you don´t look after it. You have to gather resources, but these can be stolen from both your corpse and your house. You have to set a spawn point by making a sleeping bag, but this can also be destroyed. You can even be killed while you're offline, so you're never safe!
One of the great things about this game is that it doesn´t have a minimap. You can't just look at a map in the corner of your screen and see where everything is, you have to memorize the environment. This might seem really harsh and it sort of is, but after playing it for a couple of hours I knew where I could find everything. Just follow the road, my friends told me, and they were right. By following the road and memorizing its surroundings, you know where everything is and it really adds to the experience.
I would definitely recommend this game to everyone who doesn't care for a story and just wants to have fun. It's more fun with friends, but even on your own you can accomplish a whole lot. The game is still in alpha, so there are a lot of small things that don't seem quite right, and bugs are found everywhere too. Servers keep going down lately because of hackers, but this is not the game's fault. I'm sure the game itself will be a lot better when it's finished, but even now I can recommend this game.

EDIT: It seems recently that Rust has begun cracking down on the cheaters. They've also removed the zombies and I'm pleased to say that I'm happy about both of these changes. With the banhammer swinging wild, the game is safer to play and enjoy. You're still gonna have all of your hard work ruined, but at least it won't be by some teleporting, C4 hurling god. The other change, hte removal of zombies, is also good, because hte game was never about them. Let's face it, they were never that big a threat. They were too weak and too few to be a threat. The game was more about surviving your needs and fellow man from the begining. With these changes implemented, I'm happy to change my review to a positive one and recommend this game again.
Unless you really love working hard just to have everything blown up, don't bother with this game yet. Don't get me wrong, the game itself is great. For an alpha, it's really functional, with very few game breaking bugs. Exploring the wilderness feels dangerous and tense, and getting a group of friends together to build and defend a fort is awesome. But as it stands, server crashes, bad lag, and worst of all, hackers are completely ruining this otherwise great game. Valve Anti Cheat is used on every official server, but that seems to do nothing. People will still spawn in the best possible gear, teleport into your house, kill you and your friends, and then, for fun, blow up every last shread of your fort which took you days to build. I'm not concerned with the 'bandits', the players who are aggressive towards others, have a shoot-on-sight mentality, and will do anything to steal your gear. My issue comes from the vast ammount of hackers. In the future, if they can make hacking more difficult (I'm well aware that hacking can't be truely stopped), this game will be playable again, and it will be a lot of fun. But as it stands, you'll only be spending money on a tool to frustrate yourself.

I picked this game up over the Steam sale hoping it would eventually go on sale however it didnt. I found a server with a low population and it was fun for a few days , but you have to spend hours at a game like this. So if you are a  casual player make sure you have friends who also play or you wont get anywhere in this game. Thing is in this game you are never truly safe . Youll get raided non stop . to give an example 5 minutes prior to writing this review i relogged into rust only to find my base being held under seige by a group of players in kevlar. Even if you have a base players can put up ramps to get in or even break/blown down walls and doors Which i really dont find fun if you have spent so much time in the game , but hey it happens. Oh also i forgot to mention since the game is still farely new it patches quite frequently so servers will usually get wiped , so all your goods stored away and your bases will go poof and sometimes so will your crafting recipies. I also wouldnt recommend joining full servers because ppl will just run around as nomadic nudists killing you >_< and yes that had happened to me the first time i ever played this game. If youve got the time , dedication, and friends then be my guest and drop $20 on this . if you dont .... well i'd figure surviving out in the wilderness irl will be more fullfilling

Whilst it's still clearly an alpha, Rust shows much the same promise and appeal of Minecraft, Garry's mod (or countless other sandbox environments/games).  The beauty of Rust for me is observing human behaviour, and how my own behaviour changes within the game world:  Someone's running towards me, do I greet them? flee? Shoot to kill? Should I live out my days in the woods with the bears, or should I group together with others and form a community/township?  Maybe the world needs a roving gang of thugs pillaging the other players towns?
Freedom is the greatest gift and greatest risk in any game.

One day someone will try to come and take your stuff so find a community to team up and protect each other. Soon enough you'll have a town, working together to further the general interest of a group that was comprised of Ex-naked-men-from-the-woods.
Buy it. While a raw game, there is a ton of potential. This is by Garry of Garry's mod.

Rust is an early access survival of the fittest type FPS that grants players the ability to build houses, kill other players, (There are PvP disabled servers for more casual players) create an arsenal, and strive to forge alliances in order to survive the harsh, apocolyptic wasteland given to them. Rust fits well in with tradtitional survival games by pressing basic needs into gaming, by forcing players to hunt animals for food, gather wood for a shelter, and even use bandages when damaged by the unforgiving aspects of the wild.
Pros:
-Great Multiplayer game (Singleplayer doesn't exist, but still a great MP game nonetheless)
-Strong survival aspects provide constant awareness
-Challenging
Cons:
-VERY hard to find any source of metal to build guns
-Due to lack of resources, the experienced players can bully and ruin the experience for newer players
-Requires a HUGE amount of FPS unless you disable grass (Grass isn't needed though)
The final verdict: Rust is a fun multiplayer game that has challenging aspects to it. However, it may be too challenging for those unwilling to spend hours trying to find the only metal ore on the map, or those being bullied by stronger players. While it doesn't set any landmark strengths in the survival/FPS genre, it's still worth the $20. Plus, it's in early access, so it has room to improve drastically.

For an Alpha this is an amazing game. the graphics are not the best but they are not bad ether. the gameplay, in my opinion, is amazing. Rust at it's core is a survival game. It does have zombies but it is not a dayz clone. Infact zombies are a very smal part of the game. In rust you have to survive. you must worry about hnger level, radiation level, body temp, other animals (wolves and bears right now), the occasional zombie, and the most dangerous preditor in the game. Other players. The community, while some might think it is horrible, is great in my opinion. if you press "T" you can type and everyone on the server can see it.  You can get basic questions answered by the community this way. However do NOT run up to people to ask them questions. First that is just annoying and second they will assume you are hostile and kill you.  Rust also has a really cool feature for a survival game. when you are in a particular proximaty of other players you can hear them talk (assuming they are holding down the talk button). they can also hear you talk. this can act as a warning system for possible hostile parties.
If this was the finished product I would only give this game a 6/10 or a 7/10 because it is a bit buggy but considering it is in Alpha stage and you are still getting the final game when it comes out (not to mention you can give input and make this game into something that you would enjoy more) and the game makers are working on making the game less buggy and adding features I would have to give it a rating of 10/10 for now. RECOMMEND X 1000. Even in its alpha release, this is still a 60$ value game. And it's only 20 and only going to get better. I'll chunk this review into sections of gameplay, and be as honest as possible.
Things you need to know before I describe early game: The game's resources are respawning-node based. If you find 4 rocks and 4 wood piles in an area, after you loot them all they'll come back in that area. The wandering nomad style doesn't do that well in rust - there's a lot of empty landscape with no nodes. However, all the spawning locations are near well-off areas. The game is "Find an area with decent resources and settle down" focused. Explore once you're on your feet.
Early game - You start with nothing, and the very early game is kind of gimmicky. Hunger is a factor, and the only source of food in the game is killing animals. The animals fight back and, like I said, you don't start very well equipped to fight them. One animal does give more than enough food to set you up for mid game, and if you find a pig (doesn't fight back) you're on easy street. If the pig you find is a near a bear
The current solution to this is an exploit, that I honestly hope they keep around. Once you get enough wood to build a shelter (you can either hit trees or search for wood piles that give ~100 wood in 6 seconds and then expire), you can stand in the doorway and animals will treat you as inside and not attack you, allowing you to safely kill hostile ones. Kind of a trade 50 wood for safety against animals and easy food mechanic, I like it.
Mid game - Once you're not going to die to starvation, mid game is all about building up and teching. You start crafting better tools, move out of your shelter into the very well-done house building system, get a furnace and workbench made, and all of a sudden the materials you get from mining rocks can be turned into guns. Neat!  With guns it's pretty easy to start  looting the zombie-guarded and irradiated cities, and you start looting research kits and rarer gear. Research kits can be consumed to teach you how to craft an item in your inventory; basically you loot rare♥♥♥♥♥♥and learn how to craft it forever. There's a LOT of items you don't know how to craft at the start.
End game - Dog eat dog. End game is all about building huge fortresses, storing your most important items, and taking your "less important" guns and food out to kill other players. Terrorize an area of the map, killing all the nearby players and looting their houses, until everyone you don't want around leaves. And then claim that♥♥♥♥♥♥as your own. Build a huge wooden♥♥♥♥♥♥shaped house in the middle to show your dominance, who gives a♥♥♥♥♥♥ you've got 15 wood pile nodes all to yourself now.

If you've got $20 bucks laying around then get this game, if you're looking for game of the year material then don't.
As of now, it's a rinse and repeat process. If you have other friends on the same server as you, it's near impossible to find eachother. There's no map system implemented so your forced to communicate out of game. If you manage to find your friends, you have to start gathering materials. There's three different types as of now: wood, stone, and ore. They spawn randomly in locations around the world. The entire map is huge, but not the entire thing is used. If you ever played the Arma 2 DayZ mod it's the same as debug land. It's nothing, just trees and low quality textures. The game becomes grindy when you begin constructing a base. It takes a TON of wood for building a good base. The gun system is alright, but it's RNG based if you find the plan to make the good ones. You have to camp the rad bases to get them. The way that raiding/griefing works at the moment is awful. When you log off the game, your character stays in the place that you logged off. Often people will raid your base while you're offline and you will log and and lose all previous progress. Short term gain, short term fun.
Overall I've enjoyed the game and there are some features that make a great game, but there is a lot of work to be done.

You start off in the woods naked (literally), a gray screen filter fades and you see trees, rocks, grass all around you. Your objective? Stay alive. This game has a real interesting way of introducing survival aspects, with the way it has body affects such as cold and hunger but in a much more dynamic way than other games with this mechanic such as Infestation and DayZ. You need to chop down, shoot, cook, and steal anything that is in your way. You need to find blueprints to make new weapons, medkits, and structures. Make bases, sleeping bags, doors to keep the main enemy, the player as far away from you as possible. The game really makes you feel like you are alone, and no one is there to help you, players that find you usually kill you on sight, the game really is a kill or be killed situation which is amazing, though does not go without it's faults. For an alpha it is great, but I do hope they add some type of friend system in the game, where it doesn't immediately teleport you to your friends or anything but shows you where they are using some sort of directional arrow. That being said the game being in this state I would give it a 10/10. I hope to see more updates to this game from Garry and his Team.

Something that is worth noteing before you consider buying this is that they are re-makeing the game, however you can acsess the old one (Called Legacy) quite easyly. The game is worth buying for that alone because its so damm awsome, but this review is for the newer version (Experimental). On experimental I have somewhere around 10/20 hours (Out of my almost 200H on the old and new version combined)
Anyways, the review! This game was, and still is great! The current version (As of 01/11/14) shows great promise and is a very much playable game, despite a few issues and nucences. Despite this being a suvival game it is very different, Theres something about the game that makes it so immersive, you feel like theres actually something at stake throughout the whole game witch cannot be said for alot of other games. The systems in the game also work very well. It is a solid game that suffers from quite few game-breaking bugs.
On the down-side, there are quite a few bugs! None of them are game-breaking and its still fun but the game sometimes messes up, I sometimes found animals where invisible and could kill me, but this only happened a few times. I also noticed a large lack of content in experimental at the moment, I had the best guns in the game within an hour or two, and my base was made with top-level walls within about 3/4 hours. This was a shame because old rust had alot of stuff to do in it. I am sure both these issues will be totally gone within a few more updates, It would be worth noteing updates are comeing out very fast for this game, and they tend to include two or three new aditions to the game.
In tems of the community I have found alot of them will kill you if you are a naked (Yes liturally naked because thats how you spawn in this game) but if you get a gun and gear people will treat you nicely. I'd recogmend you play with a friend or two because if not larger groups of people WILL trample you, witch is quite fun, because you find yourself thinking about your base even when you are offline, and hoping nobody breaks in.
Overall, if you are unsure if you want it, get it because even if you don't like the game right now it will improve in a few updates.

For old review, look below.
---REVIEW---
First of all, this was written on the 26th of November, 2015. Some things may have changed since then (now for me)
First, the basics of the game.
Graphics, Sound and Performance: 4/5
Highest settings take quite a beefy setup, but I can get a fairly steady 30FPS on medium settings.
The ambient sound effects are alright, but I don't hear them much.
The game looks amazing when you have a good computer.
I will now review the gameplay in 2 ways: a busy (50-100 player) PVP server(A), and a PVE server(B).
Combat/Hunting:
A) 3/5
For a game where everyone is instantly hostile, the combat could be improved/made more realistic (like Fallout's crippling system, making hitting the legs better)
B) 4/5
The animals are difficult to kill sometimes: from the AI both helping and hindering at the same time.
AI:
A+B) 4/5
Sometimes it is very realistic as hostiles will follow for ages and the movement speed is just right for hunting, but I have seen horses run up vertical cliffs.
Building:
A) 3/5
The system is good, but the community just tears it apart.
B) 5/5
I would have been happy with this game if all I got was this building system. It is complex yet easy to learn, and upgrading is the easiest thing to do. The construction cost is balanced.
Community:
A) 1/5
My experience is that as soon as another player finds you they will follow you with a rock till you or they die. building is a nightmare if you are on a raid server.
B) 5/5
The server I am on most of the time has great admins, players and we all respect each other. No hostility, just the beauty of the games graphics.
Overall Score:
A) 3.5/5
B) 4.5/5
Would recommend for the PVE, only recomend PVP to people who are good at or like that sort of thing.

Cons
-There is so little content that i can count all the in game items on one hand

-Poor hit registration, if a player goes to hit you with a rock you can just run through his body to the other side.

---REVIEW---
First of all, this was written on the 26th of November, 2015. Some things may have changed since then (now for me)
First, the basics of the game.
Graphics, Sound and Performance: 4/5
Highest settings take quite a beefy setup, but I can get a fairly steady 30FPS on medium settings.
The ambient sound effects are alright, but I don't hear them much.
The game looks amazing when you have a good computer.
I will now review the gameplay in 2 ways: a busy (50-100 player) PVP server(A), and a PVE server(B).
Combat/Hunting:
A) 3/5
For a game where everyone is instantly hostile, the combat could be improved/made more realistic (like Fallout's crippling system, making hitting the legs better)
B) 4/5
The animals are difficult to kill sometimes: from the AI both helping and hindering at the same time.
AI:
A+B) 4/5
Sometimes it is very realistic as hostiles will follow for ages and the movement speed is just right for hunting, but I have seen horses run up vertical cliffs.
Building:
A) 3/5
The system is good, but the community just tears it apart.
B) 5/5
I would have been happy with this game if all I got was this building system. It is complex yet easy to learn, and upgrading is the easiest thing to do. The construction cost is balanced.
Community:
A) 1/5
My experience is that as soon as another player finds you they will follow you with a rock till you or they die. building is a nightmare if you are on a raid server.
B) 5/5
The server I am on most of the time has great admins, players and we all respect each other. No hostility, just the beauty of the games graphics.
Overall Score:
A) 3.5/5
B) 4.5/5
Would recommend for the PVE, only recomend PVP to people who are good at or like that sort of thing.

The game has promise. Aside from the connnection issues and the abusive players, gameplay has the potential to grow into something explorative and entertaining at the same time. There has to be a system where newly spawned characters / players can have some leeway from being targeted by the already established players, like a "safe zone".
Mechanics-wise, of course there has to be changes, like farming the right materials from the right places. But building up your own camp and expanding your aresenal to meet your daily needs is vastly immersive and you can lose hours trying to survive. Feasible for gameplay for solo or alliances, just watch out for your back and lock your doors.
EDIT: DON'T BUY IT YET. If you decide you're going to buy, don't play yet. The player base has taken on the culture of KOS (Kill-On-Sight). This means that any new player / spawn will die instantly since most of the current players are already established and will have firearms already. There are server wipes often, but that doesn't change the fact that players will KOS and raid others on an hourly basis. If you want to try it out, I suggest a NO PVP server at least. THIS GAME NEEDS FURTHER BALANCING.
EDIT 2: Hey, it's been 2 years since my last review. Buy it. It's good now. Turn off the censor for some realistic teabagging. Level up by hitting a tree with a rock. Learned to craft a sentry turret by making a campfire.
11/10 will build 2000 campfires again.

Do you recommend this game? Not currently. Which pains me to say this because my intention was to get 4-5 of my friends playing it with me.  Writing this reveiw won't encourage them to play to say the least.
The gameplay is very interesting and the game itself is very mysterious. There is no map and you have no compass. You basically need to familiarize yourself with the game world which can make grouping up fun.
PvP isn't as bad as most people say, but getting to the point where you can start having fun is a huge curve. Challenging gameplay to me is fun and weeds out people you don't want to play with.  I spent too much time trying to find a animal to kill.  They do need more of these available. This game has great potentiol but they are not focusing on some key aspects.
My problem? The servers and the menu.  This is the worst main menu and server setup that I have seen to date. Please invest time into this aspect of the game so that I can actually play the game.  It is kind of annoying when you pay money for something you can't play. I did read the disclaimer that the game is still in alpha, some things work and some things don't.  I didn't expect that to mean that I wouldn't be able to play the game. Logged in today and my previous servers were not full and now I can't connect to any server in the whole game.  My guess is it is the menu system being buggy.
Official servers you were on prior are always full at peak hours.  Not only that but the refresh server button has never worked for me.  I did notice new servers pop up that had larger capacities so I got excited.  It is just annoying having to restart the game to see if someone left a server you were previously on.
With that being said if things I mentioned do not frustrate you then invest money in the alpha version of this game. It will be worth it once the kinks are worked out. Honestly I am dieing to learn how to play better but I always move onto another game after fussing with the stupid menu for 15 minues and not finding a server that I can join.

There's only one thing I could say about Rust, and that is, it has potential!
I say this because it's still in Alpha mode and is clearly unfinished. For starters, there is a lack of animals to hunt and a lack of rocks to mine. It would also be nice to have a few more non PvP servers up and running, just because that's how I like to play this game. The lag is a bit of a downside too, BUT (and it's a big but), the gameplay is good, the whole menu layout is simple and relatively easy to learn. There is certainly a lot of potential for this game and would totally recommend you buy it, but maybe you should wait a bit until the biggest problems are fixed!
At this early point in development, I would give the game a 7/10, but once more rocks and animals have been added (which I can only hope they will be), it would imagine it would make 8.5/10 :)

What has become apparent to me through the time i've spent playing this game is the amount of fear that you experience when faced with another player. This game is hardly about the poorly animated zombies, of whom i've noticed float 6 inches above the ground when in combat, it is about hunting, exploring, surviving dark nights and bright days, and avoiding possible fights to the death with other survivors. I recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a challenge and is willing to die from a bullet in their back every now and then, forcing them to start their life over from the beginning. I don't, however, recommend it to anyone who's looking to play with a Steam friend. This game isn't designed for co-op play in that matter. All of the survivors you meet are found while traveling through the large and at times complex forests. There is no easy way, as far as I know, to quickly teleport near or to a friend. Aside from this co-op "flaw", I would say that $20 is the right price for a game with such an immensive crafting, hunting, and building system in a cruel, harsh, and realistic world.

EDIT: 10/2/2015
I have played this game (as vaguely stated above) since a very early release of it on steam. Even then it was solid. As of right now I would like to say a few things that makes this game stand out.
1. The Dev team. It is so relieving, after scowering the webs for games to play, to come back to this game. The Dev team not only CARES, but seems to be extremely passionate, dedicated, and not to mention talented. Everything I have seen come out of this team has been gold. Anything that fell short was promptly removed, and brought back with a much more apealing 2.0 version. They take the time to make things the way they should be, and take NO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It is teams like this that deserve the money they make off of their games.
2. The atmosphere. Just the general feeling of the game. It feels like you can play it either very laid back, or binge. Now I will say that survival games tend to attract the type of crowd that doesn't appeal to everyone out there. Plainly stated most of you guys are total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when you play the game. With Rust, you will have to use your instinct, not a humanity number, to figure out if you can trust people.

After around an hour and a half of bad spawns, scarce resources, and short-lived ventures into the more inhabited areas of the map, I ran into the first friendly player I had met in Rust. I had initially spotted him pretty far away, but I paid no real notice to him as he had a rock equipped. Eventually he got close enough for us to clearly see each other and, upon the realization that neither of us were hostile, we both pulled out torches as a mutual sign of peace (or the highest possible level of non-aggression that can exist in Rust). I dropped my old hatchet for him as I had just finished crafting one with metal, and he gave me some food as a sign of good faith. After nearly 30 minutes of searching and scavenging, we had pooled enough resources to craft us each some minimally decent gear. We knew that if we wanted to progress any further we would need to mine boulders, and a lot of them. I used what remaining materials we had to put together a 9mm handgun and several bullets, though I reminded him it was only in case we really needed it. I had decided earlier during my many unwanted experiences with bullets to the face that I would try my hardest not to run around slaughtering every newly spawned player that I came across. A few minutes out from camp we had encountered a player with a hunting bow. I had been running with my hatchet out, so I quickly took out the handgun in my inventory and pointed it in his direction, attempting to scare him away. When the player was far enough away we continued up a road towards a few stones. The area was surrounded by trees so I opted to stand guard with the handgun while my friend mined. Just as we were moving on to the next boulder, I heard the gunfire start. I turned around to see a player with an assault rifle gunning down my friend, and before I could land any shots on him he had already begun shooting me. It was at that moment that I remembered I hadn't even crafted a sleeping bag for the camp, as that was one of the objectives of the trip we were taking. I typed into the chat, thanking the friend I had made for all of his help and asking the player who had killed us if we had been intruding in his area or something along those lines. He simply wrote "Sorry guys :D" This is the single problem that I have with games like this. Why does it have to be "shoot-on-sight?" That player had obviously taken us by surprise and was better equipped than us. Even if he had a justifiable reason for approaching two very poorly equipped players (which he really didn't considering we were in the middle of the woods and he had pretty much all of the gear you could need in this game) he could have easily told us to cooperate by either putting away our weapons or just leaving the area. But of course, he comes around, sees some players trying to gather enough supplies to get to a stable point in the game, and decides to go out of his way to approach us and use unecessary ammo for a hatchet and a handgun with four bullets. Then, to add even more of an insult, he adds an apology at the end, as if he had no choice but to shoot two unexpecting, half-naked, unprepared players.
All in all, though, I do see a lot of potential in this game, and the good in the community does shine through every once in a while. I just wish that people would realize that they don't need to go around killing players who haven't had the chance to experience the game. People like that are the single reason why so many players on steam feel that they wasted money on what would otherwise be a great experience.

It's Rust. It's what you expected when you heard about it long ago. It's a game where you're thrown in to a huge world with just a rock, and you have to survive. Essentially, it's a game where you're a naked caveman trying to live and avoiding and/or killing other naked cavemen. That being said, do NOT go into this solo, as it is not meant to be played as such. The possibilities of things you can do and things you can craft are near endless, until some asshat shoots you and you die and lose all your stuff. Be sure to bring a buddy and help each other survive, but don't kill each other. Death holds a lot of meaning in this game, so if you don't like that, steer clear of Rust. It's still in alpha, which means it has a lot of room for improvement, and it has a ton of potential. It's a really great game if you're into surviving and killing other people to dominate their stuff. That being said, don't be the asshat who picks a fight he/she can't win. Because then everyone will hate you. Overall, this is a game that is definitely worth trying. Might as well get it in alpha, because you don't know if the price may go up when it goes into beta or releases. It's worth the 20 bucks, just make sure you take precautions to ensure your survival. Oh yeah, servers may be a little laggy or slow depending on your computer, but it'll get better as the game develops. Definitely well hyped, another great gem by Garry. 8.5/10 (Alpha Ver.)

Well I will be honest and say at first I was not to sure to buy this game. Early access scares me at times, I've mad a fair few wrong decisions in the past. Rust from what I understood was a Dayz clone, which shouldnt be held against it. I wasnt to sure how well this game will do in terms of keeping myself intrested.
As I am writing this I believe i have nearly spent 7-10 hours in game on a single medium populated server (which i suggest finding one to start off, learn the basics etc). At first I found it annoying, I wasnt to sure what to do (no in-game help, but its in Alpha so i didnt expect any different) I spent alot of time hitting a stone against the large rock formations hoping to get the stone resources I needed to create axes and so on. However once you start to find your feet with the game you are up and running.
I enjoyed the survival element of the game, at first I stayed away from anything that moved, even the wild boar. Once i got used to the wild life, zombies and half naked people running around just like myself i started to really enjoy the game. Once you arm yourself with either a bow or a pistol it is time to run for those radioactive buildings and find some taste loot. On top of looking for loot by either killing zombies or searching through randomly spawned boxes a real neat feature that is in the current build is supply drops. From my understanding every hour or so a plane will fly over the map and drop several boxes of loot. This is very enjoyable, more than I thought. The rush to beat other people to the drop to then meet face to face with another person brings a fair few challenges. However great.
Lastly the player building. At first I wasnt to sure how this would go - I wasnt to sure how important a 'house' was in terms of game play. After playing for several hours it comes apparnt that it is needed, hell its your base of operations, your fort your life line. So when it comes down to creating a structure to keep the enemy at bay I wasnt to sure how well this feature will be implimented. Again this is Alpha so I knew it wasnt going to be polished and very basic but saying that I was amazed at how well it works. Yes it is basic, this is no Sims house creation but at its current build it has everything you need plus more.
I will edit this over the Xmas period if I have more time to play the game. I will recommend this game to anyone as I have had a blast with it. I do hope updates and added features come into the game soon. I look forward to see how Rust holds up in terms of development with such games as Dayz but one thing is for sure, this game has great promise.
I wish the Devs all the luck with this game, this could be a gem.

The update added a proper progression system to the game, so each era of gear, or technology, lasts a decent amount of time, meaning a server will go through different phases of what type of gear the majority of players have, from primitive bows and spears, to fully automatic rifles and explosives.
I'd definitely recommend this game, but go into it expecting to die a lot. Get used to losing your stuff, and taking big risks to get stuff.

After around an hour and a half of bad spawns, scarce resources, and short-lived ventures into the more inhabited areas of the map, I ran into the first friendly player I had met in Rust. I had initially spotted him pretty far away, but I paid no real notice to him as he had a rock equipped. Eventually he got close enough for us to clearly see each other and, upon the realization that neither of us were hostile, we both pulled out torches as a mutual sign of peace (or the highest possible level of non-aggression that can exist in Rust). I dropped my old hatchet for him as I had just finished crafting one with metal, and he gave me some food as a sign of good faith. After nearly 30 minutes of searching and scavenging, we had pooled enough resources to craft us each some minimally decent gear. We knew that if we wanted to progress any further we would need to mine boulders, and a lot of them. I used what remaining materials we had to put together a 9mm handgun and several bullets, though I reminded him it was only in case we really needed it. I had decided earlier during my many unwanted experiences with bullets to the face that I would try my hardest not to run around slaughtering every newly spawned player that I came across. A few minutes out from camp we had encountered a player with a hunting bow. I had been running with my hatchet out, so I quickly took out the handgun in my inventory and pointed it in his direction, attempting to scare him away. When the player was far enough away we continued up a road towards a few stones. The area was surrounded by trees so I opted to stand guard with the handgun while my friend mined. Just as we were moving on to the next boulder, I heard the gunfire start. I turned around to see a player with an assault rifle gunning down my friend, and before I could land any shots on him he had already begun shooting me. It was at that moment that I remembered I hadn't even crafted a sleeping bag for the camp, as that was one of the objectives of the trip we were taking. I typed into the chat, thanking the friend I had made for all of his help and asking the player who had killed us if we had been intruding in his area or something along those lines. He simply wrote "Sorry guys :D" This is the single problem that I have with games like this. Why does it have to be "shoot-on-sight?" That player had obviously taken us by surprise and was better equipped than us. Even if he had a justifiable reason for approaching two very poorly equipped players (which he really didn't considering we were in the middle of the woods and he had pretty much all of the gear you could need in this game) he could have easily told us to cooperate by either putting away our weapons or just leaving the area. But of course, he comes around, sees some players trying to gather enough supplies to get to a stable point in the game, and decides to go out of his way to approach us and use unecessary ammo for a hatchet and a handgun with four bullets. Then, to add even more of an insult, he adds an apology at the end, as if he had no choice but to shoot two unexpecting, half-naked, unprepared players.
All in all, though, I do see a lot of potential in this game, and the good in the community does shine through every once in a while. I just wish that people would realize that they don't need to go around killing players who haven't had the chance to experience the game. People like that are the single reason why so many players on steam feel that they wasted money on what would otherwise be a great experience.

It's Rust. It's what you expected when you heard about it long ago. It's a game where you're thrown in to a huge world with just a rock, and you have to survive. Essentially, it's a game where you're a naked caveman trying to live and avoiding and/or killing other naked cavemen. That being said, do NOT go into this solo, as it is not meant to be played as such. The possibilities of things you can do and things you can craft are near endless, until some asshat shoots you and you die and lose all your stuff. Be sure to bring a buddy and help each other survive, but don't kill each other. Death holds a lot of meaning in this game, so if you don't like that, steer clear of Rust. It's still in alpha, which means it has a lot of room for improvement, and it has a ton of potential. It's a really great game if you're into surviving and killing other people to dominate their stuff. That being said, don't be the asshat who picks a fight he/she can't win. Because then everyone will hate you. Overall, this is a game that is definitely worth trying. Might as well get it in alpha, because you don't know if the price may go up when it goes into beta or releases. It's worth the 20 bucks, just make sure you take precautions to ensure your survival. Oh yeah, servers may be a little laggy or slow depending on your computer, but it'll get better as the game develops. Definitely well hyped, another great gem by Garry. 8.5/10 (Alpha Ver.)

Let me start out by saying, this game is right now in Alpha.  That means gameplay is subject to change and anything you might see in the game now could be gone in a few weeks.
I came into this game not knowing anything about it, just a buddy that told me to try it out.  I did, and I'm having a blast.
I was trying to write the Pro's and Con's to the game, but when I think about it, every part of the game can be thrown in both.
The community, which can be an absolute nightmare, is very rewarding once you find people you trust.  Now keep in mind, I've already had this community coming into the game.  I can imagine it is even more rewarding if you find people you can actually trust.  The people in this game write the story for you.  This is what people complain about, but define your gameplay experience.  You are surviving, and the people are your number one threat.  Keep your distance if alone, and get a damn place to put your stuff ASAP.  I would suggest learning the game on a low population server.  Don't expect a good time jumping into a server with 100+ people.  You will die a lot, and frequently.
Building: great for making a base you can defend, but a nightmare for getting a lot of people into it.  If you want your base to be secure, you're going to need to need a LOT of material.  You're going to need a lot of metal doors.  If you build your place out of wood, you will need to make sure any wooden walls are not exposed to important places inside your base.  A couple explosive charges and someone will be in your base and looting everything you worked hard to get.  Our base has multiple levels with doors at the top of stairs. You can't blow through ceilings, so at the top of the stairs we have 3 or 4 metal doors (if the stairs are on the outer wall you don't need to protect one side.)  All of the important stuff you want to keep is at the top.
Building explosive charges is expensive and time consuming, so the more layers of protection will make it that much harder to breach.  Only the person who puts the door down can use it.  This is annoying.  We've had to make multiple layer paths into the base in order to accommodate for each new player from our community who wants to join up.  Then only a few people can actually get to the top levels without needing help getting access (opening those doors).  I hear they are adding access codes which will allow multiple people to use these doors.  This will make fortifying much better and until then this part of the game is a hassle.
Resource gathering, go with people.  Go armed but only bring things you don't care about losing.  It might even help making a small base to retreat to or a place to dump your stuff down in intervals.
Know your surroundings.  If you know there is a clan that has a huge base and is very active.  I wouldn't go knocking on their door to see whats up.  They probably already know you're there and will kill anyone coming up to their place.  This is what our group does, and we guard the resources near our base.  We communicate a lot and we guard our territory very heavily.  Don't expect to take over a territory alone.  You'll need to scout and use your in game voice to discover things to help you out from other players.   If an airdrop is near you, expect a firefight.  They have explosives that you can't learn on your own or from blueprint drops.  You need a research kit and loot/learn one of these explosives to learn how to make the charges entirely.
We are the end game.  Our group has managed to make a name for ourselves, and the entire server knows who we are and where we're located.  While it kind of sucks hitting the ceiling and having pretty much everything we can get.  The only option is to raid bases and take other's stuff while defending/fortifying your own.
The game promotes aggression to the core so expect an aggressive community.
TL;DR - Stay with friends, make friends, build a strong base.  Learn everything.  Be smart.  Stay safe.  Be prepared for anything. Expect madness.  You will die... a lot.

Here are my initial impressions of the game. Its in alpha, but seems to be relatively bugfree, just content light at the moment.
My first hour in the game went like this: Spawn, get some wood, run around looking for stone, find one node, get killed by player, spawn again, find one node of stone, get killed by player, spawn, get killed by wolf. I jumped around to a couple other servers, having similar results.
But finally on the fourth attempt and server, I manage to finally find 2 nodes of stone without dying, make a stone hatchet, but then realize I'm going to die of starvation. I run around looking for wildlife til I'm at zero food and I start losing health. Finally in desperation, I run toward a big, player built house. 2 people in armor come up to me, point guns at me. I use built in voice chat to ask them if I could trade all my metal and sulfur for some food. They give me 10 food, which is enough to last for several hours. I thank them and run off. That same player runs into me two more times, checking me out to see if I'm trouble, and ends up helping me two more times, finally giving me a pistol and 9 bullets.
By the end of my first 3 hours, I finally have a little wood shack, a campfire, crafting bench, a sleeping bag for a respawn point, and a storage crate with a decent amount of supplies.
So, do I recommend this game? I think it highly depends on who you run into in the game, whether you enjoy the initial hours or not. Or, you could bring a RL friend in with you, and then once you finally find each other in the wilderness, you'll have a blast, assuming you like tense, challenging survival games. Either way, once you get over that initial painful beginning process (and definitely check out a guide to help with your first hours), you just might have a blast with it.
TL:DR - Extremely hard game that needs more content and some difficulty balancing for the first hours. Bring a friend. And remember that its in alpha right now, but has lots of potential, IMO

You awaken, with only a rock and a torch. You learn to gather wood for a fire and shelter. Then you later start to gather stone to make tools for hunting and gathering. You soon find animals, you hunt for a bit. With the food and cloth you feed yourself and conjure a sleeping bag. Nightfall approaches, you stay inside and stay warm. Later on you see sunrise, you seek for better surroundings, so you grab your belongings and head on. You come across an irradiated filled town, you start to feel strange but you want to search the area for interesting items. You luck out and find a pistol with some ammo, but the radiation becomes too unbearable to last much longer. You escape the town and try to recover while suddenly you come across a group of zombies too fast to run away from, so you grab your pistol and try to stop them. While taking considerable damage you manage to rid of the zombies and come out with some blueprints for weapons. While the day is still young you venture forward only to stumble upon a valley filled with rock and wood, you quickly find a place to make shelter then start gathering. Not long after the sun starts to settle, so you take what you gathered and quickly went back to your shelter and stored what you have. During the night you think of a plan for your new house with the materials you just collected. Come morning you get started, thinking to make a bunker to put the most rare of tresures and to leave a place for your workbench and furnace. You realize that its getting late and you need some sleep, so you head to your shack and rest.....
You awaken with only a rock and a torch and realize, you had died. Someone had killed you while you were asleep and took everything you worked hard for....but, you spent more hours gathering supplies, hunting, looting, making friends, making enemies, and most of all, surviving.
This is Rust.

The twisting of DayZ and Minecraft with its own spin on immersing the player in an evolving world. To be able to build and craft, you have to survive. What has surprised me the most is how diverse the game mechanics are from the first hour of playtime to the point where guns and ammo are common tools.
The start out of your game is the "Naked" stage which literally means you are naked physically and metaphorically. You have no food or clothes, but you do have a rock. This rock is your weapon, tool, and the stepping stool to survival. Maybe you'll be randomly killed by another player, or perhaps a wolf will chase you down. If you're unlucky enough the area you search will have no resources availiable dooming you to starvation.
When you actually do find your niche in the world, you will prosper. Ypur humble abode will come together, and you'll soon discover the key to survival isn't just food and clothing anymore. Guns and a Bow will ensure that Zombies and players are fair game.
Players will make or break your happy experience. I found a group of survivors that took me in and we became rulers of a valley until a lone gunman used his superior skills and resources to wipe us off the face of the island. Another incident had a raider haunt our house for an entire night until we fought back unsuccessfully.
Rust is kind of game you have play with people, cooperation or competition is the best way to describe the interactions within the game.

You've probably heard this before, but if you enjoy DayZ (or even the idea of it) along with the inventory managment/crafting aspect of Minecraft set in an MMO world. There's a high chance you'll enjoy this game. The biggest issue with Rust is not with the game itself, but rather the community. Everyone has a "shoot on sight" mentality and there's a very good chance you'll get frustrated rather quickly. Sticking with it however, will bring great satisfaction and reward. Rust is harsh. You start off with nothing but a rock and you must mine and gather resources to start building a home and protect yourself. Many things can be crafted at the start of the game, but you'll find loads of blueprints out in the world that will allow you to craft additional: guns, mods, survival gear along with many other items. It does take quite some time before you even get enough materials together to even protect yourself from vetern users in your server. So chances are, you're going to spend 20-30min gathering items just to be killed and have to restart.
There is PVE servers (official and community made), some of which are more of a trust system hoping others follow the rules, but there are servers were you simple cannot kill other players. If you really want to enjoy this game, you're better off starting there. Get a feel and understanding of the game and how everything works. Find the quickest ways to get what you need to be safe out in the real world. Then take on PVP. Of course, this is an Alpha, So for example: all meats are labled chicken breast, you can't tear down built items, along with a few minor graphical and animation bugs. On the bright side, it's rather stable and you can spend hours upon hours playing, getting lost within the game forgetting it's an alpha. If you have patients, and enjoy what you've read so far, $20 is a steal.

The twisting of DayZ and Minecraft with its own spin on immersing the player in an evolving world. To be able to build and craft, you have to survive. What has surprised me the most is how diverse the game mechanics are from the first hour of playtime to the point where guns and ammo are common tools.
The start out of your game is the "Naked" stage which literally means you are naked physically and metaphorically. You have no food or clothes, but you do have a rock. This rock is your weapon, tool, and the stepping stool to survival. Maybe you'll be randomly killed by another player, or perhaps a wolf will chase you down. If you're unlucky enough the area you search will have no resources availiable dooming you to starvation.
When you actually do find your niche in the world, you will prosper. Ypur humble abode will come together, and you'll soon discover the key to survival isn't just food and clothing anymore. Guns and a Bow will ensure that Zombies and players are fair game.
Players will make or break your happy experience. I found a group of survivors that took me in and we became rulers of a valley until a lone gunman used his superior skills and resources to wipe us off the face of the island. Another incident had a raider haunt our house for an entire night until we fought back unsuccessfully.
Rust is kind of game you have play with people, cooperation or competition is the best way to describe the interactions within the game.

We are animals, only more sheltered and civilized. But in here, you either become an animal, or die a human. Ever wondered what it's like to be a caveman? Here's your chance! Rust was an interesting experience.
Starting off with a rock, torch, and a few bandages. You feel kind of helpless as you see how massiv the world is around you. But the experiences I had in the span of a few days with this game have got me hooked for life.
I started out mashing pigs with my rock to creating massive bases and going out for wood/supply runs. Zombie hunting, player raiding. The interactions you have with other players is one of its most redeeming qualities.
Rust caught my attention/fascination like minecraft did when I first got it back in Alpha. It was something new, interesting, and fun. Rust is an awesome new spin on the sandbox survival genre and there is a TON of potential for it moving forward. I can easily say I'm excited for its future.

This game is amazing. It takes Minecraft and puts into a realistic world, that is massivley online. I only have one problem with this game, pvp servers, I do not play on them there are servers you can play on that take away the pvp.
*Edit after having more hours on the game*
In the previous version of this review I said that I hated the PVP. This was only because I did't have very much experience on the game and I did't know how the PVP worked at the time, and after having over 100 hours on the game I see that the PVP is actually really fun. there are really good raiding mechanics also, because it is actually pretty balanced. Just about the only way to break into a house is to get C4, which is very hard to obtain, and most of the time it will take 2 - 3 C4 to break down a wall, whilst metal doors take 4 - 5. The PVP is actually pretty tactical, as you can be offed with a single shot to the head, and just a few shots to the torso. I still do recommend PVE servers to new players, just because the game takes a little getting used to like how the mechanics work, just because the game is actually pretty unique as far as survival games go, but overall I have had a TON of fun with this game and really love it. If you are looking for a good survival game with an option of PVE or PVP, then this game is the way to go in my eyes.
There are also lots of updates to come for this game, so you will get bored of the game, just to come back and see that there was an update. Making you want to play the game again to see all of the new features that they have added. There is one factor that might put off some players, the game as of now is only online, so there is no single player included, and the servers for the game are about $20 USD a month if you want to make you own, which to some people is very pricey.

Even though I haven't played this game for long, I can allready say that this game has real potential! The community is unbelievable nice. I was playing on a server with 60 people and instead of shooting me, they give me food, show me where I am and help me out as a noob.... and that on an PVP server.
The crafting system is ok, but needs more content for lategame. Collecting blueprints takes quite a while but it's possible with a group of people and are usually found in the ressource drops. (with the plane)
That drops also make fun situations, as everyone is searching for it and gives you a hunger games feeling but really less deadly as you would imagine it.
With good weapon gameplay and a mature and friendly community this game is going to be a good game and with Garry behind it, there's no chance that it will fail!

(Old)The gameplay per se is nice, the community is not. I've played games like this one, WarZ..DayZ but this annoys me more than ever. This is still an early access but if they want to keep the buyers in their game the developers should fix the situation, where a newbie gets killed over and over again and you either play with friends and have fun or you play alone and you struggle to survive because shoot on sight is the n1 rule in this kind of game. Remove the guns, make them much more hard to craft because right now zombies are not even a close threat and it's just a pvp deathmatch between raids of people (3-6) and random guys who just like to build their own houses but in the end they always get killed and griefed. Edit 06/02/2016: 2 years later and I have the chance to play this again, with friends. The game improved a lot, I quite like the new cartoonish style. The blueprint system is great and the building system is intuitive and smooth, you can build (almost) impenetrable bases... IF you survive long enough. Public servers are ok, we decided to build in the worst area of the island (only wood, no stone nearby so its harder to upgrade your walls) and we managed survive, somehow.
The community is still the same even if I saw some spark of humanity this time, like people trading blueprints for wood/stone but other than that its shoot first ask questions later, period. AND DON'T TRUST NAKED GUYS.
I admit I had fun this time around, the game changed, mostly for the better and with friends you share both the fun and the pain togheter.
If you wanna get this game then ask yourself this question:
Do you feel like investing your never coming back hours of your life in a game where at any point, even when you log off you risk to lose your 60+ hours of gameplay sometimes without having the chance to fight back? If yes then go ahead, its gonna be a bumpy ride.

In the previous version of this review I said that I hated the PVP. This was only because I did't have very much experience on the game and I did't know how the PVP worked at the time, and after having over 100 hours on the game I see that the PVP is actually really fun. there are really good raiding mechanics also, because it is actually pretty balanced. Just about the only way to break into a house is to get C4, which is very hard to obtain, and most of the time it will take 2 - 3 C4 to break down a wall, whilst metal doors take 4 - 5. I still do recommend PVE servers to new players, just because the game takes a little getting used to like how the mechanics work, just because the game is actually pretty unique as far as survival games go, but overall I have had a TON of fun with this game and really love it. I very badly want to love this game. 95% of it is brilliant! One of the best open-world, sandbox-style games I've ever seen. But the 5% of bad is really a game-breaker.
I understand that this is Alpha and will be sticking it out hoping these things get improved. In detail: I LOATHE the lack of protection for logging out. This game penalizes you for sleeping, working, or doing anything else IRL. To be successful in this game you would literally need to replace your real life with it. When you log out you face-plant on the ground much like in the movie "Avatar" - leaving your body and everything you're carrying vulnerable to anyone who can get to you. I support that there is no way to completely defend your base from raiders and would never ask for that to be changed, but it is utterly soul-crushing to start with absolutely nothing every time you log in.
I understand that this was implemented to prevent "combat-logging", however there are other games that have already solved this problem. Things such as log-out timers have been implemented for ages. Create an active timer counting down from 2 minutes (or another arbitrary time value) and have the character disappear after that time. Provide the same static wait time upon a d/c/alt+f4.
TLDR: Though I love the old-school style punishments for failure this game is TOO punishing. Don't expect to be successful unless you can LITERALLY live within it's world.
P.S.
As a secondary minor issue, metal is far too rare given how important it is to the game. More spawns, or ability to pick at mountains the way we pick at trees.

EDITED REVIEW:
Rust went from being a half finished game with a world of potential to a half finished game with no potential and no direction. Still being gradually updated, but the vibrance the original game had is gone and the devs seem to have decided to follow the loudest minority instead of the patient majority, resulting in a massive exodus of players.
Game is as buggy as it was 6 months ago, and has been remade from the ground up at least once, but every iteration of it seems less interesting and more grindy.
ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW.
If you're waiting for Dayz, stop, this is better. Not much more to be said.
But, it is in early alpha.
Be aware that it is in alpha, and from the looks of the upcoming updates, it may well turn into "one of thooooose games"
Weapon sway, ultra realism, die in two shorts, injuries...
but none of the realism that's fun.
So you'll hit a rock with another rock and amazingly, it just turns into metal suitable for gun manufacturing at that wooden table over there miraculously.
But then you point that gun at an enemy, and suddenly you have alzheimers, a blood clot, have been running for half an hour, it's 20 below zero and you're a particuarly shaky person.

Rust is by far the most impressive early access/alpha build games I've ever bought. Just the fact that it's alpha, but the lighting is magnificent and there are so many features that seem so fluid already. I spent my whole afternoon playing this with friends, and in that time, I'd found my friend, we then killed zombies for blue-prints and looted the nearby radtown constantly building up a nice supply of items, we made an alliance with two friendly players whom helped us out immensely, we met up with another 2 friends, and then we started making out base. It's funny though, we ended up with the best weapons we could get, surplus ammunition, decent clothing, and a whole host of weapon addons, but we we're still defeated by zombies when we went on an expedition. This game is really about survival, no matter what you have, you can still be as easily killed as the next guy over. The periodic supply drops are interesting, hearying the plane go overhead, watching the cannisters parachute to the ground, and then running in that direction hoping to find them before any other players, though it can be quite frustrating when they land on mountains that have no way of climbing.
If you have a bunch of friends to play this with, I would highly recommend buying Rust, sure it's fun solo, but it's worth it to play with friends and to co-ordinate and build large fortress-like bases. The upcoming features are really going to make this game stand out from all the other survival games on the market.

UPDATE: Oh look, Rust is being wiped out and started over again from scratch. I guess you 500 people who disliked this review feel pretty stupid at this point, huh.
Shame the game has been made with 99% of the exact same disgusting development mindset, but now instead of having the option to dedicate time and effort to harvest materials, your progress is instead capped on a daily basis through rétarded time-set spawns for both rock deposits, animals and even moreso random blueprints dropped from barrels that are required for literally everything past flimsy stone buildings with physical keys (that drop when you die) to your doors while deathmatching and utter devastation of anyone that is even remotely new on a server is more prevalent than ever. It also manages to run like absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on even the most beefiest of computers.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
An excellent example on how you can take an absolute brilliant piece of concept and turn it to utter rubbish by messing up the execution part. Rust is so severely plagued with moro nic developer decisions, It's physically and mentally painful to play it for more than an hour.
Starting off right from the bat is the horrible community. Trolls, griefers, "Bandits" and hackers make up for most of the population as any new player entering the game will be utterly bullied down to the ground without remorse by the veteran players, simply looking to kill some time with a near-infinite amount of hi-tech guns, ammo and bodyarmor, all made by hand. "Testing" phase or not, the percentage alone of people looking to simply ruin the experience for others is stomach sickening and we have the pacing of the game to thank for that which is expanded upon more below.
Second major issue with this game is how fast you can turn from slapping a rock against a tree to a gun-blazing maniac with hundreds of bullets. All you need is some iron ore, stone and wood, all being open for grabs within the first couple of seconds of playing as slamming your free starting tool against a nearby rock deposit will supply you with 66% of the ingredients, trees (that are everywhere) being the remaining 33% and you're good to go to create weapons that can 1-2 hit any fully-armored newbie player from 25 feet away making the game a thing of deathmatching rather than a case of actual survival against nature and all It's elements & trials since resources are nowhere close to being scarce. I wrecked up about 400 units of metal ore within 2 hours of first setting my foot into the game and that's enough to build over 15+ firearms with ammo to boot considering I also had significant amounts of sulfur (all being harvested from the same, generic rock deposits)  which is a compontent to create gunpowder.
Third problem would be the game mechanics. Glitching through doors & walls is more than a common occurance, leaving most methods of banking extremely unsafe and when player constructions aren't as easy as butter to go through with either hacks or abuse, they are instead utterly impenetrable in the form of having Metal doors (also, very easy to make) that require over 11-15 blank-range hand grenades to be destroyed or 3+ plastic explosives which are one of the most expensive items in the entire game.
This means you'll not only need some of the most rare recipes there is in order to even be able to break into other people's houses without wooden doors but you also need to grind SIGNIFICANTLY to even have a chance to raid any half-decent base that has more than a single metal door. 3 C4 costs over 900 gunpowder to make (amongst other things) so If you plan to raid a mediocre house with say, 5 metal doors in it (which requires only 1000 metal fragments and some wood), you'll need:
------------
4500 Gunpowder (2250 Charcoal + 2250 Sulfur / 400 Sulfur Ore)
2250 Metal fragments (450~ Metal Ore)
1125 Sulfur (200~ Sulfur Ore)
450 Low-Grade Fuel (900 Animal fat + 450 Cloth)
25 Leather
15 Flares
------------
Just those numbers of supplies will hopefully come across as a lot, even for those of you who haven't even played the game yet. And all of these requirements for C4 makes the alternative of hoarding up on a whole bunch of ammo, building a tower in a populated area and then taking pot-shots to 2-3 hit kill whatever person/newbie that comes within 1-2 miles of range a routine no-brainer time-killing choice for anyone who played the game for more than 6-10 hours on one server. And If you play on a server with decay activated, (which a majority of all servers currently have, about 70-90%) just waiting for someone's house to wither away is a much more viable method than spending days upon days on mindlessly grinding supplies for explosives as can be witnessed by the common scenario of someone raiding with C4 and being laughed at in the global chat due to the cost to gain ratio.
And as described vaguely above, there's also a rather dumb rule where you need to find "Blueprints" in order to create anything more advanced than an 9mm pistol/dirty shotguns/cloth armor which you find rarely by looting world-crates and red bears & wolves which are often complete suicide missions for any newbie due to the rampaging deathmatching going on everywhere. But suicide or not, if you do find a blueprint, you can simply "use" it and your character will learn it permanently even through death which may sound like a good idea at first until you realize that every guy who played on the server before you will have an insane, massive advantage with that development decision in place, easily being able to create high-tech body armor and assault rifles as you are constricted to recoil-heavy 9mm's & dirty shotguns while wearing clothed diapers.
One may argue for a skilled FPS/Survivalist player, this would not be much of an issue.. Except the health & damage system in this game is so depressingly shallow, restricting itself to "Health points" and "Statuses" such as bleed being thrown at you during certain injuries which can instantly be healed by consuming bandages. It's the same disgusting design philosophy seen in games such as The War Z where you can jump around like a complete psycho & hide and wolf down health-kits like nobodies business.
Sure, this may seem acceptable at first but when you are facing an overwhelming foe and say, you headshot him 3 times in the head with your 9mm pistol as he ambushes you with an assault rifle from a nearby tower and he still doesnt die but instead rub his buttocks to the left a few inches, healing back to full HP within seconds, there's something seriously wrong with the game. Throw a grenade if you have one you say if they're behind cover? Sorry, but they are completely useless as you require up to 3 consecutive, blank-range exploding grenades to have a chance of killing someone UNARMORED. If they have any range from the explosion impact and armor while healing, you could be talking about tossing 15 of them and still have nothing happen.
For this game to have ANY hope whatsoever, the developers will need to REALLY re-think a majority of the decisions they've made, be it making guns a RARITY (as there are other ranged weapons like bow & arrow which require actual skill to use) while remaking the method of raiding others or revamping the entire health system completely to have things such as infections, concussions, broken bones and bruising instead of the current, despicable health-kit mouth-absorbing simulator that has no longevity other than mindless grind of ores and certain blueprints while bum-rushing naked to airdrops in hope to get explosives to even have a chance to raid other people's houses which currently litter every inch of the current Rust map before disappearing into thin air rather than having any meaningful player interaction.
