Keep in mind that this game is in very early development. Also, the fact that beta access is purchasable this early into the games production is a little worrysome as it could be a sign of financial problems. After some time playing this game my review is as follows:
Rust is a Hardcore, Single-player, Multiplayer, PvP, PvE, Survival, Sandbox based game in which the first 5 minutes into the game is spent running from the horrible community that currently plagues it. The main spawn area is plagued with freshly created characters killing each other and your only hope for surivial is to run. Don't run towards any buildings though because if you do you will be greeted by Rust's vicinity based voice chat and a shotgun to the face.
If you do manage to find someplace relatively sparse of other players and the few that are near you are friendly then you might be able to smack some trees and build yourself a small shelter. Of course that won't be much use because you quickly strave to death because you didn't build yourself a hatchet which is absolutely necessary to obtain meat off an animals bones, (That is if you found an animal to kill in the first place).
The lack of direction, horrific community, laggy servers, badly designed enviroments, and terrible AI make Rust a not so fun game. But the potential of this game is sky high and because it is in very early stages of development it could evolve into something much better than the current state. This is a game that should be watched closely, but approached with caution.

Well, I've got 15 hours put into this game so far in the 2 days that I've owned it and from that... I've noticed a lot of bad things about the game so far, a lot more than good things... I know the game is only in Alpha, but a lot of what I write in this review probably won't get corrected. But for the record, this isn't my official review of the game... as maybe I'm currently just having a bad experience with it so far.
Pros:
Voice chat with a limited distance to a player is a nice feature. There are a few nice players in the game which try to help new players out a little by giving them armors and weapons. Whether you like the game or completely hate it, if you love the survival aspect of it, then it is somewhat addictive. It is fairly difficult to handle the recoil of the guns which I like cuz it adds a need for skills to handle them properly. The survival aspect of the game seems to be well done in the sense that you can get cold, hungry, bleed to death from a bear or zombie attack, etc... and you always have fear on the brain because you never know who will attack from where or if a zombie or bear will pop out of nowhere to attack you.
Cons:
Editing game options hardly works at all: Raising or lowering graphics detail does nothing, only resolution changes have any effect, editing control options before launching the game does nothing as you need to change it again once in the game, and the in-game UI seems to have minor issues too and feel too basic. Half the players are bandits and shoot on sight or pretend to be friendly until your guard is down for just a second. The map may be big, but the terrain all looks the same... it's so ridiculously easy to get lost in the game or lose the spot where you placed your base. Also, while the map is big, it still always feels crowded with players even with a 50 player limit. There's only 1 non-PvP server out of hundreds and it's only 128 players and is always full so don't ever expect to be able to force your way in there. There's no way of knowing which player killed you or trying to kill you unless you were up close to him and had a chance to see the name before dying... The detail in graphics are only slightly better than 7D2D (although they have plans to greatly improve that) and yet it requires so much more out of your GPU (first game I've ever needed to lower my resolution and even then could only average 45fps until a gun fight breaks out lowering it to about 20fps). All the good items in the game require you either find blueprints or find research kits which seem to be extremely rare because I never once found one in the 15 hours of play and I explored a lot and visited the rad cities a lot. Night time leaves you 100% blind or if you use a torch or flashlight or make a fire, makes you a really easy target for bandit players... therefore the only safe option is to hide for 20 minutes of the game in total darkness until it's daytime again which is really boring. No matter how much effort you put into making your base secure, they'll always get in the moment you log out... or will destroy the base with C4 with you in it... The few players who are friendly are so nervous that even they sometimes shoot on sight out of fear of being raided... It's just a game loaded with frustration and stupidity... speaking of stupidity... I shot a naked guy in the head with a 9mm 3 times and he was still trying to attack me with a rock (then the bear clipped through the floor and killed me). Wearing a complete set of leather armor hardly protects against bullets... you still die in 1 or 2 seconds depending on attacker's aiming skill and it requires so much effort to make the armor so in the end, you're better off just running around naked and pretending to be weak since you have pretty much the same chances of survival in a gun fight. And new players with nothing worth mentioning in inventory and completely naked get killed for no reason, they have no weapons and give clear signs of non-hostility (jumping and/or voicing friendy in chat), bandit players seem to kill anything that is near them and are always in groups so you tend to not stand a chance against them even when in your base. Animals can clip through structures to get to you without warning (can reach you on the top floor while the bear is underneath). In the 15 hours of play, I still felt as though I had nothing worth fighting for in my base... I was so limited because I couldn't find blueprints that I needed or even a research kit to be able to make my own blueprints. PvE is a bit challenging at first until you have your first true weapon, then they become easy prey (if they remove zombies from the game, PvE will really have nothing left in terms of challenge, so they'd need to add something else to take it's place). You're very limited in how you can build your base in terms of materials used, where the walls and doors can be placed, if there's terrain clipping through the foundation, you can't place anything near it, etc...
In the game's current state, I'd rate the game below average and is no competitor of 7 Days to Die because 7D2D, which is also in Alpha, has so much more variety in every meaning of the word and effort put into the game and allows players to fully customize their servers and you even have the option to play offline which is still lots of fun because PvE is being designed really well. I haven't tried DayZ Standalone yet, but I hear that game has just as many issues right now, so maybe DayZ is a good competitor with this game. I might put in a few more hours into this game later on if I can find a non PvP server that isn't always full, but till then, I kind of regret buying this game, especially at full price too. While $20 isn't a total rip-off, knowing what I know now, I wouldn't have paid more than $5 - $10 for it.

My opinion in short: Already quite a great game despite a few drawbacks, with lots of potential to become truly awesome!
Critic and ideas:
- Sleepers: Mostly favors the "veterans" and a demotivation for starting up. I say this because  team-working players, or even just great solo-players, will always  have so much items that it's really not possible to combat-log with all your valuables, so they will lose quite a lot anyways, but beginners and intermediate players will lose everything in an attack, and probably quit the server. If great groups of people get to keep something after an attack, they will more likely rebuild and continue faster, and that way endgame will be more balanced and probably be more enjoyable. At least fix the server list so it shows if a server has sleepers or not, cause server names don't always tell.
- PvE: Perhaps remove the ability to kill other players, and remove the ability to destroy objects you have not built yourself. This way it is actually possible to learn something while playing with others, instead of finding a totally unpopulated server just to try to enjoy the game and learn.
- Animals and zombies: The fact that these tend to keep to certain locations can turn things quite dull, in my mind. It could be that making all creatures roam and spawn randomly, og at least larger groups moving around, would make things more interesting and unpredictable.
- Multiple owners of a house: Perhapse making keys and adding a key-pouch of some sort, so multiple people can open a door, or similar.

There are very few games that can leave a gamer with a lasting real emotional impression which borders surprisingly close to reality. The type of feeling you have after a real life event which changes the way you look at things..... Rust so far, has been one of those games.

I have only been exposed to the Alpha and only have 6-8 hours invested but must say it is certainly going to be one that will consume many hours of my life as it grows into a polished and complete game title.
Even though this game title is only in Alpha at the time of this review, I give it 4 out of 5 Stars.

**Updated review**
Ok... so i admit that my previous review may have been somewhat harsh, but i have to say that any game that stirs this kind of emotion in me now days, deserves some further attention. Indeed this last week for the game has been interesting for the developers with the router and ddos issues they have been having. However, aside from attackers making the game all but unplayable for many folks, the dev team rolled out many new updates (sometimes several daily). Lets not forget it was prime holiday season too... So my hats off to the team and their devotion to moving the game forward. Updates fixed a number of issues for players, including my inability to connect to most of the servers. So, I'm inclined to to change my rating and make this a positive recomendation for players who want something different, (and initially) very challenging. This game does offer many different elements to appease many different player styles and preferences. The trick now seems to get players to immerse themselves long enough to discover the hidden treasures this alpha title has to offer. On another note, im looking forward to the modding communities response to this game. Garry (of garys mod) has stated that this game will be readily moddable as the game moves forward (in fact there are some mods already available!). This should make for fun and diverse playing environments and configs!

Of course once i built a campfire and figured out how to use it, i was disconnected for no apparent reason and never was able to reconnect again.... Not my idea of a fun game but I do enjoy the minecraft survival style play idea (with upgraded graphics), though it is nowhere near being a fun playable experience in my opinion. Think ill just wait a few months and try again. maybe my opinion will change after all the paying alpha testers have solved some of their problems for them...

This game is all about survival of the fittest. Unfortunately, unlike natural selection, the less fit individuals are equally as important as the fittest, because their money is just as good. The game seemingly does not care one bit about that.
In most online shooters, not being an elite player does not mean you cannot enjoy yourself, but in Rust it absolutely does, because you will be forced to start over from scratch over and over again with nothing but a rock to defend yourself with. It's a long, luck-based and extremely dull PvE grind that locks you out from the game's only saving grace: the shooting. It's a grind that will quickly shift your perception of the crafting system from 'look at this impenetrable fortress I have crafted!' to 'how quicky can I build a 1x1 house with a metal door so I can craft my first gun in peace?'.

This game is pretty fun, it has pretty much everthing you could want in a zombie survival game. It has a good crafting system that is much more free than others of the same genre and the recipes are fairly easy to find. It has the aspects that you will normally find in a game like mining rocks for ores and stones, cutting trees for wood and hunting animals for food and items such as animal fat, leather and cloth. The open world has a great amount of buildings that you can scavenge for goodies such as blueprints for better armor, guns and building materials, but also can give you better weapons, armor and food outright. The world has sections of irradiated wasteland that you need to get special armor to get through but the rewards are generally much better as well. The zombies are a little simplistic right now but they dangerous none the less and since this is early alpha, it is subject to change. There are still a few bugs and a couple optimization issues that are being worked on and the crafting system is still relatively small but they are working on adding more. All in all this a game you should seriously look into buying, especially if youve been dissapointed in the survival crafting genre. This game aims to not dissapoint.

I was taken in by a kind, naked man the first night, and together we ate chicken and kept warm by the fire.  The next morning I said my goodbyes and left the shack, in search of my own adventure.  That is exactly what I got.
This game is amazing, it's pretty hard to start out, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be hunting deer, defending your base and raiding enemies, as well as making friends on the way.  Highly recommend this game to those who like minecraft, or games like DayZ as it is these games merged into one.
I was skeptical at first, but I really love this game.  You don't need steam friends to play with, because there are many players in the servers who are willing to team up with you and help you , although there are a few bandits).
As of now, I found a community of friendly people and they have helped supply me and my friend to make sure we can survive and raid with them (Which is very fun and exciting!)
There is no 'endgame'.  A challenge will always be available.  You may think you have the best clan, but you will be challenged and inevitably defeated, which adds excellent replaybility and requires you to start with less gear, or restart ENTIRELY!
So yeah, give this alpha 8.5/10

I think the best short description of this game is "Minecraft meets WarZ" or Infestation, how it`s called by now...
You wake up with a stone in your hands and if you haven`t watched a video or have any other information you have no indication of what you are supposed to do and you will die by a zombie. The next try you will be killed by a bear because you`re running from a full equipped guy who is hunting you. On the next day a wolf will kill you. This is not very encouraging but if you stick around you will learn very fast what to do, once you know where to go and how to avoid threats and defend yourself.
Once you`ve got the basics of the game you want to start crafting and building your home. I really like that you have to find blueprints to learn how to build thing because who knows how to build weapon attachments? The reverse-engineering part is also a great idea and makes it a bit easier to learn everything you want. It should be self implied that you have to learn everything again, once you decide to play on another server. The building system is really great and intuitive. You will learn really quickly how to build your own base and I have seen almost evrything you can imagine, from small 1x1x1 cubes over insanely high wood towers with a 2x2 foundation to gigantic metal castles.
Except for a few animals everything that moves will kill you. If you want to play alone you should play on a low-pop server but even then you will probably die often. Every Server I played on so far has one or two dominating groups that go around the map and take every base apart that looks worth raiding or looks like it could be a threat later. I have to say though, I don`t play alone but in a group of 4-6 people and the servers we`ve played on for more than 5 hours we become on of these groups.
Except from some minor things the biggest problem (if you want to call it that or don`t like that) in this game is that you can`t really play PVE. This is the same problem WarZ had in the beginning and maybe still has. These "Survival games" attract a lot of single players that want to be the lone wolf in the world against the zombies and the environment but they can`t because behind the next rock sits a guy with a shotgun who will shoot on sight. The thing is, almost everybody will become that guy with the shotgun because after the third time you let the guy with "only" leather trousers go unharmed and he shoots you in the back you`re starting to get tired of this and won`t let anyone do that again. To be a real PVE game these zombies are far to less a threat. After you played for an hour you won`t have any trouble dealing with them because even in the danger zones there are far to less zombies to become really dangerous.
Apart from the game itself I think a problem is some admins abusing their rights. You`re minding your own business building the interior of your base and suddenly a admin stands next to you in the closed building saying "Hi, this is my server, I`m just looking around". I wouldn`t have a problem with that but telling their friends where good places to raid are, how many people are in the building and which storage box contains the good stuff so they can grab that and be gone really quickly is no fun. I have to say, this only happened to me/us once. I`m just saying be aware and if you`re suspicious just change to another server because most of the admins I met were really nice and for the most time you won`t be able to tell who the admin is because he/she doesn`t want everybody crying for him. Not a spread problem though...
In the end I have to say, if you like or don`t mind the biggest part of the game being PVP and gathering resources to build your ultimate base and not the surviving in an unfriendly environment this is a really fun game that will chain you to your pc and it`s worth every cent you pay.

So playing the game for about an hour and a half I've come to write a review.
Now, the sole reason I purchased this game was to play with friends in the sort that'd we be able to travel together and do whatever we wanted. This is, however, not the case.
Let's start with the positive aspects (I do realize this game is in Alpha, this is for the game at its current state 12/13/13)
So joined into the server US Central 3, along with 2 other friends. We expected to be able to group up and start to tackle this game together. My wishes did not come true. You are spawned very spaciously across the map. Some might take this at a positive and some a negative. I found this a drawback in the case that at the games current state it has no minimap or compass to show you where you're headed. Unless you've been playing this game for a long time and can figure out all the landscapes and where to tell your friends to go, you wont be grouping up for a LONG time. For the 2 hours I played this game, we were unable to find eachother for the entire time. I found this a bit dissapointing as most of the time I was traveling and being beaten to death by another newbie with a rock. This is also another reason I found the start to be very annoying. Everyone is out to kill you, you're lucky if you find someone who wont kill you and in the end, they probably will end up smashing your head in. I have read that you can follow and try to meet up right under the sun or moon but after attempting this for awhile, I found it to be no use because we still could not find eachother. I would say my last issue is the server lag.
But, I still need to hand it to this game. It's in Alpha, and a damn good alpha. Being a huge Garry's mod fan I know the features and content coming out in the future will greatly improve this game. I still recommend the game because I know it will be perfection when it's finished.

Rust is an unusual game in the best way possible.  It's not terribly original, because one can sum up its premise as Minecraft meets DayZ with a side of Call of Duty.  But it takes elements from the aforementioned games and paces the gameplay in its own unique way.  It's goofy and makes no sense but in a perfectly whimsical "videogamey" attitude that is just incredibly fun and kept me playing round after round.
The premise is very much similar to DayZ and Minecraft.  You spawn in a random location on an empty safari-esque island equipped with nothing but a medkit, torch, and your only weapon being a large rock (seriously, you have nothing else on you, not even a loincloth).  With your rock you start harvesting wood, stone, and other materials which you can use to craft items and build structures to keep you alive.
Again, Rust is not original in that sense, but what makes fun compared to DayZ is the pacing.  In Rust, there always seems to be something happening around the next landmark compared to DayZ which I felt was a little too sparse in doling out rewards for players' risks.  And it's different from Minecraft in that, although building structures and crafting items are essential, the focus is on survival rather than simply being a sandbox lego game that happens to have a survival element to it.  The threat of your ever diminishing hunger meter and having to guess if the player in the distance intends or even has the means to kill you keeps the gameplay always enjoyably tense.  If you die, your body will be practically always guaranteed to be looted by whoever killed you, so you start from scratch.  Which sounds annoying at first, but it makes you value your accomplishments and your life even more everytime you spawn into the world.
The game is currently in Alpha and it is quite obvious.  Graphically, the game is aesthetically pleasing in its over the top almost cartoony style, but technically textures are low res, characters and the environment are crudely low poly.  The menu and interface are barebones but functional.  In-game chat is appropriate in that you can only hear other players that you're near to in the game world.  But performance-wise the game runs surprisingly smooth considering the support for up to 200 players per server.
All in all, even in its current state, Rust is a refreshingly different type of game amidst the sea of predictable FPS games, MOBAs, and Action RPGs.  It's not perfect by any means, but gives such an entertaining type of experience that I am willing excuse it from being perfect.  The developers promise to be making changes as development continues and I can only see changes for the better.  I paid 20 dollars for early access and so far am not regretting a single cent of it.  Highly recommend this game for anyone who wants to have some great goofy fun.

Overall, I am very disappointed with the development process this far and have given up until things are more developed.

Unlike some other early access titles on Steam (ahem, Starforge), Rust has FREQUENT updates that work & generally aren't game breaking, with active devs (see devblogs on
It's got many great features and is a game you don't get bored of - you've still always got to be careful, although those first one or two nights in game will be a little more difficult.

Rust just recently beat the all-time peak population of its game, which is very impressive considering it first debuted on Steam around ~2 years ago.
The grind in Rust isn't so bad as some say, even for solo (and if you still hate it you can play increased gather rate servers). You can get a nice stone base in like 1-2 hours. Combat is hectic and fun, and when there are things at stake it's way more adrenaline pumping.
The game is really fair, runs quite well, and isn't overly complicated like some other survival games. It's easy to learn, but can be hard to master.
I can say without a doubt as a huge survival game fan that Rust is the best survival game that I have ever played. It's seriously good, and it's worth $20 for hundreds of hours of fun.

This is my opinion based on the state of the game i last played rust. (pre-steam release)
Before you buy this game, Note that It has some pretty huge play time requirement and investment.
TLDR;
Simply put, time invested in the game is directionally proportional to how well off you will be compared to other players.
The best features in this game are probably the worst features in others eyes.
-No rules
-No admins
-No goals
-Hardcore survival (food, warmth, sickness and possibly more will be added in)
-Lose everything equipped on death
-World PvP
-Little to no incentive to group up
-Crafting
-Building (build structures based on a square grid)
You are able to claim land and build a little shack to live in, but logging out means you cant defend it when someone else is trying to break in.
Same goes for you though, see a empty house? they only have a wooden door? Well, time to see what you can steal when you break down the door.
While this game has no rules, or goals or anything to guide the player, the game play falls down to the most primitive of concepts of online games: "if i kill that guy he might drop something useful for me"
Personal skill like, knowledge of the game, accuracy and out thinking other players only plays a small part in this game.
If you have spent more time in this game then the other player, you will have had researched more items, have a stash of backup equipment should you die, and the ability to re-spawn in a location you marked with a sleeping bag. (players without sleeping bags set have random spawns in the world)
If you have a problem with spending 2 hours gathering the resources to build a home, only to have someone break into it as your logged out and steal everything you did not have in your personal inventory, then this is not the game for you.
Similarly, if you find the concept of breaking into other players homes, and stealing from them fun, then this might be the game for you.

Very fun game if you like to collect resources, improvise your weapons and fight over an airdrop from a carrier. Has it's moments of glory, but waiting 500 seconds to craft stuff can get tedious if you are considering building a big base, but it really pays off in the end with the added safety from other players.
There's a bunch of high end gear you can get if you are paitent and live long enough to make a base of operations, or risk it in the radiated industrial/military buildings where zombies/mutants of different difficulties protect some nice gear and blueprints.
4 hours in (note I played this game before Steam Release) I managed to make a small home with metal doors, get food, wood and ores. Also got a nice bow with 50 arrows, a handcannon (improvised shotgun) and some armor.
It's a good mix between Minecraft and DayZ I would say. Resource gathering, crafting and eventually building your huge fort, to hunting other animals and players and take their food, gear and loot up until you have the very best items in the game.
It is early access, and it's going to screw you over here and there. The map will sometimes reset removing your buildings, the game might crash a few times on you, but if you can look past that, it's a great experience. But if you get bored of games quickly, I suggest you wait until it's released to have a more pleasant experience.
If you're going into the world of Rust I also recommend checking out some tutorials for it. Diving into the game with no idea what to gather, how to craft or even cook food, it can get very frustating. Don't be afraid to look up a wiki or have a tutorial on your steam browser as you are playing. Fun times!

Awesome Game! But don't forget it's survival ,if u get ganked by people your loss :) . Basicly here is a small tutorial for starters , and to make a ideea before buying.
The 2 Moast Important Things:
1.I Recommend a Microphone! By the time you write friendly usually you get a bullet in the head!
2.Not all people are Friendly Be CAUTION , i recomend stay away from them!
Anyway,
U spawn naked , with  a rock , a torch , 2 first aid (first aid is used only to stop bleeding! ).
What should you do first?
-Well you start with 1250 food that should last a while but the main this is find some food (pig / chicken / rabit the only ones u can kill with rock easy) , after that gather wood (wood should be gathered if available from the wood stacks not from trees) , and finally get some stones (they help you make the stone axe wich is quite usefull and good , if u know the game you can get to that first)
-How to make a house and where?
Frist of all the idle zone for a house is near resources , zombies , and places to loot from .This is a hard question to say , there are 2 ways of building a house:
A. Build it in the midle of the resources to get them asap and raise a huge tower surounded by spikes.
B. Find a place near resources in mountains and build so it's not very visible to others (i will explain why below).
If you are the kind of person that will play this game 12/24 hours a day i sugest A. But if you play less i sugest a hidden house because the wood door breakes easy , the metal door easyer xD (don't forget doors dissapear in a few days u always have to fix them with either wood either metal fragments)..
Everything is build on rust to be destroyed easy (one thing i don't enjoy that much) , and if you play on a sleeping server (normal mode) , you have to always take care of your character where he sleeps , the house to be guarded , cause u may wake up naked again :)  .
Ok so you build your house what now?!
Search for bloody weapons it's a survival after all !  :) You can get these from:
A: Crafting (with metal , melten in the furnance)
B: Kill other players to get them (it may be hard considering u have a axe or a stone).
C: Kill zombies , this is actually not hard after you have a bow , you have to just one shot the moast. The black ones die from 4.  From zombies you can get basicly everything weapons , bules , blueprints (blueprints are used to learn stuff like leather , kevlar , m4 , 250 pistol , shotgun , F1 grenades , Explosives etc etc etc) and many many more stuff don't want to ruin surprises :) .
D: Loot places , this is the easyest asuming there are no radiations in the area ^^. Loot places have boxes that have the same drops as zombies.
Warning , if you have for example a M4 weapon from a fallen player , and you don't have the blueprint you can still learn it. How?! Well it's simple you need to have a salvage kit and paper , dropped from boxes , zombies , players.
Oh yeah and to warn you one last thing silencers  lower the range xD i died a few times not knowing.
These are actually the main and base stuff u need to know , telling more will spoil the fun. I hope you liked the review / mini guide , and have fun.

Summary: Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.     -

Rust is one of the best survival-oriented games I've ever played.
It's like Minecraft, DayZ, and Stalker combined. Minecraft on building, DayZ on harsh environments and players, and Stalker on the apocolyptic setting.
The community is what sells it. You really can't trust anybody but your friends, and even they might have a chance to backstab you. You'll find huge bases that are home to entire armies of men in powerful armor, and small forts made by a naked dude that doesn't know what's coming. Even if you're at the top of the ranks, you can still be dumbed down by raiders and bandits.
Every Thursday, there's a new update added to the game. These updates are documented, but can be a pretty good learning experience if you don't know what's coming. This way the game has a bit of freshness every Thursday. This can vary based on the size of the update, though.
The game can also produce some comedic moments. I have fond memories of a great event - My friends and I were all running up a hill naked, and I asked one of my other friends to play some tribal music. He did...but after a minute, the tribal music changed to Wiggle by Jason Derulo. You can guess where things went from there.
I would suggest buying this game if you're a fan of survival-oriented games. It's an experience you can't miss out on. To some players, this game may feel like just repeats of "get killed by man with big gun" but I can definitely say that it's much, much more than that.

Summary: Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.     -
